stories.Headline: CoreWeave falls 6.13% as AI cloud selling deepens and loan talks reportedly reach 4 billion dollars
stories.Summary:
CoreWeave shares fell 6.13 percent to close at 53.13 dollars on Friday, November 13, 2026, due to selling in AI cloud stocks. This specialized neocloud provider for generative AI workloads experienced a price drop that outweighed its strong revenue growth during the trading day. Trading volume reached 77.6 million shares, which was about 72 percent above the three month average of 45.1 million shares. The stock decline extended losses from the previous day following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on November 12, 2026. Investors are now watching the company for future guidance and financing needs after the market closed at 4:00 PM ET.

The company is reportedly pursuing at least 4 billion dollars in loans to expand its AI infrastructure while holding over 40 billion dollars in debt. CoreWeave, which IPOed in 2025, has grown 33 percent since going public and currently has a market cap of 31.22 billion dollars. Its third quarter results showed revenue rose 168 percent to 3.7 billion dollars, with 2026 guidance raised to between 13.0 and 13.3 billion dollars. The stock range for the day was 49.24 to 56.36 dollars, while the 52 week range was 40.58 to 138.25 dollars. The company maintains a gross margin of 27.35 percent as it manages its significant leverage and buildout risks.

Robert Izquierdo reported that Nvidia was a major financial backer, shareholder, and strategic partner to the neocloud provider before the CEO resigned. He stated that the departure of Jensen Huang created uncertainty regarding how the relationship between the chip giant and CoreWeave might change. Izquierdo noted that adding more debt during a period of rising interest rates raised justifiable concerns among investors on Wall Street. He explained that while the revenue update initially impressed the market, shares later reversed due to the high debt burden. The analyst highlighted that leverage and buildout risk remain central to the current investor debate regarding the company.

Other AI cloud peers faced pressure, with Nebius Group closing down 9.92 percent at 115.88 dollars and IREN falling 6.72 percent to 18.17 dollars. These declines reflected broader capital spending concerns and turmoil related to Nvidia, which affected various data center services and infrastructure providers. The S&P 500 fell 0.40 percent to 7,562, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 0.91 percent to reach 25,136 on November 13. Investors in the Nasdaq 100 previously wiped out approximately 2.5 trillion dollars in market value during a sharp retreat in early November. Lenders and credit investors are now reassessing their exposure to companies that are financing the expansion of AI data centers.

The AI boom relies on heavy spending today on chips and infrastructure to capture economic returns from technology that reshapes industries tomorrow. J.P. Morgan Global Research estimates that global AI capital expenditure could reach approximately 900 billion dollars during the year 2026. The five major US hyperscalers may spend as much in 2026 as they have cumulatively since ChatGPT launched in November 2022. The International Monetary Fund identified an AI driven market correction as a potential risk to global financial stability in October 2026. This investment cycle increasingly involves debt, equity issuance, and complicated financing arrangements rather than just cash from established technology companies.

Nvidia is scheduled to report its third quarter fiscal 2027 results on November 17 to measure if AI computing demand remains strong. Markets will watch these results to see if the industry's enormous investment cycle can be supported by continued demand for chips. The articles leave open whether the current sell off is a temporary correction or a warning about the economics of AI. There is ongoing uncertainty about the pace of future investment and the possibility of greater scrutiny for data center projects. It remains unclear if AI adoption can turn into durable profits quickly enough to justify the extraordinary infrastructure costs.

stories.Headline: Tomorrow Together launches a $1.1 million effort to shape the Democratic AI agenda before 2028
stories.Summary:
A Democratic political organization called Tomorrow Together launched a new effort to shape the artificial intelligence agenda before the 2028 presidential campaign. This initiative was announced on November 12, 2026, during a two day event called the What's Next conference held in Denver. The group wants to change how the party talks with voters about the powerful technology to create a contrast with Donald Trump. This push follows sweeping Democratic wins in midterm races and aims to chart a course for the next major national election cycle. The organization is deepening its investment in this issue because party leaders believe it is a critical way to win more votes.

The new research initiative requires an initial investment of 1.1 million dollars to start the effort to shape the party's AI agenda. Tomorrow Together previously spent 6.5 million dollars on behalf of candidates who called for more regulation of data centers and artificial intelligence. The group is reacting to warnings that AI poses risks to humans as companies develop versions that can build new versions themselves. This effort takes place in Denver, where Rep.-elect Bob Brooks and Rep.-elect Paige Cognetti of Pennsylvania attended the conference on November 12, 2026. Other attendees included Senator-elect Josh Turek of Iowa, Rep.-elect Jamie Ager of North Carolina, and a moderator named Alex Edelman.

Chief program officer Maddie Kriger said that getting this issue right will be critical for winning the votes of the American people. She stated that the group wants to be prepared to take action if more and worse AI incidents occur in the next year. Co-founder Rob Flaherty argued that Democrats now have the lead on this issue because voters want to see technology being regulated. Co-founder Karthik Ganapathy agreed with this assessment, stating that he would rather be on the Democratic side than the Republican side. Data analyst David Shor told the crowd that they are watching the birth of a new political issue before their eyes.

Voters of both political parties embrace regulation, which creates an opportunity for Democrats to become the party that pushes for AI guardrails. President Donald Trump has embraced a position that Democrats believe is wildly unpopular because he opposes the regulation of this powerful technology. Some Republicans have distanced themselves from this pro industry stance, most notably Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, who may run for the presidency. The effort is designed to counter the huge campaign war chest of the industry that Tomorrow Together fought during the midterm elections. This political shift affects how candidates will communicate with the public regarding the risks and the development of artificial intelligence.

Tomorrow Together previously acted as one of several groups that tried to counter the industry's financial influence during the recent midterm elections. The group pushed for new limits on data centers and artificial intelligence to protect the public from potential risks of the technology. The current political climate is shaped by the recent midterm wins and the upcoming 2028 presidential campaign for the Democratic party. The organization believes that the public is now more likely to trust Democrats over Republicans on the issue of technology regulation. This background sets the stage for the party to use AI as a primary wedge issue against the current Republican platform.

The group will now use its research initiative to develop specific messaging and policy goals to present to voters before the 2028 election. They intend to move quickly to help people and take action if new AI incidents happen within the coming calendar year. The organization will continue to monitor the positions of Republicans like Ron DeSantis to see if the party splits on regulation. The articles leave open exactly what specific guardrails the group will propose for the development of new artificial intelligence versions. It remains unclear how the industry will respond to this increased political pressure for regulation from the Democratic party and its allies.

stories.Headline: DEEPX completes DX-M2 design for Samsung 2nm process and targets Q4 2027 mass production
stories.Summary:
The fabless semiconductor company DEEPX announced on November 10, 2026, that it finished the design for its next-generation artificial intelligence chip called the DX-M2. The company completed the mask tape-out for prototype production in early November, which transferred the finalized design data to the foundry. This milestone allows the company to begin photomask production for the chip. DEEPX expects to receive its first silicon chips in March 2027 and provide evaluation samples to customers during the second quarter of that year. Initial mass-production shipments are scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2027, with full-scale global supply expansion planned for 2028.

The project requires an investment of more than $100 million to cover production engineering and performance verification expenses. The DX-M2 will be manufactured using the second-generation 2-nanometer foundry process from Samsung Electronics, which is known as SF2P. This chip is designed to run vision-language models and large language models at a power consumption of approximately 5 watts. DEEPX is targeting industrial systems, robotics, and AI-enabled personal computers for this specific hardware. The DX-M2 also earned a CES 2027 Innovation Award in the AI category from the Consumer Technology Association.

DEEPX stated that this investment represents a significant bet on running AI models directly on devices instead of using remote data centers. The company explained that this on-device approach can reduce costs, energy use, and the delays caused by sending data to the cloud. They noted that their semiconductors are intended for applications outside of data centers, which currently face backlash for consuming massive amounts of water and power. This follows the August 2025 mass production of the DX-M1 chip, which used a 5-nanometer process from Samsung.

As of October 2026, DEEPX had secured 88 purchase orders worth about $13.3 million across 10 different countries. The company forecasts revenue of $40 million for 2026, which is more than double the $17 million target it announced last year. This growth follows a 2025 fiscal year where the company recorded annual revenue of 3.3 billion won and an operating loss of 20.1 billion won. The company will now move toward customer evaluations and mass manufacturing throughout 2027 and 2028.

stories.Headline: Intel forms 23-company Korean AI alliance and pitches HBM-free inference GPU
stories.Summary:
Intel formed a twenty three company Korean AI alliance on November 11, 2026, during the Intel AI Summit Seoul. The company launched this coalition to build AI infrastructure tailored for the South Korean market using domestically manufactured servers. Intel is also pitching a new inference GPU that replaces expensive high bandwidth memory with low power DRAM. This strategic move aims to target the sovereign AI and physical AI markets through a broad hardware and software partnership. The alliance was officially announced by Tae Won Bae, who serves as the president of Intel Korea.

The K AI Full Stack Alliance includes twenty three companies such as KTNF, Dnotitia, Panmnesia, Upstage, Nota AI, DEEPX, FuriosaAI, and Exina. This coalition focuses on an open infrastructure and ecosystem built around servers made in Korea and powered by Intel chips. Intel will also sign a memorandum of understanding with Seoul AI Hub to support the growth of domestic AI startups. The company unveiled the Crescent Island GPU, which uses LPDDR5X memory to support a capacity of up to 480 gigabytes. This GPU consumes 350 watts of power and is scheduled for a commercial launch during the next calendar year.

Tae Won Bae stated that the alliance represents a commitment to creating innovation together with Korean companies on an open infrastructure. Santosh Viswanathan, the Asia Pacific regional head, identified sovereign AI, personalized AI, and edge AI as key emerging opportunities. Dan Rodriguez emphasized the need for collaboration among hardware and software partners to deliver AI innovation in real world settings. Anil Nanduri explained that AI inference will become a matter of scaling, requiring GPUs that can be easily expanded. Marcus Lawrence noted that Intel provides design and foundry services from the conceptual stage to the actual product.

The alliance affects domestic AI companies and startups by providing tools to enhance their development capabilities and technical collaboration. Intel demonstrated that its GPU D Series provides 30 percent lower latency on Gemma models than the Nvidia RTX 6000 Pro. The D270 model showed 5.9 times higher computing performance in financial simulations and 2.2 times higher AI agent performance. These figures are intended to attract Korean fabless companies that are currently investing heavily in neural processing units and infrastructure. The partnership aims to help these local firms respond quickly and flexibly to the rapidly evolving global AI market.

Intel is mass producing Clearwater Forest, a Xeon server processor that features up to 288 high density, energy efficient E cores. The company plans to launch Diamond Rapids next year, which will feature up to 256 high performance P cores. Intel also introduced the Core Ultra Series 3, a system on chip integrating multiple processing units for edge customers. The Crescent Island GPU was developed to enable high capacity, low power AI computing without using costly high bandwidth memory. These products are part of a broader strategy to challenge the market dominance currently held by the company Nvidia.

Intel will continue working with local partners and the government to support the development of the broader Korean AI ecosystem. The company intends to offer turnkey capabilities ranging from chip design to production for clients with their own designs. Future efforts will focus on integrating processors of different architectures using advanced packaging to create more efficient AI hardware. The articles leave open the specific terms of the memorandum of understanding with the Seoul AI Hub for startups. They also do not specify the exact date for the release of the Diamond Rapids processor in 2027.

stories.Headline: Nebius lowers 2026 revenue guidance and raises capital spending forecast as shares fall 20%
stories.Summary:
Nebius Group N.V. shares plunged 20% in premarket trading on Thursday, November 12, 2026, after the artificial intelligence infrastructure company announced higher capital spending plans and a delay in expected revenue. The company said some revenue originally anticipated in 2026 would move into early 2027. As a result, Nebius lowered its full-year revenue outlook to the bottom of its previously projected range. The announcement raised concerns about the timing of returns from the company's investments in AI infrastructure. Nebius operates in a capital-intensive market where expanding computing capacity requires substantial spending on equipment and data centers.

Nebius lowered its 2026 revenue guidance to $3 billion to $3.2 billion, trimming the upper end from its previous $3.4 billion forecast. The revised outlook followed delays in bringing some third-party data center capacity online, now expected in the first half of 2027. Nebius raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to approximately $27 billion, from $20 billion to $25 billion previously, with spending projected to reach $40 billion to $45 billion in 2027. The company is targeting $12 billion to $13 billion in 2027 revenue, close to Wall Street's $12.28 billion forecast. Nebius expects advance payments and funding linked to contracts with investment-grade customers to cover 75% to 85% of its 2027 investment budget.

Nebius reported third-quarter revenue of $980.8 million, up 571% year over year and above analyst estimates of approximately $907.5 million. The company posted a GAAP loss of 13 cents per share. Despite the near-term setbacks, Nebius expects 2027 revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion and targets pre-tax break-even by year-end. Management also indicated that customers are already seeking computing capacity for 2028. The company faces competition from other AI infrastructure providers, including CoreWeave, as demand for computing resources continues to grow.

The Nebius sell-off followed fresh turbulence across U.S. AI infrastructure stocks after NVIDIA Corp.'s CEO Jensen Huang's sudden resignation on Thursday. CoreWeave fell sharply, while Nebius lost nearly 20%, and IREN Ltd. also faced pressure. Nvidia's strategic and financial relationship with the neocloud ecosystem has made its leadership transition a source of concern for investors assessing the sustainability of AI infrastructure investments. The Tradr 2X Short NBIS Daily ETF emerged as Thursday's top-performing fund, surging approximately 39% as Nebius shares plunged nearly 20%. NBIZ seeks to deliver twice the inverse of NBIS's daily performance, making it a leveraged vehicle for traders betting against the stock.

For investors, the main concern is whether higher spending will translate into revenue quickly enough to support the company's expansion plans. The 20% premarket decline suggests investors are reassessing those expectations following the revised outlook. The difference from a straightforward 40% gain can arise from actual daily performance and fund expenses. NBIZ targets twice the inverse of Nebius's daily return, not its cumulative long-term performance. Daily rebalancing and compounding can cause returns to diverge significantly over multiple sessions.

The next catalyst will be Nebius' updated financial guidance and progress in converting its infrastructure investments into revenue during early 2027. For ETF investors, NBIZ's rally highlights how leveraged single-stock funds can capitalize on earnings-driven volatility, even as the underlying company's longer-term AI growth opportunity remains intact. The articles leave open how the leadership transition at Nvidia will affect the neocloud ecosystem going forward. The articles also leave open whether Nebius can convert its infrastructure investments into revenue quickly enough to support its expansion plans. The articles do not state what specific third-party data center capacity was delayed or which customers are seeking capacity for 2028.

stories.Headline: LangChain raises $300 million led by CapitalG at a $3 billion valuation
stories.Summary:
LangChain, an AI agent management startup, raised $300 million in a Series C funding round led by CapitalG, the company announced on Friday, according to TechGig. The Wall Street Journal reported on November 12, 2026, that Alphabet Inc.'s CapitalG fund led the round, SiliconANGLE wrote. The round included participation from Singapore's GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP and Sapphire Ventures, TechGig reported. The investment values San Francisco-based LangChain at $3 billion, more than double its $1.25 billion valuation from a year ago, TechGig said. LangChain began in 2022 as an open-source project addressing tasks difficult for early large language models, such as web searching and API calls, according to TechGig.

The new valuation more than doubles the company's worth in approximately one year, TechGig reported, after it raised $125 million at the earlier $1.25 billion valuation. LangChain reports 7,000 LangSmith customers, including startups Harvey, Rippling and Clay and enterprises Nvidia, Toyota and Salesforce, according to TechGig. After its previous funding round last year, LangChain disclosed its open-source tools were being downloaded about 90 million times per month, SiliconANGLE reported. Its LangSmith suite is used by Autodesk Inc., Cisco Systems Inc. and a long list of other tech firms, SiliconANGLE wrote. LangChain reportedly plans to nearly double its headcount to 850 employees by the end of 2027, hiring infrastructure experts, AI engineers, salespeople and marketers, according to SiliconANGLE.

CapitalG led the Series C round, and it was joined by IVP, Sapphire Ventures, GIC and DFJ Growth, SiliconANGLE reported. TechGig described CapitalG as the lead investor and listed GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP and Sapphire Ventures among the participants. The articles attribute no direct statements to CapitalG or LangChain executives beyond the funding announcement itself. TechGig reported that the company announced the round on Friday, while SiliconANGLE cited The Wall Street Journal's report on the funding. SiliconANGLE reported that LangChain is best known for the eponymous open-source framework it released in 2022.

LangChain's software, LangSmith, is designed to be model, cloud and ecosystem agnostic, allowing businesses to maintain ownership of their intelligence, according to TechGig. SiliconANGLE described LangSmith as a suite of paid products developers can use to build agents and maintain them once in production. LangGraph, LangChain's second open-source tool, links multiple LangChain-powered agents into a single automation workflow and can require humans to approve sensitive actions, SiliconANGLE reported. Deep Agents, the third component, adds a virtual file system, a work planning tool and a subagent generation feature, according to SiliconANGLE. LangSmith saves agent iterations in a centralized repository, restores earlier bug-free versions and compares output quality across versions, SiliconANGLE wrote.

LangChain later shifted its focus to managing AI agents, TechGig reported, after starting in 2022 as an open-source project. The LangChain framework reduces the work of building AI agents, making it simple to connect an agent to a large language model, integrate tools and add a system prompt, SiliconANGLE reported. The framework also lets developers customize details such as the format of prompt responses, according to SiliconANGLE. LangSmith generates traces, logs describing every step of a workflow through an agent processing a prompt, and analyzes them to find, prioritize and fix technical issues, SiliconANGLE wrote. SiliconANGLE reported that an AI agent usually goes through multiple iterations before release to users.

LangChain reportedly plans to nearly double its headcount to 850 employees by the end of 2027, according to SiliconANGLE. The company will hire infrastructure experts, AI engineers, salespeople and marketers, SiliconANGLE reported. The articles do not state how the $300 million in proceeds will be allocated beyond hiring plans. The articles give no date for when the round closed beyond the Friday announcement and the November 12 report. The articles do not say whether further funding rounds or a public listing are planned.

stories.Headline: Google blocks K-12 search unless districts opt into AI
stories.Summary:
Google announced this week that starting in January it plans to block K-12 students from using its search engine unless districts opt into the company’s AI-generated version of it. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president and general manager of education, said on Monday during a virtual briefing that a school uncomfortable with that and wanting AI off can choose not to have Search at all. The announcement came as districts across California debate restrictions on artificial intelligence and technology use in the classroom. Los Angeles Unified, the state’s largest district, has already placed restrictions on generative AI. The story was written by Vani Sanganeria and Mallika Seshadri and originally published by EdSource.

Google will block both its integrated AI tool and Google search for K-12 students unless a district turns either feature on, with no option for a search engine without AI integration. The company said in a blog post on Tuesday that it will update its search function for schools by making its “Guided Learning” AI product the default. Google said the product will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork. Google clarified in a post on X on Tuesday that schools can turn off Gemini and Gemini Notebook and use search, but AI Mode and AI Overview will remain integrated into Google search. Google said Tuesday that education leaders need to either accept some AI in classrooms or lose access to its search engine, and that early next year Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search will automatically be turned off for school districts, which must opt in.

Phillips said a school not comfortable with that and simply wanting AI off has the choice to not have Search on at all. Google said in its X post that it knows there is concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork and that schools have told the company they want control. Google said that is exactly why it is making these changes to address feedback from educators in recent months. Google said it will continue to engage deeply with educators to ensure it is giving schools more choice, more controls, and improved Search for learning. Google did not respond to The Hill’s request for comment.

Lila Byock, founder of parent advocacy group Schools Beyond Screens, described Google’s decision as an act of “bullying” and said educational value, not shareholder value, must determine the technology used by students. Byock said Google forced its AI products into classrooms, parents fought back, and now Google is refusing to take no for an answer. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into public schools and that no corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children. Clay Lavercombe, freshman principal at Springboro High School in Ohio, said changing anything in the middle of a school year, big or small, is a challenge. An estimated 60,000 K-12 schools use Google Workplace, and around 93 percent of U.S. public schools either use or plan on using Google Chromebooks in classrooms.

About three-quarters of American teens and tweens use or interact with the AI summaries in search results, according to a recent report by Common Sense Media. In a series of 180 tests, Common Sense Media researchers found that Google’s AI Mode completed students’ homework assignments for them every time. The AI feature also invented fake answers to questions, returned different answers to the same questions and cited unreliable sources such as Reddit, Facebook and YouTube. Yvette Renteria, chief program officer at Common Sense Media, said Google search helps with media literacy, understanding, evaluating and analyzing resources, which are crucial to learning. Common Sense Media researchers have not reviewed Google’s Guided Learning mode.

Rory Mir, director of community tech engagement at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, said the tricky thing with schools is that they enter into long contracts, and the switch comes with real monetary costs as well as labor costs and disruption. Renteria said districts with more robust technology departments are more likely to find work-arounds to Google search, but that is not the case across the board. L.A. Unified uses a statewide purchasing arrangement for Google Workspace for Education, which includes Google Docs and Slides, and it also has a new Generative AI Ad Hoc Committee. A district spokesperson told EdSource that the district is reviewing Google’s announcement and its potential implications for schools, educators and students. Some parents of Long Beach Unified students, part of a new tech policy group that also includes teachers, students, administrators and industry experts, will have an opportunity to provide input into the district’s options, a district spokesperson said.

Many school districts will have to decide to opt into Google’s AI-integrated search or find a new search alternative in the middle of the school year. Byock said districts should reclaim their authority from corporate interests and divest from Google. Mir said Google’s new policy should invoke among schools a big discussion about Google’s role as a monopolist with undue power over schools’ decisions. Mir said he is hoping folks funnel this outrage into reevaluating these contracts with Google and demanding a higher bar for students. Eric Gibbs, vice president of education at AI detection company Copyleaks, said Google risks undermining its own position by forcing schools and districts to choose between access to information they already have and control over how students use AI.

stories.Headline: Connecticut passes a law requiring AI chatbots to remind minors they are AI every hour
stories.Summary:
A letter to the editor published by HK Now on November 13, 2026, and received November 12, 2026, called for guardrails around artificial intelligence, and it was written by Joanne Nesti. The letter said artificial intelligence has been the biggest technological advance in our lives over the past several years, for better and worse. It said as many as two-thirds of all teens in the United States use AI chatbots. It said bad advice, questionable motives and a drive to keep users engaged have caused tragedies already. It said we need to protect our children from the worst outcomes.

As of January 1, 2027, Connecticut will have a new control in place to better monitor the use of AI, the letter said. That date falls just days after Connecticut youth will likely receive new phones, tablets and laptops for the holidays, the letter said. A new law passed earlier this year will cover several AI issues, and one particular piece will directly impact families, the letter said. Under the new law, chatbots will have additional controls to prevent them from developing close relationships with humans, the letter said. A bot will need to remind a user it is AI every three hours for adults and every hour for children, the letter said.

Before a minor starts using an AI chatbot, as of January 1, 2027, operators will need to prevent it from engaging in harmful conduct, the letter said. The letter said some news stories have described AI companions and chatbots encouraging members of the public to consume unsafe substances, encourage unsafe behavior like disordered eating, or even commit violence. As of January 1, 2027, AI systems will need to be updated to prevent this, the letter said. Another change requires AI chatbots to pick up on thoughts of suicide or self-harm and direct a user to help, such as suicide and crisis lifeline numbers, the letter said. Any violations of the law will be enforced by the Attorney General's office, the letter said.

The letter's author said he voted for this legislation earlier in 2026 and is proud to have done so. He said the law isn't meant to prevent AI or technology companies from operating their products, but it meets the disturbing and tragic stories heard in recent years and tries to prevent them from happening again. He said that as a grandfather he is concerned about his own grandkids' safety, and that as the owner of a manufacturing company he has seen how quickly technology can evolve. He said we need to make sure there are common-sense protections in place for at-risk children. He said the changes aren't going to put OpenAI or Anthropic out of business and aren't going to impact the free market.

The letter said Connecticut is the seventh state to regulate AI companions, so the state is not going out on a limb by itself. It said the state needs to stay safe and protect its youth from threats, and that putting guardrails on AI will help. A separate letter in The Globe and Mail on November 15, 2026, said a large proportion of the projected massive investment in computing power for artificial intelligence will be used for utterly trivial purposes. That letter said AI should be treated like the mainframe computing of 60 years ago, only accessible to those with a serious need for it. It listed gaming, AI-generated cat videos and pornography, trivia questions, fake job applications and academic fraud, not to mention crime, as such purposes. It said the next time someone wants to erect an energy- and water-hogging data centre in your neighbourhood, consider how much of its power and carbon footprint will be used for such purposes.

The Globe letter described a hockey playoff pool started in 1979, in which one team this past April picked JJ Peterka "on Buffalo." It said the nine-time champion asked whether the team had used AI to make the pick, and they sheepishly admitted it. It said Mr. Peterka, who played on Buffalo the prior season, got zero points in the playoffs and that team lost the pool by 10 points. It said the next best player, whom they would have picked on Buffalo had they not used artificial intelligence, got 10 points, and they would have tied for first place. The Globe letter also said its writer's fantasy football team was picked by artificial intelligence and received a C from the AI, and the writer is in last place in his division.

stories.Headline: Sundar Pichai unveils eight AI and hardware releases over five days including Gemini 4 models and smart glasses
stories.Summary:
Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced eight major AI and hardware releases over five days from Monday to Thursday in November 2026. These updates included two new TPU systems, two Gemini 4 models, three DeepMind projects, a developer API, and smart glasses. The blitz targeted AI researchers, businesses, and developers with enhanced capabilities for complex coding, cyber defence, and rapid execution. Gemini 4 Hydrogen launched on Thursday, while Gemini 4 Carbon became available on Tuesday for paying developers and AI Ultra subscribers. Pre-orders for Android XR audio glasses also began on Thursday, with shipments expected to arrive during the holiday season.

The TPU 8tx system handles encrypted data for governments, while the TPU 8i Max combines two chips for AI agents. Gemini 4 Carbon costs two dollars per million input tokens and ten dollars per million output tokens for complex tasks. The Gemini Decisions API costs ten cents per million input tokens and provides yes or no responses via an AI Studio endpoint. Gemini 4 Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times quicker than Gemini 3.8 Flash and offers four reasoning depths for diverse agentic workflows. Samsung and Google developed thirty Intelligent Eyewear models, including sixteen Gentle Monster and fourteen Warby Parker designs, for a December 10 launch.

Sundar Pichai detailed the product releases, while Koray Kavukcuoglu, senior vice president at Google DeepMind, described the new Hydrogen model's speed. Kavukcuoglu stated that Hydrogen is built for rapid execution of everyday work, such as writing code and running various tests. He noted that Hydrogen is better at following guidance and calling tools to get reliable outputs with less back and forth. The company claimed that Hydrogen is two times less likely to circumvent permission boundaries than the previous Gemini 3.8 Flash model. DeepMind reported that Gemini Robotics 2.5 improves tool handling, resulting in job completion rates that are 20 to 30 per cent quicker.

The new smart glasses affect users in South Korea and the United States, where they support translation and meeting summaries. These glasses, weighing 41 grams, feature a 12 megapixel HDR camera, two open ear speakers, and four microphones for the wearer. Users can photograph whiteboards to save summaries to Samsung Notes, while the battery provides nine hours of use on one charge. Academics can access the AlphaGenome 2 API for free, though companies must join a private preview for this science release. The AlphaProof Code project verified Signal's one to one messaging encryption code in four weeks and found no new flaws.

Google previously launched Gemini 4 Argon two weeks before Carbon, and Gemini 3.8 Flash was released in September to power Search features. The Intelligent Eyewear was showcased at Google I/O in May and Galaxy Unpacked in July before the full lineup was revealed. These glasses use the Qualcomm Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 platform and offload some processing tasks to a connected Galaxy smartphone. AlphaGenome 2 investigates how DNA changes affect cell types to help trace disease origins, but it is not for diagnosis. The eighth generation chip family now expands to four systems with the addition of the 8tx and 8i Max.

The Intelligent Eyewear will launch in the United States and South Korea on December 10, though only Gentle Monster models hit Korea. Google continues to work on safety and security for Hydrogen, specifically focusing on jailbreak resistance to improve the model's overall reliability. The articles leave open whether the AlphaGenome 2 private preview will expand or if other countries will receive the glasses. It remains unclear if the Gemini Decisions API will add written output or if the free tier has specific usage limits. The text does not state if other hardware partners beyond Samsung, Warby Parker, and Gentle Monster will join the project.

stories.Headline: BIM Tiruchirappalli and UT Arlington launch joint AI in business master's for working professionals
stories.Summary:
Bharathidasan Institute of Management, a business school based in Tiruchirappalli, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with The University of Texas at Arlington. The agreement covers a joint Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence for Business, known by the abbreviation MSAIB. The signing was reported by The Hindu BusinessLine on November 13, 2026, and a photograph shows officials from both institutions at the ceremony. The programme is aimed at working professionals and will integrate AI machine learning, data engineering and generative AI into business strategy. It will be hosted at IIT Madras Research Park rather than at either partner's own campus.

The programme will begin with an initial trial cohort of 25 students, and faculty from the University of Texas at Arlington will facilitate it. It carries an indicative tuition fee of US$27,000, set as an alternative to the substantially higher overall cost of two years of full-time residential study in the United States. The hybrid learning model uses eight-week courses, with seven weeks of online instruction followed by one week of in-person learning. Students will be taught by the American university's faculty throughout the programme. They will also take part in a one-week immersion in the United States, which includes company visits, interactions with business executives and exposure to industry applications of artificial intelligence.

Ravi Appasamy, Chairman of the Board of Governors at BIM Tiruchirappalli, described the partnership as a deliberate step in building a globally recognised institution. He said the Board is firmly committed to positioning BIM as globally connected, academically distinguished and industry-relevant. He added that BIM is entering a new phase of its transformational journey, and that the institute is not simply building for the next decade. In his words, it is laying the foundations for the next generation of management education. Asit K. Barma, Director of BIM Tiruchirappalli, was also at the signing, as was Fernando Jaramillo, Associate Dean of Academic Affairs at the Texas university.

Radha K. Mahapatra, Chair and Professor of Information Systems and Operations Management at the University of Texas at Arlington, spoke about how students will be admitted. He said enrolments will be conducted through the university's own specialised framework. Although the programme is designed for working professionals, he said the university is also open to selecting capable students who have just completed their undergraduate studies. Separately, Anurag Behar, CEO of the Azim Premji Foundation, wrote in Mint on November 11, 2026 that India's higher education is in worse shape than its school education. He argued that artificial intelligence could be the death blow to the country's higher education institutions if the existing mess is perpetuated.

The partnership comes at a time when international student mobility has been disrupted by visa policies, rising education and living costs, and geopolitical developments. The Institute of International Education's Open Doors 2025 report said new international student enrolments in the US fell by 7 per cent. Australia saw international student commencements drop by 12 per cent compared with the corresponding period. The UK reported a 16 per cent year-over-year decline in sponsored study visa grants to Indian nationals. Meanwhile, several global universities have set up in India, including the University of Liverpool in Bengaluru, the University of Bristol in Mumbai and the University of Western Australia in Mumbai and Chennai.

Behar's article offers its own account of the problems facing Indian higher education. He argues that many college classrooms sit empty because neither students nor teachers show up, and that research is conflated with teaching. He says public funding has been squeezed while enrolment ambitions have grown, and that his estimate is only 10 to 15 per cent of institutions are serious about their work. He pictures a loop in which a machine prepares the lesson, another writes the student's answer and a third marks it, so that no human mind learns anything. He calls for AI to be mostly banished from education and for a good higher education system to be built on new foundations.

The articles say the programme will start with a trial cohort of 25 students, but they give no start date for classes or for the first intake. They do not say how many students might be admitted after the trial cohort, or how the programme will be assessed. The articles do not say whether the Master's degree will be awarded by the University of Texas at Arlington, by BIM or jointly by both. They also leave open when applications will open and what admission criteria the university's own framework will use. The sources do not explain how the indicative tuition fee of US$27,000 might change, or whether any part of the cost will be covered by the partners.

stories.Headline: NTT DATA becomes AI consulting partner of the ATP Finals in Turin
stories.Summary:
NTT DATA became a Gold Partner of the Nitto ATP Finals, taking the roles of Official AI Consulting Partner and Official Technology Consulting Partner, Telecompaper reported on 13 November 2026. The tournament will be held in Turin, Italy, from 15 to 22 November 2026. NTT DATA announced the partnership in Tokyo on 12 November 2026, according to its own release. IT Brief UK reported the news on 12 November 2026. The partnership gives NTT DATA a presence at the 2026 tournament in Turin.

The tournament takes place at the Inalpi Arena in Turin, Italy, from 15 to 22 November 2026. NTT DATA plans to present technology demonstrations linked to sport and human performance at the arena. The company will host a Tech Corner featuring computer vision, physical AI and AI infrastructure in settings including monitoring, safety, construction and humanoid robotics. The Tech Corner will also house the Mental Economy Gym, developed with Formula Medicine, an Italian specialist in sports medicine and human performance. At the Fan Village court, an on-court experience presented by FITP will combine cognitive and physical monitoring with AI-based computer vision.

Kazuhiko Nakayama, President and CEO of NTT DATA Group, said what makes sport extraordinary is ultimately human, citing the ambition to push boundaries, the courage to take risks and the determination to achieve more. He said technology can unlock greater possibilities by helping people see what was previously invisible and discover new ways to improve. He said that as an AI Consulting Partner of the Nitto ATP Finals, NTT DATA wants to celebrate human potential while demonstrating how technology can expand what people can achieve. He said NTT DATA combines AI capabilities with deep industry expertise to help clients transform their businesses and create new value. NTT DATA described the partnership as the latest in a series of sporting partnerships that bring its global brand positioning statement, "Intelligence to Impact," to life.

NTT DATA said the agreement reflects its belief that intelligence comes not only from AI and technology but also from human expertise and deep industry understanding. The company said it will continue to build on these efforts, using sport as a platform to demonstrate how AI and technology can enhance human potential and create meaningful impact beyond sport. Visitors to the Mental Economy Gym can take on digital challenges that measure indicators such as concentration, reaction and mental workload. NTT DATA is a $30+ billion business and technology services leader serving 75% of the Fortune Global 100, with experts in more than 70 countries. NTT DATA is part of NTT Group, which invests over $3 billion each year in research and development.

The partnership provides a global stage for NTT DATA to showcase how AI, data and technology can support human potential, according to the company. NTT DATA said elite tennis brings together skill, judgment and the ability to adapt under pressure, and it aims to show how technology can provide deeper insights into performance and help people and organizations address challenges beyond sport. The company released a key visual for the Nitto ATP Finals, supported by NTT DATA Group as a Gold Partner. NTT DATA offers clients access to an ecosystem of innovation centers as well as established and start-up partners. The company describes itself as one of the world's leading AI and digital infrastructure providers, with capabilities in enterprise-scale AI, cloud, security, connectivity, data centers and application services.

NTT DATA will use the tournament to show how AI, data and related systems can generate performance insights and support decision-making under pressure. The company said its consulting and industry solutions help organizations and society move confidently and sustainably into the digital future. NTT DATA is a Global Top Employer, according to its release. The articles leave open what the partnership costs and how long it runs. The articles do not say which players will take part in the 2026 tournament.

stories.Headline: Nvidia ships Vera Rubin systems in volume and expects 20% of data center revenue in fiscal Q3 2027
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence chip stocks suffered a brutal sell-off over the past month, as shown by a 20% dip in the PHLX Semiconductor Sector index. Nvidia dropped 26% over the past month and lost its status as the world's largest company in the process. Advanced Micro Devices retreated 15% over the same period. Harsh Chauhan of The Motley Fool wrote the comparison of the two stocks, published on November 12, 2026. The article appeared on AOL and was dated Thursday, November 12, 2026 at 2:29 PM UTC.

Silicon Analysts estimates Nvidia will control 75% of the AI chip market by the end of 2026. Nvidia says its Vera Rubin chip systems consume twice as much power as the previous-generation Blackwell processors but deliver 10x higher performance-per-watt. Nvidia has begun shipping Vera Rubin systems in volume and expects the platform to account for 20% of data center revenue in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. Nvidia has guided for a 70% increase in fiscal 2028 revenue, which ends in January 2028 and coincides with the majority of calendar 2027. Analysts forecast a 71% increase in Nvidia's earnings per share in fiscal 2028, after a projected 95% jump this fiscal year.

Silicon Analysts notes AMD controlled 6% to 8% of the AI chip market last year. AMD's data center revenue surged 97% year over year in Q3 to $8.5 billion, while Nvidia's data center revenue surged 106% to $96.2 billion in the last reported quarter. AMD's Q4 revenue guidance of $17 billion implies a 66% year-over-year jump, higher than the 45% growth reported in Q2. The data center business produced 64% of AMD's revenue last quarter, and AMD expects the segment to account for more than 80% of its top line in 2027. AMD expects total revenue to increase by more than 80% next year, an acceleration over the 50% top-line growth expected in 2026.

AMD's EPS growth is projected to accelerate from 93% this year to 108% in 2027, according to Yahoo! Finance consensus estimates. Nvidia's median 12-month price target of $318 implies a potential jump of 88%, higher than AMD's projected 12-month gains of 26%. Chauhan wrote that Nvidia looks like an ideal investment for investors seeking a chip stock trading at attractive levels. He added that investors won't go wrong with AMD either, as its accelerating growth will help it justify the valuation. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Advanced Micro Devices and Nvidia.

Daniel Sparks wrote a second article, published November 13, 2026 at 3:13AM EST, covering six data software stocks. Snowflake's product revenue climbed 37% year over year to $1.49 billion in fiscal Q2 of 2027, the period ended July 31, 2026, up from 34% in fiscal Q1 and 30% the quarter before. Snowflake lost $192 million on a GAAP basis, down from $298 million the year before, and CFO Brian Robins credited the core platform and a meaningful step-up in AI revenue. Datadog's third-quarter revenue climbed 35% year over year to $1.20 billion after 36% growth in the second quarter, and its largest customer cut usage, with fourth-quarter guidance of $1.19 billion to $1.20 billion about flat with the third quarter. Datadog's net income more than tripled to $118 million.

MongoDB's revenue climbed 30% year over year to $771.8 million in fiscal Q2 of 2027, which also ended July 31, and CEO CJ Desai called it the highest level of growth in several years. MongoDB swung to GAAP net income of $40.9 million from a $47.0 million loss. Cloudflare's third-quarter revenue climbed 39% year over year to $782.5 million, its fastest rate in almost four years, while gross margin fell to 71.2% from 74% and the GAAP net loss widened to $34 million from around $1 million. Elastic's revenue grew 15% year over year to $478 million in fiscal Q1 of 2027, which also ended July 31, slowing from 16% and 18% in the two quarters before. Palantir's third-quarter revenue climbed 96% year over year to $2.31 billion, U.S. commercial revenue grew 148% to $984 million and topped U.S. government revenue for the first time, and net income more than doubled to $1.13 billion.

Sparks wrote that Cloudflare trades at around 170 times expected non-GAAP earnings for its next fiscal year and Snowflake at about 99 times. Elastic is the cheapest at about 22 times earnings, arguably because its growth keeps slowing. Sparks wrote that MongoDB strikes the best balance at about 43 times earnings with 30% growth and a GAAP profit. Palantir costs about $172 per share as of the writing, or about 69 times expected 2027 earnings, and Sparks wrote he would consider buying both MongoDB and Palantir. Sparks wrote he would want to see where Datadog's biggest customer's usage settles before paying about 59 times earnings.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid affair allegations and chip smuggling claims
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the chief executive of Nvidia on November 12, 2026. His departure followed allegations of affairs, including one with Alice Huang. This event caused Nvidia shares to plunge 13 percent in early trading. The company designs graphics processing units that power AI models like Claude and ChatGPT. Huang met leaders like Emmanuel Macron, Keir Starmer, and Mohammed bin Salman in 2025.

Nvidia promised 260,000 advanced chips to South Korea under non-transparent terms. The company acted as a central bank by investing hundreds of billions of dollars. It funded neoclouds to buy chips and gave cash to OpenAI for purchases. Huang built high-trust relationships with TSMC starting with a personal letter in 1997. Alice Huang, an executive at Singaporean firm Megaspeed and alleged Chinese spy, had an affair with Jensen.

This relationship allegedly helped Megaspeed smuggle 7.5 billion dollars of chips into China. Other tech giants like Google, Meta, and Microsoft are now developing their own chips. TSMC manufactures most AI chips using expensive lasers but has a 60 percent yield rate. Nvidia's complex web of circular finance involves various governments and large US tech companies.

The company's valuation relies on its role as the most important player in AI. A new chief executive might bring more transparency to secretive corporate contracts and supply chains. Many questions remain about the order of the years-long queue for obtaining Nvidia chips. It is unclear if the AI economy can survive without its central bank.

stories.Headline: Nanjing University researchers find AI coding agents fail to write valid test cases and overestimate pass rates by 100%
stories.Summary:
Nanjing University’s Professor Liu Jiaheng team proposed the TestPrism benchmark after finding that 14 Coding Agent configurations collectively failed to write valid test cases, and that AI-generated code pass rates were overestimated by 100%, as reported by 36Kr on 12 November 2026. The team evaluated 14 Coding Agent configurations from six model families, including Codex and Claude Code, on test generation. The strongest configuration reached only 28.00% on the Joint Success Function while its single reference evaluation success rate was 59.67%. The research conducted expert annotation on 286 failure traces and summarized 3 categories and 7 test generation error mechanisms. The team also proposed the TestHelix framework, which raised JSF by 11.67 to 12.00 percentage points under the same reasoning budget.

TestPrism contains 300 test tasks and 3000 candidate implementations from 17 sources, with each task carrying a verified panel of correct and wrong implementations. Each panel holds 1 reference implementation, 4 correct alternative implementations and 5 wrong implementations, hidden from the Agent during test generation. The full benchmark contains 2000 tasks, of which 1700 form the training set for TestHelix strategy optimization and 300 form the test set, with no overlap between them. The 300 test tasks cover six languages including Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, C/C++ and Go, come from 67 code repositories and projects, and split into Bug Fix (167), Programs and Algorithms (53), Performance Optimization (28), Feature Expansion (20), Project and Workflow (19) and Refactoring and Migration (13). Two experts with development experience independently reviewed task requirements and verifiers, with Cohen’s κ = 0.68, and tasks still in doubt were excluded.

The core indicator, the Joint Success Function, requires a test to fail on the original code, accept all correct implementations in the panel and reject all wrong implementations in the panel. Reference Acceptance Rate is the proportion of tasks where the test fails on the original code and passes on the reference implementation, the traditional single reference evaluation. Valid Acceptance Rate is the average proportion of the 4 correct alternative implementations accepted, and Invalid Rejection Rate is the average proportion of the 5 wrong implementations rejected. H is the harmonic mean of VAR and IRR, measuring whether the two are balanced. Change Coverage and Entry Coverage follow SWT Bench and TestExplora definitions and measure how much reference modified code and related entry code the test covers.

The paper states that mainstream benchmarks such as TestGenEval, CLOVER, MultiFileTest, SWT Bench and TDD Bench Verified generally follow a Fail-to-Pass criterion, which assumes a test distinguishing before repair and after reference repair is enough to judge any implementation. The authors argue this assumption is hardly valid, because tests may miss key inputs or make weak assertions, or may depend on fixed internal function names, output formats or intermediate states of the reference answer. Works such as OmniCode and SWE Mutation have begun to introduce implementation variants but mainly examine whether tests reject wrong variants, lacking systematic evaluation of accepting correct alternative implementations. The team collected tasks from 17 public benchmarks including the SWE-bench series, Terminal-Bench series, SWE PolyBench, SWE rebench, EvoEval, USACO and AlgoTune, covering repository maintenance, function specification evolution, competitive programming and numerical optimization. Candidate implementations were obtained by different Coding Agents and models actually solving the tasks, and after removing empty commits, duplicate and unapplicable patches, implementations passing all checks were labeled correct and those failing any check wrong.

JioHotstar evaluated six approaches to code retrieval for AI coding agents, comparing filesystem tools, Sourcebot, Graphify, CocoIndex Code, Repowise and an in-house retrieval-augmented generation pipeline, as reported by TechGig on 13 November 2026. Abhishek Bansal, Senior Staff Engineer at JioHotstar, led the comparison using subsets of SWE-bench and CodeScaleBench plus a custom question-answering harness for JioHotstar’s codebase, with Claude Sonnet as the solving model. The study measured task accuracy, token consumption, agent turns and tool usability. The filesystem baseline relying on locally checked out repositories and standard search remained competitive on concrete tasks, while Sourcebot, which provides indexed text search and symbol definitions, performed better than the baseline on harder SWE-bench Verified tasks and cost less. On simpler SWE-bench Lite tasks, retrieval generally added overhead without consistently improving results, and CodeScaleBench showed semantic retrieval helped more when agents interpreted ambiguous problem descriptions.

The JioHotstar report highlighted tool design, noting agents frequently preferred familiar developer operations such as searching text and reading files over higher-level abstractions. Siddharth Vaithinathan raised in a LinkedIn post whether coding agents should understand the code and the company that produced it, suggesting extending agent knowledge beyond code and documentation to architecture, constraints, decisions and incidents. JioHotstar recommends retaining filesystem tools as a baseline, using structural search for concrete code-focused problems and semantic indexing for ambiguous or cross-cutting requirements. The engineering team also emphasizes measuring tool-use traces alongside task accuracy. Hugo Venturini discussed accountability in AI-generated code, noting that humans remain responsible despite AI’s role as a powerful tool, and examined how AI reshapes code review and traditional engineering roles.

The TestPrism paper notes that Coding Agents such as Codex and Claude Code can already browse repositories, modify implementations and continuously refine tests with execution feedback. Testing now serves as the basis for Agent self-verification, evidence for code review and even the reward signal in reinforcement learning, so the quality of generated tests determines whether these downstream links can trust the tests’ judgment. The paper states that there are often multiple correct implementations for the same requirement and many seemingly reasonable but implicitly defective wrong implementations, so a test may recognize the standard answer yet let buggy code pass, or treat implementation details of the standard answer as the requirement itself. The team used three indicators to screen tasks: Solution Size, the number of valid lines of code of the reference implementation; Test Count, the number of test functions or check items; and Test Density, the number of tests per modified file. The screening threshold was calibrated according to each source’s distribution, and representativeness was balanced through source quotas.

The TestPrism paper leaves open how robust generated test evaluation is when implementation methods change, asking whether a reliable test can act like a prism to distinguish implementations under the same requirement. The team requires the correct implementation group to meet an average AST distance standard, and for the wrong implementation group treats different sets of failed check items as diverse, requiring an AST Jaccard distance check when sets are the same. The panel is repeatedly generated and replaced until both groups meet the diversity requirements at the same time. JioHotstar’s findings suggest retrieval approaches should be selected according to task characteristics. The articles do not state what further steps Nanjing University, TestHelix, JioHotstar or Hugo Venturini will take next.

stories.Headline: Nonprofits sue Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI over uncontrolled AI risks
stories.Summary:
A group of experts and nonprofit organizations filed a lawsuit against five major technology companies on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The legal action was submitted to the Superior Court of the State of California for the County of San Francisco. The plaintiffs include the Heat Initiative, the Alliance for Secure AI, the Irreplaceable Education Fund, and Public Citizen. They are suing Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceXSI.

The lawsuit seeks to address the potential for advanced artificial intelligence systems to cause catastrophic risks to humanity. The plaintiffs argue that these systems must be managed before they can cause severe damage to the world. The legal challenge targets the developers of these advanced technologies to prevent future disasters. This action aims to hold the five named tech giants accountable for the safety of their creations.

The nonprofits and experts responsible for the complaint claim that the defendants cannot control the systems they have built. They believe that the current trajectory of AI development poses a fundamental threat to human existence. By taking this case to court, the organizations hope to force a change in how these companies deploy their technology. They assert that the risks are too great to leave to the companies alone.

stories.Headline: How two 23-year-old Indian-American entrepreneurs doubled their fortunes as AI startup hits $20 billion
stories.Summary:
Two Indian-origin entrepreneurs, Adarsh Hiremath and Surya Midha, both 23, doubled their fortunes to an estimated $4.2 billion each after their artificial intelligence startup Mercor secured fresh funding at a $20 billion valuation. The US-based company raised $750 million in a Series D funding round announced on November 10, with investors including Benchmark, General Catalyst, Nvidia and Salesforce. Hiremath and Midha are two of Mercor's three co-founders, alongside chief executive Brendan Foody, and the trio made history last year as the world's youngest self-made billionaires at 22. According to Forbes, each founder owns an estimated 21 per cent stake in Mercor, and their wealth has nearly doubled from about $2.2 billion each in October 2025, when the company was valued at $10 billion after a $350 million round.

Mercor began as a recruitment platform connecting freelance coders in India with US companies before expanding into data labelling and AI training, linking professionals such as doctors and lawyers with AI companies. The latest funding will support the expansion of its evaluation and post-training business, which helps companies test AI models, measure their performance and improve how they handle professional tasks. In a post on X, Foody said Mercor had grown from $1 million to $3 billion in gross annualised revenue in just over two years, and he reported $250 million in gross sales in its latest month. He also said the company had more than doubled its customer base to over 100, while its valuation remains below competitors Scale AI, valued at around $29 billion after Meta's investment in 2025, and Surge AI, estimated by Forbes at approximately $24 billion.

Hiremath and Midha studied at Bellarmine College Preparatory, an all-boys school in San Jose, California, where they became friends through the debate team and became the first team from their school to win all three major national policy debate championships in a single year. They later joined forces with Foody to establish Mercor in 2023, and the founders were also selected for the Thiel Fellowship, which provides young entrepreneurs with $100,000 to pursue business ventures. Midha, whose parents moved to the US from New Delhi, was born in Mountain View and raised in San Jose, while Hiremath studied computer science at Harvard University before leaving after two years to concentrate on the startup. Midha is the youngest of the three by around two months, and Kalshi co-founder Luana Lopes Lara, 30, is recognised as the world's youngest self-made woman billionaire.

stories.Headline: Italy fines Meta 805 million euros for accessing Android photos without consent
stories.Summary:
Italy's data protection agency fined Meta 805 million euros on Saturday, November 14, 2026, for violating privacy laws. The regulator alleged that Meta accessed photos and videos from Android users without their specific consent or proper information. This action targeted the camera roll suggestions feature used when people are browsing the Facebook social media application. The agency claims the company used a single permission for the entire app to access the device photo archives. This fine represents the largest penalty ever issued by the Italian data protection regulator since its inception.

The company must now get separate and specific consent for the feature and explain how it can be disabled. Meta has 60 days to implement these changes and must ensure the feature is disabled by default for all. The regulator found that the 2025 investigation showed a generic warning failed to inform users about the specific suggestions. The authority rejected Meta's objection regarding jurisdiction in favor of the Irish authority because the ePrivacy regulation differs. This specific feature suggests photos and videos from a phone gallery for users to add to their Facebook posts.

The Italian Data Protection Authority is responsible for this ruling and issued the details in a formal statement. They stated that granting full permission allows the app to read the entire photo archive, usually on a permanent basis. The authority noted that users and regulators cannot verify which specific pieces of information the application is actually using. They argued that the current permission system covers multiple features with different needs under one single authorization request. Meta did not immediately respond to requests for comment but maintains the legal right to appeal the decision.

Android users are affected by this case because their private galleries were accessed without clear and specific user consent. The Italian regulator believes the company failed to provide a clear explanation of what the camera roll feature does. Some officials argue that the current permission model is too broad for the sensitive nature of personal photo archives. The authority believes that the lack of transparency prevented users from understanding the scope of the data access. This ruling forces the company to change how it interacts with millions of users across the Italian territory.

The investigation into these privacy violations was launched in 2025 to examine how Meta handles Android device permissions. The regulator focused on the Italian law that implements the European Union's ePrivacy directive regarding electronic communications and privacy. They found that the authorization request was preceded by a generic warning that was insufficient for informed user consent. The agency determined that the one-stop-shop mechanism does not apply to the specific ePrivacy regulation used in this case. This background led to the conclusion that Meta operated outside the legal requirements for data protection in Italy.

Meta must now disable the camera roll suggestions feature by default for all users, including those who previously authorized it. The company has a sixty day window to provide clear explanations and obtain specific consent for the feature's use. The articles leave open whether Meta will choose to appeal the decision or comply with the regulator's demands. It remains unclear if other European regulators will launch similar investigations into the Android permission systems used by Meta. The final outcome depends on whether the company can successfully challenge the jurisdiction of the Italian data authority.

stories.Headline: Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution showcase AI data center battery systems at RE+ 2026
stories.Summary:
Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution will compete at RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas starting November 17. These two companies will showcase energy storage systems and backup power solutions for artificial intelligence data centers. They disclosed their participation plans on November 15 for the three day renewable energy trade show. The event draws about 40,000 visitors and 1,300 companies to the largest renewable energy show in North America. Both firms are targeting North American orders by emphasizing their local production capacity for these battery systems.

LG Energy Solution will use a 279 square meter booth to show the JF3 AC LINK with US-made LFP batteries. This product increases energy density by 26 percent and uses AI and digital twin technologies for grid stabilization. Samsung SDI will exhibit the SBB 2.0 using locally produced LFP prismatic cells in a 20-foot container. Samsung will also show the U8A3 prismatic battery using lithium manganese oxide for uninterruptible power supply applications. LG will display the JP6 Rack for UPS and BBU products based on cylindrical 2170 batteries.

Kang Chang-beom of LG Energy Solution said stable power storage and efficient operations are essential for AI industry growth. He stated the company will become an energy platform by combining battery technology with intelligent operations and North American production. Samsung SDI claims the U8A3 is the first to pass all UL Solutions large-scale indoor fire test criteria. An industry official noted that companies now focus on profitability rather than the cutthroat competition seen in the past. This shift follows a trend where the three major battery firms moved toward making profits this year.

The competition affects Big Tech clients like Amazon, Microsoft, and Google who need cooling and power for AI chips. LG Energy Solution is sitting out a 1,180MW South Korean auction, leaving Samsung SDI and SK On to compete. This auction totals about 7.08GWh in storage capacity, which is larger than the first two rounds combined. Samsung SDI has about 15GWh of production capacity in South Korea with roughly 5GWh of remaining supply. SK On has about 3GWh of LFP capacity converted from an EV line in Seosan for deliveries.

Samsung Electronics previously spent 1.5 billion euros to acquire Germany's Flakt Group for data center climate control technologies. The company is now pursuing US cooling maker Modine to gain North American production facilities and customer networks. Modine recently began mass producing 2 to 3 megawatt chillers at a 63,400 square meter plant in Grand Prairie, Texas. Modine's data center revenue reached 439.7 million dollars in the third quarter, which is up 95 percent from last year. Samsung is also building a 240 billion won production line in Gwangju to start operating in early 2028.

Samsung may acquire Modine for 7.5 billion to 8 billion dollars through a merger agreement or a tender offer. The deal requires approval from two-thirds of voting rights, meaning about 35.41 million votes in favor are needed. LG Electronics is also competing by building a chiller plant in Virginia to begin operating in the first half of 2027. Other competitors like Daikin and Vertiv are expanding through acquisitions to win large projects from North American Big Tech firms. The articles leave open whether Samsung shareholders or Modine's board will ultimately agree to the proposed acquisition.

stories.Headline: Chennai headmasters buy Claude subscriptions and Chicago's Alpha uses 2 Hour Learning to teach students
stories.Summary:
Government model schools in Chennai and a private school in Chicago adopted premium artificial intelligence tools to teach students better in 2026. Headmasters in Chennai spent up to 1 lakh rupees on annual subscriptions for platforms like Claude to improve student learning. In Chicago, Alpha Chicago uses AI powered software called 2 Hour Learning to teach core subjects like math and science. These initiatives aim to modernize education through technology, though they operate in very different public and private school settings. The Chennai pilot program took place at the Centre for Academic Excellence in Saidapet to test these new digital tools.

The Chennai system involves 38 model schools, one per district, which share platforms with other schools in their neighboring districts. Teachers use Claude to generate codes and Gemini for image generation, while developers use GitHub to create a data dashboard. Students at the Chengalpet model school use more than 30 tablets after class hours to take various online assessments. In Chicago, students spend two hours each morning on computers before learning life skills like sewing, cooking, and public transportation. Alpha Chicago currently has 50 students but can hold 500, with tuition costing nearly 55,000 dollars per student.

Senthilvalavan, the headmaster at the Centre for Academic Excellence, said the tools help analyze where students need more academic help. He noted that these tools are useful for entrance exams like JEE, which test problem solving speed and error avoidance. Manikandan, the JEE coordinator for TN Model Schools, explained that the dashboard categorizes test results to show student performance. Senthilvalavan added that this process can widen the pool of students who clear the cut off for these exams. He also mentioned that teachers were trained in data analysis to read trends and provide supporting worksheets to students.

Owen, a student at Alpha Chicago, said the software feels different from using an iPad because he feels he is learning. Carrington Haas, the lead guide at Alpha Chicago, stated that the magic of the school is teaching real world life skills. These life skills include leadership, teamwork, financial literacy, and public speaking, which are taught after the morning AI sessions. The students affected by these changes are those in the 50 Alpha campuses across the country with 1,500 students. In Chennai, the students benefiting are those in the model schools who struggle with specific topics and need re-teaching.

The Alpha Schools model replaces traditional teachers with guides, most of whom do not have a professional background in education. A February analysis by the University of Colorado's National Education Policy Center found only one third of guides have education degrees. In Tamil Nadu, the government model schools provide a specialized environment for students preparing for competitive entrance exams like the JEE. The Chennai schools use a system where data from answer sheets is used to identify specific student weaknesses. These background details show a shift toward data driven instruction and the use of non traditional educators in Chicago.

School education director P Naresh said the department could explore implementing these AI tools across all regular government schools. However, he noted that the volume of students is much larger in regular schools than in the model schools. Naresh believes the department will lean toward training teachers with data to help them tweak their teaching methodology. The articles leave open whether the high cost of Alpha Chicago tuition will limit its growth to wealthy families. They also do not state if the Chennai government will provide funding for subscriptions in all 38 model schools.

stories.Headline: Anthropic files for IPO to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each
stories.Summary:
Anthropic, PBC, an artificial intelligence research and development company based in the United States, recently filed for its proposed initial public offering with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, according to Hydrogen Fuel News. The company aims to sell 825 million Class A shares at a price range of $70 to $78. The filing comes as Anthropic anticipates substantial future commitments, reportedly reaching approximately $900 billion related to computing and infrastructure. The article was published on November 15, 2026.

The expansion initiatives by Anthropic highlight the increasing demand for data centers capable of accommodating advanced AI systems, the article says. These facilities require significant computational power, which leads to mounting pressures on electricity grids and infrastructure. The article states that Anthropic's IPO may have significant implications for AI infrastructure and energy solutions, including the exploration of hydrogen as a potential power source amid growing data center demands. The article does not name any person responsible for the filing or include any statements from Anthropic or its officials.

The article does not provide further context beyond the filing details and the energy implications it raises. It does not say what happens next in the IPO process or when the offering is expected to take place. The full article is behind a paywall, so additional details may exist that are not available here.
