stories.Headline: Allegations against Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang spark debate over US and China AI competition
stories.Summary:
China's Jensen Huang, the Nvidia chief executive, has been at the centre of a controversy over an alleged extra-marital affair and claims that Alice Huang is a Chinese spy. Commentators and social media have turned the saga into widespread entertainment, with memes and influencer gags spreading online. The matter has also prompted questions about its effect on the frontier artificial intelligence race between the United States and China. Analysts see the episode as a potential shift in that contest, one that could influence how the two countries compete in AI development. The coverage gives the story a central place in the wider debate over AI leadership.

Huang has long been seen as a villain by many US hawks because he has argued for relaxing restrictions on the sale of Nvidia chips to China. The latest allegations have added to hawkish views about him, and the scrutiny extends to concerns over alleged corporate espionage. An HT analysis of trade data shows China has rising import dependence on commodities that are likely GPUs or related products. The United States has tried to restrict China's access to cutting-edge chips and GPUs, while China has limited rare earth mineral supplies to the US. The Pax Silica alliance, launched by the US in December 2025, is designed to ease American access to rare earth minerals.

China has denied the allegations of spying and has downplayed the controversy, as expected. The Straits Times writer argues that some pain for Nvidia could help secure the West's AI lead over China in the long run. Commentators disagree on how much China needs Nvidia's chips, and the actual evidence on that question is not clear. The HT analysis notes that the disclosure of Huang's affair is certain to add paranoia in the US AI ecosystem about a Chinese catch-up. The writer's view is that Nvidia's weakening might also spur competition and innovation.

China's trade surplus is expected to exceed a trillion dollars for a second consecutive year in 2026, according to the HT report. China released the open-source reasoning model DeepSeek-R1 in January 2025, bringing it within striking distance of leading frontier AI developers, all based in the US. A Lowy Institute report shows Chinese models are catching up fast with American models, although the US leads China in every AI field except human resources. A Carnegie China report, cited by HT, indicates China is catching up quickly with the US in skilled AI workforce. Huawei announced a new chip-design approach in May 2026 that could limit the effect of US export controls.

The articles leave open whether the constraints on chips and rare earths will matter in the long term, and whether either side will crack its challenge before those constraints become redundant. The Lowy Institute report says Huawei could design chips by 2031 with transistor density equivalent to TSMC's 2028 chips, but whether this succeeds is not yet known. Beijing countered the Pax Silica alliance with the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization earlier in 2026. The articles do not say how the allegations against Huang will ultimately be resolved or how Nvidia's position will change.

stories.Headline: SMIC warns AI computing power and chips may remain in short supply until 2028
stories.Summary:

This financial growth was driven by an intense increase in enterprise demand for domestic artificial intelligence infrastructure across the country. The company's co-CEO, Zhao Haijun, warned that computing power and supporting chips may remain in short supply until the middle or second half of 2028. This shortage persists as the nation struggles to secure the advanced processing power necessary for large scale data center buildouts.

The current situation requires a significant shift toward domestic foundries to mitigate the risks of tighter American chip curbs. Washington has already implemented restrictions on Chinese access to advanced processors, but scrutiny over former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang could intensify these measures. Such a shift would force Chinese firms to rely more heavily on local manufacturers like SMIC to meet their technological needs. The company believes that the relentless demand for AI infrastructure will keep the market strained for at least two more years.

Zhao Haijun expressed his concerns during the company's financial report, stating that the computing crunch would likely last until 2028. He suggested that the reliance on domestic production is becoming a necessity as international trade barriers grow more restrictive. The company is betting that this trend will continue to drive their profits as more enterprises seek local alternatives. These leaders believe that the domestic industry must accelerate its growth to fill the gap left by restricted American technology.

stories.Headline: Big Tech AI Capex Up 66% in Three Years, but Free Cash Flow Plunges 84% — Hyundai Research Institute Warns of 2028 Correction
stories.Summary:
AI capital spending by the five major US Big Tech companies, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle, is projected to rise 65.6% from $789.6 billion this year to $1.3079 trillion in 2029, according to a Hyundai Research Institute report released on the 15th and covered by BigGo Finance on November 14, 2026. Over the past four quarters the same five companies' combined free cash flow fell about 84% to $32.7 billion from $201.1 billion a year earlier, while capex reached 95.5% of operating cash flow in the third quarter. Their corporate bond issuance from January to October totaled $182 billion, roughly double last year's full-year figure of $93.25 billion. About 70% of announced US data center capacity has not yet broken ground, and 38.4% of planned capacity sits in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, three states where tighter regulation has drawn attention since this month's midterm elections.

The report, titled "We Must Prepare for a Possible Correction in the US AI Investment Boom," assessed sustainability across demand and profitability, financial health, financing, regulation, and infrastructure and supply chains. It expects demand and profitability to stay sound through 2027-2028, but sees financial health and regulation deteriorating from neutral to unfavorable and financing slipping from favorable to neutral, with infrastructure and supply chains remaining unfavorable. The US Census Bureau found only 24.6% of American companies were using AI as of last month, and 57% of adopters applied it to three or fewer business functions. The bond yield spread over 10-year Treasuries is 0.65 percentage points for Microsoft but widened from 1.45 to 3.10 percentage points for Oracle between February and this month.

The institute said the diagnosis is not that AI demand has peaked but that the cash capacity and infrastructure needed to sustain the spending are nearing their limits, and it expects a correction around 2028 as delayed profitability, funding burdens and regulatory and infrastructure constraints converge. It said investment is likely to keep expanding through next year given cloud revenue growth and locked-in plans, with companies later postponing or scaling back spending case by case, a process it compared to past general-purpose technologies such as the internet. It warned that a US AI capex decline could hit South Korea's semiconductor exports, production, facility investment and employment in a chain reaction, and that an AI asset price adjustment could spill into Korean financial markets. The institute said Korea must preemptively prepare for economic fluctuations from changes in the US AI investment cycle while strengthening the domestic recovery, and it pointed to export opportunities in power equipment and to connecting AI to productivity gains. Market watchers said how early correction signals around 2028 are detected will shape earnings outlooks, with the timing of actual investment cuts as the watershed.

stories.Headline: Goldman Sachs restricts AI coding tools for staff over security risks

Goldman Sachs has restricted the use of artificial intelligence coding tools inside the bank, citing security risks, according to a report published on November 14, 2026. The firm took the step to limit how employees use AI software that writes or assists with computer code. The restriction applies to coding tools rather than to all AI use at the bank. The report did not specify which tools were affected or how many employees were covered.

The move requires staff to follow new limits on the AI coding software they may use for their work. The bank framed the decision as a response to security concerns tied to such tools. The report gave no further detail on the specific risks the firm identified. It also did not say whether the restriction is temporary or permanent.

Goldman Sachs is responsible for the policy, and the report attributes the decision to the bank itself. The articles do not name any executive who commented on the change. No spokesperson statement or direct explanation from the firm was included. The report did not describe how the bank communicated the rule to its employees.

The context is the growing use of AI coding tools at financial firms, which handle sensitive data and face strict security demands. The report does not say what happens next or whether other banks will follow. It also gives no timeline for reviewing or lifting the restriction. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Acting manpower minister Jasmin Lau urges stronger push on flexible work and deeper AI use in firms
stories.Summary:
Acting Manpower Minister Jasmin Lau gave her first interview to local media since taking the role at the Ministry of Manpower in July's Cabinet reshuffle. In the interview, published on 13 November 2026, she said the ministry must do a lot more to push flexible work arrangements. She suggested shining a light on good employers and workplace culture as one way to do this. She also said her own experience as a working mother has been sometimes a bit painful and a bit of a struggle.

Lau said parents have told her that policies such as childcare leave exist but can be hard to ask for or apply for. The hesitation is not that they are not allowed to take the leave, but that they are committed to their work and find it hard to get colleagues to take over, she said. Guidelines on flexible work arrangements were put in place in 2024 and set out a process for workers to request changes like different locations or timings. An MOM report released in May said 84.5% of employees who needed a flexible work arrangement received one, but the rate at which workers request such arrangements is low.

Lau, who is 43 and a mother of two boys, said policies alone are not enough and that she feels she really needs to do something for working parents. She entered politics at the 2025 general election and is also Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information. She said her portfolio covering workforce transformation and artificial intelligence strategy is extremely hot and very relevant to what people want to understand. She said many firms here use AI in areas like digital marketing but have not used it deeply in business processes such as inventory management, warehousing and just-in-time delivery, which is partly why workers here have not been so affected yet.

She said she is conflicted daily about what deeper AI use would mean for affected workers, which is why firms need to do things like job redesign. The recent retrenchments at GovTech, where she is minister-in-charge, provided learning points, including that a long transition period can weigh on workers every single day. She said retrenchment experiences are highly personal and emotional, and some workers may need time to process the news before seeking career support. She said life is exhausting on all days for her and that the idea of work-life balance that keeps a working mother happy and healthy is very hard to achieve.

Articles.Title: Jasmin Lau on pushing harder on flexible work, ‘hot seat’ portfolio of manpower and AI - The Straits Times

stories.headline_source: Jasmin Lau on pushing harder on flexible work, ‘hot seat’ portfolio of manpower and AI

stories.Headline: Worker.ai acquires Prague voice AI startup DeltaGen and launches an operating system for small businesses
stories.Summary:
Worker.ai announced its acquisition of DeltaGen and launched a company operating system for small businesses on 12 November 2026. The company announcement names John Roberts as CEO and DeltaGen founder Rene Bystron as COO. The announcement brings DeltaGen's conversational AI technology into a platform that assigns work while retaining human approval of business decisions. The date marks the public announcement and product launch, and it does not establish a separate transaction closing date. The acquisition started with a personal connection, because Worker co-founder and CEO John Roberts knew DeltaGen's technology from his previous job at a cybersecurity company.

Worker.ai acquired Prague-based DeltaGen, a startup that builds real-time voice AI, and the financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. All three of DeltaGen's founders are moving to Worker, with René Bystroň joining as co-founder and COO, Michal Studnička working on product, and Matúš Ondreička taking over technical development. DeltaGen's team of around 10 people will stay in Prague, and Worker plans to grow its product and engineering team in the city. DeltaGen previously received investment from Dutch firm Forward Venture Capital and from Techstars, and in November 2025 the startup launched Virtual SE, a tool that gives B2B sales reps answers to technical questions while they are on live calls with clients. Worker's product site positions the platform for owners and leadership teams of small and midsize businesses, and its interface brings together weekly meetings, operating metrics, goals, tasks and issues.

Worker says it can set these up from a customer's spreadsheets or exports, access is requested using a work email, and Worker says it sets up each company itself and admits new companies in small groups. Worker says the service does not join meetings, send in a recording bot or create audio or video recordings, and its privacy policy instead describes processing meeting materials produced by customers' own tools, including transcripts and notes. Section 6.1 of the privacy policy says content on free and self-serve plans is used by default to train and improve Worker's own models, with an account setting that stops this prospectively, and identifiable content on paid plans requires written opt-in for that use. The policy makes separate commitments for connected-account data, because information received through its Google and Microsoft connections is excluded from model training, evaluation and improvement on every plan. Worker also says third-party model providers are contractually prohibited from training on customer content.

Ratmir Timashev, the Veeam founder backing Worker, said that building Veeam showed him the opportunity to bring powerful technology to businesses of all sizes. He said AI can now give small businesses more capacity without asking already stretched owners to work longer days, and he called Worker his bet on that shift. Bystroň said his dad ran a small construction firm, kept working harder, but the business wasn't always growing. He said the internet was supposed to make running a business easier, but for his dad it added more demands to a day that was already full, and he said AI will have failed people like his dad if all it does is give them more work to keep up with. He said they are building Worker so they can grow a business and still come home with time and energy for the people they love.

For institutions already evaluating DeltaGen, the acquisition raises a question of contractual continuity, and reviewing the relevant contract assignment provisions would be a separate institutional assessment rather than a consequence that can be inferred from the launch announcement alone. The stated audience remains business leadership, and the announcement does not identify a university or research-office deployment. EDUCAUSE describes HECVAT as a vendor questionnaire covering cybersecurity, privacy, accessibility and compliance, and its fourth generation adds AI-related questions. The acquisition announcement itself establishes neither institutional approval nor validated research performance. The source attribution was corrected on 13 November, and the sources were checked on 2026-11-15.

Worker puts a company's plan, responsibilities, key numbers and processes in one place, where employees and AI workers share the day-to-day work, and teams can hand off recurring tasks such as preparing updates or following up on commitments while decisions about the business stay with people. DeltaGen's technology listens to conversations as they happen and picks out decisions, commitments and next steps, and Worker then turns those into assigned tasks. If a team agrees to send a proposal once pricing is approved, for example, an AI worker writes the draft and asks for approval, and the responsible employee signs off on the pricing and sends it. Access is offered through managed onboarding, and the launch comes with managed onboarding. For universities considering this launch, HECVAT provides a relevant assessment framework, and the source of the data and the applicable account terms deserve separate attention.

stories.Headline: Chinese company launches AI laser device that targets flying mosquitoes
stories.Summary:
A Chinese company recently unveiled a new laser device powered by artificial intelligence that targets mosquitoes while they are flying. This innovative machine uses advanced tracking technology to identify the insects and burn their wings instantly. The product was introduced to the public on November 13, 2026, as a potential breakthrough in pest control. It aims to eliminate the need for traditional chemical sprays by using light to destroy pests. The system requires autonomous technology to ensure that the laser beams do not harm humans or household pets.

This specific design allows the device to distinguish between a small insect and a larger living creature. By focusing only on the mosquitoes, the machine can operate safely within a residential environment. The company believes this approach represents the future of how people will manage annoying insects in their homes. The developers of the technology are responsible for ensuring the safety and efficiency of the laser tracking system.

They stated that the autonomous features are specifically designed to keep people and their pets safe from the beams. While they did not provide a specific name for the company, they highlighted the precision of the AI. The goal is to provide a high-tech alternative to existing methods of mosquito eradication. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Thailand expects its AI industry to reach 12.2 billion USD by 2030
stories.Summary:
The National Board of Digital Economy and Society Office announced on Friday, November 13, 2026, that Thailand's artificial intelligence industry is poised for significant growth. The agency expects the sector to reach a value of 412 billion baht, or roughly 12.2 billion U.S. dollars, by 2030. This represents a substantial increase from the 187 billion baht, or 5.5 billion dollars, estimated for the current year. The growth is fueled by government support, foreign data center investments, and the nation's role as a global exporter of AI hardware.

This expansion requires a compound annual growth rate of 20.5 percent between 2025 and 2030, starting from an estimated 162 billion baht in 2025. Currently, hardware and infrastructure account for 72 percent of the industry's value and 86.6 percent of the 31.1 billion baht, or 921 million dollars, invested last year. Data from the National Electronics and Computer Technology Center shows that 53.7 percent of Thai organizations use AI this year, compared to 17.8 percent in 2024. Meanwhile, software and data services are growing the fastest at 26.3 percent annually.

The BDE is responsible for these projections and clarified that the figures measure the AI value chain rather than the gross domestic product. The agency noted that while demand for high-performance computing will drive investment, several risks exist. These challenges include a lack of AI talent, a dependence on imported graphics processing units, and energy supply issues for data centers. The agency believes that as AI spreads to the broader economy, more investment will flow into software, data platforms, and model development.

Articles.Title: Thailand expects AI industry to reach 12.2 bln USD by 2030 - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO following reports of extramarital affairs
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang abruptly resigned as the president, chief executive, and board member of Nvidia on Thursday, November 13, 2026. His immediate departure followed his admission of an extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman and reports of two other affairs with company employees. This sudden leadership change caused Nvidia shares to drop as much as 14 percent, eventually closing at $166.19. The company ended the day with a market value of $4.01 trillion.

The company now requires a permanent replacement for Huang, while Colette Kress, the chief financial officer and executive vice-president, will serve as the interim chief executive. The board is currently reviewing both internal and external candidates for the role. This transition occurs as the stock has fallen about 30 percent from its peak in October. Meanwhile, the company faces intense scrutiny from Congress and the FBI regarding national security and chip sales.

House Speaker Mike Johnson stated that there is a growing consensus in Congress to limit the export of semiconductor chips to China. Analysts from SemiAnalysis, including founder Dylan Patel, suggested that restrictions on China will likely accelerate now that Huang, a primary defender of market access, is gone. Ker Gibbs, a former president of the American Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai, noted that Nvidia lost its most effective advocate for the Chinese market. He believes the company will become more cautious and spend less time lobbying against export controls.

The situation may shift the balance of influence in Washington, as Huang had unique access to the White House. Lawmakers are considering whether Huang should provide congressional testimony this month to determine if national security was compromised. Observers will now monitor next week's earnings and forward guidance for signs of customer hesitation. Future developments depend on the selection of a permanent leader and the results of ongoing government investigations.

Articles.Title: Huang's exit puts Nvidia leadership, AI policy in focus - China Daily

stories.headline_source: Huang's exit puts Nvidia leadership, AI policy in focus

stories.Headline: Metanergy Inc introduces robotic arms powered by AI-enabled motors
stories.Summary:
Metanergy Inc. has introduced robotic arms that are powered by motors enabled by artificial intelligence. These advanced systems allow the robotic arms to move on their own through specialized posture and motor control. This development was highlighted in a report published by China Daily Global Edition on November 11, 2026. The integration of this technology represents a growing trend of AI implementation within various industrial scenarios. The new system requires the use of AI-enabled motors to improve overall efficiency and make the operational system smarter.

By utilizing these specific motors, the robotic arms can achieve autonomous movement without constant manual intervention. The articles do not provide specific technical numbers or dates regarding the initial development phase of these motors. However, the implementation of this technology changes how robotic arms function in industrial settings. Wang Lei, who serves as the board secretary and special assistant to the general manager at Metanergy Inc., is responsible for these comments.

He stated that artificial intelligence is playing an increasingly visible role in modern industrial scenarios. According to Wang, the use of AI-enabled motors is what makes the robotic systems smarter and more efficient. He explained that the ability for arms to move independently is a direct result of motor and posture control. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Chinese medical team introduces AI radiology tools to doctors in Tanzania
stories.Summary:
Ji Yugang, a radiologist with the 36th Chinese medical team, began exploring AI solutions for radiology in Zanzibar, Tanzania. This effort started after he noticed that Mnazi Mmoja Hospital lacked the AI tools he used in China. He found it difficult to manually review hundreds of images per patient without software assistance. The team arrived in Zanzibar on September 16 with 24 members. These specialists are divided between Unguja Island and Pemba Island.

The initiative focuses on introducing AI-assisted imaging for pulmonary nodule detection to improve diagnostic efficiency. Ji noted that his hospital in China adopted this technology eight to 10 years ago. The process requires training local doctors on AI principles, practical applications, and the necessity of professional verification. The team is also considering a system to send anonymized data to China for expert review. This would help local doctors overcome the current lack of software.

Team leader Wang Wei stated that the group provides clinical services, technical support, and professional training. He explained that the doctors also conduct free consultations in rural areas and mobile outreach programs. Local radiologist Saria Awesu Omar said the training is very important because it reduces workloads. She believes the technology will help doctors identify tiny lesions in the abdomen and chest. Omar added that the cooperation improves patient care and strengthens the friendship between the two nations.

The team currently uses real-time remote consultations to connect Zanzibar doctors with specialists in Chinese hospitals. They are working to resolve challenges regarding network connectivity and the anonymization of patient data. These steps are necessary before the AI analysis system can be used on a larger scale. The project aims to integrate mature Chinese medical experiences into the Tanzanian healthcare system. This collaboration allows local medical professionals to gain new skills.

stories.Headline: Pony.ai develops self-evolving AI to handle complex driving scenarios without human guidance
stories.Summary:
At the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit, a new stage of autonomous driving was presented. Xu Shanquan, who leads government affairs at Pony.ai, explained that artificial intelligence has evolved beyond the need for human tutoring. This shift allows AI to manage difficult driving scenarios with greater stability and efficiency. The technology now focuses on self-evolution to improve its own performance.

This transition requires AI to move toward a system of self-diagnosis and targeted evolution. By removing the reliance on human guidance, the software can identify its own errors and correct them. These changes ensure that the vehicles operate with higher safety standards. The goal is to create a system that learns independently to handle complex road conditions.

Xu Shanquan is the official responsible for sharing these updates from Pony.ai. He stated that the technology has moved past the phase of being taught by humans. According to Xu, the AI is now capable of evolving on its own to solve tough cases. He emphasized that this process increases the overall safety and reliability of the driving system.

stories.Headline: Gartner forecasts AI will create a net 1.7 million jobs by 2030 while reshaping roles for 435.5 million workers
stories.Summary:
The global market research firm Gartner published a report on November 15 forecasting that artificial intelligence will create more jobs than it eliminates by 2030. This analysis suggests that generative AI and AI agents will generate 10.6 million new positions while removing 8.9 million, resulting in a net gain of 1.7 million jobs. The research indicates that the primary impact will be a structural reshaping of the labor market rather than mass unemployment. Only a small fraction of the total workforce, estimated at no more than 1.8 percent, will directly lose their jobs to these technologies.

The transition requires a massive redesign of roles for 435.5 million people, which represents more than one in five workers globally and over 40 percent in the United States. Industry impacts vary, with the technology sector gaining 1.5 million net jobs and the public sector losing 500,000. Manufacturing, transportation, and mining will see a net gain of 400,000, while finance and insurance services will add 200,000 positions. In 2026, approximately 1.3 million hires were put on hold, and cumulative hiring delays are expected to affect over 5 million people by 2030.

Helen Poitevin, a senior vice president and analyst at Gartner, stated that successful companies view AI as a way to innovate operations rather than a tool for replacing staff. She explained that these organizations aim to ensure the economic value created by AI exceeds the simple substitution of the workforce. Gartner warned companies against cutting staff based on overly optimistic productivity assumptions, as this could lead to a need for corrective hiring later. The firm emphasized that workers remain essential to manage new technologies and operate modified work systems.

The report concludes that AI is a force that changes how work is performed rather than reducing the overall volume of employment. Companies that redeploy existing workers to match new tasks and continuously secure fresh talent are expected to perform better. Critics suggest that reducing hiring indiscriminately could block the inflow of new talent and damage long term technological capabilities. The forecast highlights that young people and those returning from career breaks will be most affected by current hiring contractions.

Articles.Title: Gartner: AI to Create Net 1.7 Million Jobs by 2030, But One in Five Workers Will Face Job Redesign

stories.Headline: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blames Chinese AI for cyberattacks on French supermarkets
stories.Summary:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent claimed on Thursday that a Chinese AI model caused cyberattacks on French supermarkets. These attacks targeted refrigeration systems and occurred in October, causing food to spoil. Bessent spoke at the Heritage Foundation and alleged that Chinese AI tools lack necessary guardrails. He stated that these models are dangerous to global security.

The attacks affected 150 grocery stores across France by exploiting remote management interfaces. Hackers activated forced-defrost functions and raised temperatures to 50 C, destroying vast amounts of food. These actions caused losses that could reach millions of euros. China's Ministry of State Security highlighted these events on October 28 to warn about threats to physical infrastructure.

Professor Hu Qimu of Huaqiao University criticized the US for making these claims without public technical evidence. He argued that Washington is using the incident to smear Chinese technology and justify containment. Hu stated that cybersecurity should rely on objective analysis rather than political accusations. He noted that the US frequently restricts Chinese firms based on national security.

French authorities previously accused Iran's Revolutionary Guard of responsibility for the October attacks. They warned that there would be consequences for the Iranian group. Meanwhile, China promoted its 2025 Global AI Governance Action Plan to encourage international cooperation. Hu suggested that nations should work together to prevent the misuse of technology.

Articles.Title: US uses French supermarket cyberattacks to smear Chinese AI, fueling broader tech containment push: analyst - Global Times

stories.headline_source: US uses French supermarket cyberattacks to smear Chinese AI, fueling broader tech containment push: analyst

stories.Headline: Shenzhen deploys AI assistants and driverless shuttles for APEC meeting visitors
stories.Summary:
Shenzhen is preparing for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting which will be held on November 18 and 19 in Guangdong Province. The city has entered a period called APEC time to welcome international visitors with various new technological innovations and smart services. AI assistants, multilingual translation terminals, and driverless shuttles have appeared across the city to greet the arriving delegates and other guests. These advanced tools aim to showcase how technological innovation is reshaping urban life and facilitating international exchanges for the global event. Preparations are currently in full swing to ensure the city is ready for the high profile meeting starting in less than a week.

Bao'an International Airport has launched an AI travel assistant and translation terminals supporting 38 languages at the service center and transportation desk. A facial recognition boarding system allows passengers to submit entry information via QR codes, completing immigration clearance in as little as one minute. Level 4 autonomous minibuses with over 20 sensors, including LiDAR and cameras, operate on a downtown route near the Luohu Port. These vehicles feature central control screens, voice commands for music and temperature, and the ability to navigate complex intersections and traffic lights. Ultra-high-bandwidth networking provides peak downlink speeds of 1.5 gigabits per second and stable speeds of 10 megabits per second during peak periods.

The Shenzhen municipal statistics bureau released data on October 23 regarding the growth of the city's high tech and advanced manufacturing sectors. Officials state that the city will showcase its industrial ecosystem in robotics, new vehicles, and the digital economy to connect Asia-Pacific markets. They report that high tech manufacturing value-added output rose 11.6 percent, while advanced manufacturing increased by 11.9 percent in the first three quarters. Production of industrial robots grew by 44.1 percent, lithium-ion batteries by 38.5 percent, and 3D printing equipment by 77.8 percent this year. These figures highlight the city's reputation as China's Silicon Valley and a global hub for embodied intelligence and artificial intelligence.

Modern Diplomacy noted that Shenzhen was chosen for the APEC meeting because of its status as a global hub for AI technology. International delegates and visitors are the primary people affected by the new smart services and the upgraded communications infrastructure at border checkpoints. In a separate development, Johannes Wigand, founder of LiveVoice, said AI translation allows congregations to welcome visitors in their own languages. Simon Egli from ICF Church stated that the LiveVoice platform is simple to use for both the interpreters and the listeners. Jan Hendrik of Willow Creek noted that the tool accommodates the needs of both their on-site and their online audiences.

LiveVoice is an Austria-based platform in Salzburg that has now surpassed 150,000 multilingual church services using AI translation in over 70 languages. The system allows worshippers to hear sermons on their own phones via QR codes, replacing expensive rented receivers and interpreter booths. This cloud-based technology has seen over 850,000 app downloads and 50,000 admin users across more than 100 different countries and various venues. It is used by ministries like Hillsong, Alpha, OM, and ICF, as well as sports events like the Biathlon World Cup. The platform can lower costs for smaller congregations by 80 percent while avoiding hygiene concerns associated with using shared headsets.

The APEC meeting will soon demonstrate Shenzhen's advanced robotics and digital economy to leaders from across the Asia-Pacific region during the summit. LiveVoice continues to expand its reach by offering participant-based pricing and pay-as-you-go AI translation for churches and other large scale events. The articles leave open how the APEC delegates will react to the Level 4 autonomous driving and the AI airport assistants. It remains unclear if other cities will adopt the specific ultra-high-bandwidth networking technology used at the Shenzhen transportation hubs and checkpoints. The future growth rates for Shenzhen's high tech manufacturing products beyond the third quarter of the year are not provided.

stories.Headline: Ian Bezek argues Analog Devices is overvalued at 29 times EV/EBITDA and doubts its 2027 EPS projections
stories.Summary:
Ian Bezek, an investing group leader writing for Seeking Alpha on November 14, 2026, argued that Analog Devices is a fine company whose current share price is unattractive. He noted that the firm trades at 29 times EV/EBITDA and 14 times EV/sales despite being a cyclical business with relatively low annualized revenue growth over the long term. Bezek wrote that Analog Devices is not a pureplay AI company and that he thinks investors have assigned too much value to the firm's data center angle. He said he expects a solid Q4 report later that month but has doubts about whether the company will hit current 2027 EPS projections. The article rests on the valuation multiples of 29 times EV/EBITDA and 14 times EV/sales, and it ties the stock's appeal to a data center angle that the author considers overvalued.

Bezek described the business as cyclical with relatively low annualized revenue growth over the long term, which he set against the current share price. He also separated his expected solid Q4 report from his doubts about the 2027 EPS projections. The piece was published on November 14, 2026, and carried the ticker NASDAQ:ADI. Bezek is responsible for the views, and the disclosure states that he holds a beneficial long position in Texas Instruments shares through stock ownership, options or other derivatives. He wrote that he has been a shareholder in Texas Instruments for more than a decade and sees the appeal of a long-term outlook for analog semiconductor businesses.

He stated that he wrote the article himself and that it expresses his own opinions, and that he receives no compensation for it other than from Seeking Alpha. He added that he has no business relationship with any company whose stock is mentioned in the article. The context is that Bezek is a former hedge fund analyst at Kerrisdale Capital who leads the investing group Ian's Insider Corner, which offers a Weekend Digest, trade alerts, an active chat room and direct access to him. Seeking Alpha's disclosure states that past performance is no guarantee of future results and that no recommendation or advice is being given as to whether any investment is suitable for a particular investor. The article does not say what happens next beyond the expected Q4 report later in November 2026 and the 2027 EPS projections.

stories.Headline: Tony Chan urges China to prioritize genuine AI innovation over model rankings
stories.Summary:
Tony Chan spoke via video on November 13 during the 17th Caixin Summit. He is a former president of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and a member of the U.S. National Academy of Engineering. Chan addressed the current state of the artificial intelligence industry in China. He urged the nation to prioritize genuine innovation over simple model rankings.

The speaker suggested that China should leverage its supply chains, traditional industries, and culture. He argued against merely increasing parameter counts for large models or trying to avoid export sanctions. Chan noted that Chinese models reach 90 to 95 percent of benchmark performance compared to U.S. versions. He estimated that the gap between the two countries is less than six months.

Chan stated that China currently leads in AI applications, mature-process chips, and renewable energy. However, he acknowledged that the U.S. maintains an advantage in capital markets, advanced chips, and top scholars. He expressed doubt that increasing computing power alone would lead to artificial general intelligence. He believes the industry must earn respect through original approaches.

The context of these remarks involves a competitive landscape where open-source models and lower costs pressure U.S. firms. Chan believes that focusing on these strengths will better position China in the global market. He emphasized that the goal should be creating value rather than chasing rankings. The summit provided a platform to discuss these strategic shifts for the future.

stories.Headline: ISC2 requires in-person testing after AI cheating found in online proctoring pilots
stories.Summary:
Test takers are turning to artificial intelligence to answer questions on IT certification exams, Dark Reading reported on November 11, 2026. Marielle Carlos, a data forensics scientist at Caveon, said AI has significantly changed the testing game for IT certification. Caveon added a new category to its testing security threats taxonomy called unknown. Casey Marks, chief operating officer at ISC2, said widespread irregular exam results and verified cheating attempts were found during the nonprofit's online proctoring pilots. ISC2 then required in-person testing for its exams.

ISC2 implemented what Marks called the most stringent security protocols available to analyze each result and detect irregularities, including biometric and identity verification. ISC2 is exclusively test-center based for all exams, which Marks said ensures no access to outside resources or technology during exam administration. The testing environment mirrors the most stringent conditions used by licensed professions such as doctors. Certifications range from entry-level cloud and cybersecurity knowledge and cover Google, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services updates. In industries like government, banking, and financial services, certified IT departments are required to stay current on compliance regulations.

Carlos said it is hard to know if an exam is measuring actual competence or someone's ability to use AI to answer the question. She said this challenges the usefulness of that exam. Marks said the candidate, the employer, and every other professional holding that credential depend on the credibility of the process. Carlos urged programs to have conversations around protecting score validity across the entire process, including secure exam design, control during administration, analysis of results, and a clear process for responding to security concerns. She said a layered approach is crucial because tools can indicate possible AI use but it is hard to pinpoint exactly.

Carlos pointed to research by Sarah Toton, director of data forensics at Caveon, who conducted an experiment comparing AI and human test taking based on test results and response patterns. Carlos said Toton has seen distinct differences in response timing, with someone using AI often six to 48 times faster compared to an individual test taker. Carlos said AI can get some things wrong, particularly questions that involve some realm of human judgment. Marks said certifications remain one of the most universal ways for employers to validate a candidate's necessary knowledge and skills when making hiring or promotion decisions. Carlos noted a huge boom of people testing fast and receiving high scores, though no concrete data exists that says it is all due to AI.

Carlos said traditional threats like harvesting pre-knowledge, plagiarism, or collusion proxy testing have evolved as people use AI as an unauthorized aid. She said the problem is still in its infancy stage. Exam administrators face a growing list of risks to monitor, from Meta Glasses to AI browsers and deepfakes. The industry is shifting toward more in-person testing and stricter fraud-detection protocols to keep certifications credible. Carlos said she and her team will look more at the trend of fast testing and high scores because of organizational interest and concern over its growth.

Marks said many certifications, like ISC2's Certified Information Systems Security Professional, have and continue to evolve to address how AI is impacting security best practices. He said new AI-specific security certifications are also entering the market. The Computing Technology Industry Association launched SecAI+ to help organizations secure, govern, and responsibly integrate AI into their cybersecurity operations. Marks said that as certifications evolve, especially with AI playing a key role in so many facets of work, the value of certifications for employers is increasing. Carlos said cheating is a risk that has existed for as long as testing has.

stories.Headline: Zimperium researchers say ArcticRAT gang adds Grok AI to Android malware for financial fraud
stories.Summary:
Zimperium researchers reported on November 13, 2026 that the ArcticRAT cybercrime gang had turned its Android malware from a cryptocurrency stealer into a full remote access Trojan. The operators added large language model services to sift stolen text messages for financial data worth exploiting. Zimperium called the change a dangerous escalation in the mobile threat landscape. The newer versions let attackers interact with infected devices in real time instead of relying on hardcoded actions. The gang used malvertising, smishing and third-party forums to send visitors to malicious websites carrying the malware.

Early ArcticRAT versions targeted users of 11 specific cryptocurrency applications to harvest data for access to crypto accounts. The new versions add remote device control and surveillance, credential and keystroke theft, screen capture, live screen streaming, microphone monitoring, and theft of SMS messages, contacts and call logs. Attackers can also steal or change lock-screen credentials, potentially locking victims out of their devices. Since July, Zimperium identified 78 unique malware samples, 42 dropper samples, 36 payloads and 21 IP addresses used for command-and-control communications. The researchers also found 129 distinct commands for remotely controlling infected devices, stealing information, monitoring activity and manipulating device functions.

Nico Chiaraviglio, chief scientist at Zimperium, said ArcticRAT uses AI to read user information such as SMS messages to filter for financial information that could be used to perform fraud. He said one particularly challenging technique is hidden remote control combined with a black-screen overlay, with attackers abusing legitimate Android features while making the device appear locked or powered off. He said defending against such threats requires AI-powered on-device threat detection, controls over application installation and permissions, and runtime application protection to spot suspicious screen-sharing activity and malicious overlays. Zimperium said the primary attack vector relied on a landing page that convincingly impersonated Google Play to trick targets into downloading a malicious application. The researchers observed attackers in some instances using Amazon Web Services storage buckets to deliver the payload directly on Android devices.

Zimperium found the malware features an API connection to xAI's Grok model, which attackers can activate remotely to examine installed applications and identify banking, cryptocurrency and trading platforms. The AI capabilities let ArcticRAT process stolen SMS messages and separate routine and promotional messages from one-time authentication codes, account balance changes and transaction notifications. It can even estimate a victim's financial standing before sending the information to its command-and-control infrastructure, according to Zimperium. The firm said this automates much of the work of sorting large volumes of stolen information rather than manually examining the data. Zimperium said that as mobile Trojan threats like ArcticRAT become increasingly sophisticated, conventional signature-based security layers are no longer sufficient to protect enterprise mobile endpoints.

Once installed, the latest version abuses Android Accessibility Services permissions to connect with its command-and-control servers, giving attackers remote control over the device. The malware first collects information about the compromised device, including its location, battery status, screen state, Wi-Fi connectivity and currently active applications. It sends that information to the attackers, who can then select which functions to activate based on the victim's device and installed applications. The malware uses a completely black, un-dismissible screen overlay to conceal attacker activities from victims. Analysts noted the trend underscores the need for users and organizations to stop treating mobile devices as secondary security concerns and to apply the same threat monitoring, access controls and protections as for traditional endpoints.

The article was written by Illinois-based Jai Vijayan, a veteran technology journalist with more than 25 years of experience covering cybersecurity. Zimperium is tracking the malware and described the evolution as an example of how quickly mobile threats are evolving, with attackers using AI to make malware more capable and dangerous. The article gives no indication of how many victims have been infected or where they are located. It does not say whether law enforcement or Google has taken any action against the gang or its infrastructure. It also does not say what the attackers do with the financial intelligence after it reaches their command-and-control servers.

stories.Headline: Google DeepMind AI agents find cheaper ways to attack 1024-bit RSA systems
stories.Summary:
Google DeepMind has announced that AI agents, working under human supervision, found two ways to lower the cost of attacking 1024-bit RSA cryptosystems. The work was done with cryptographers from UC San Diego and Inria, and the results were reported on November 10, 2026. The findings suggest that attacks on legacy RSA-1024 need less computing effort than was previously assumed. The company says the results mainly affect these older systems. The first method concerns digital signatures and padding.

DeepMind found that if an attacker controls roughly half or more of a signed block, the padding gives no protection. The finding is especially relevant to the PKCS#1 v1.5 format used in devices such as hardware security modules. In a sandboxed test, the agents re-ran an earlier academic forgery attack on a 1024-bit key and cut the CPU time from 1,380 core-years to 391 core-years, a 3.5-fold improvement. Kohli, VP at Google DeepMind, noted that this signature attack does not recover the private key and requires around 4 billion signing queries made in advance.

The second method concerns factoring several RSA keys of the same size. The agents developed an algorithm that, on average, makes factoring each additional 1024-bit key about 30 times cheaper than previous methods. That estimate, however, assumes an initial computation as costly as factoring one key, and the method has not yet been implemented. Kohli stated that modern encryption protocols, which almost universally use 2048-bit or larger keys, remain secure.

The researchers concluded that cryptographic hardness cannot be treated as a fixed assumption in an era of AI-enabled computation. The researchers emphasised that using AI to rigorously test long-held assumptions will help ensure the security of modern encryption. The articles do not say what steps are planned for operators of legacy 1024-bit systems. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Pinterest misses revenue guidance as AI disruption fears grow and Europe ARPU falls 7%
stories.Summary:
Pinterest missed its own revenue guidance in its latest quarter, and the shortfall gave fresh evidence to investors worried that artificial intelligence is disrupting the company's core advertising business. The report, published by Seeking Alpha on November 14, 2026, said the company's growth decelerated sharply from one quarter to the next. Average revenue per user rose just 1%, while average revenue per user in Europe actually fell 7%. The company's fourth-quarter guidance now implies growth of only 8% to 12%, a marked slowdown for a business once expected to expand far faster.

The article, written by Seeking Alpha investing group leader Julian Lin, said Pinterest remains a Buy despite becoming what he called a show-me story. He argued that AI disruption fears and sharply decelerating growth have compressed the stock's valuation to roughly 10 times estimated earnings. At that level, he wrote, the shares offer a margin of safety supported by net cash on the balance sheet. He also pointed to potential upside from either faster growth or margin expansion, though he acknowledged that AI-enhanced competitors and weakness in advertising threaten any recovery.

Lin placed responsibility for the turnaround on management, writing that the company still believes improving international results can restore growth to the mid- to high-teens range. He said better monetization outside the United States could deliver that recovery, but he framed it as an open question rather than a certainty. His disclosure states that he holds a beneficial long position in Pinterest shares, along with Meta and Alphabet, through stock ownership, options or other derivatives. He wrote the article himself, he said, and receives no compensation for it beyond his arrangement with Seeking Alpha.

The context is a stock that has fallen out of favor as investors weigh whether AI tools will pull advertising dollars away from Pinterest's visual discovery platform. Lin's answer is that the valuation already reflects much of that fear, leaving room for upside if international monetization improves. The articles do not say when Pinterest next reports results or what specific steps management plans to take. They also give no date for a recovery, so the next signal will be whether fourth-quarter growth lands within the 8% to 12% range the company has guided toward.

stories.Headline: NTT DATA publishes an IDC InfoBrief on sovereign AI for insurance
stories.Summary:
NTT DATA published an IDC InfoBrief on sovereign AI for insurance, dated 14 November 2026, with a second version dated 12 November 2026. The company also held a webinar on 3 November 2026 about the research. The InfoBrief looks at how insurers can deploy AI securely and at scale. It covers underwriting, claims, fraud detection and compliance.

The InfoBrief sets out several goals for insurers using sovereign and private AI. It says they should move AI from pilot to production while protecting sensitive data and keeping governance, explainability and regulatory compliance. It also lists ways to transform underwriting and claims, strengthen fraud detection while protecting sensitive data, and build trust through explainability and auditability. NTT DATA's AI Factory is described as helping organizations move from isolated AI pilots to secure, governed AI at scale with measurable business outcomes. The pages invite readers to get the InfoBrief, read a data sheet and explore a chapter for their industry.

NTT DATA presents the research as showing how insurers scale AI with trust and control. The company says its AI Factory helps organizations move from isolated pilots to governed AI at scale. The pages describe the aim as building trusted, resilient AI for insurance. They also offer a form asking for contact details such as name, email, job title, country, phone number and company.

The pages link to related material, including a blog from 14 October 2026 on agentic AI as the biggest shift in insurance since digital transformation. They also link to a 2026 Global AI Report for Insurance dated 9 June 2026 and a report on fast-tracking the future of insurance dated 3 September 2026. The InfoBrief is presented as guidance on sovereign AI for insurance, with a chapter for each industry. The pages do not say what happens after readers request the InfoBrief.

stories.Headline: Claude AI predicts Chainlink will recover before XRP in 2027
stories.Summary:
Claude AI, in an article by Sam Daodu published November 14, 2026 on 24/7 Wall St., predicted that Chainlink will recover before XRP in 2027. XRP and Chainlink have fallen sharply, dropping more than 25% in just 30 days. XRP is down 28%, trading around 96 cents, while Chainlink has fallen 26.9% to about $9.16. Both coins reached their 30-day lows on November 13 and have continued their downward trend since then. According to Claude AI, recovery means returning to pre-loss prices.

For XRP, recovery means reaching about $1.29, while Chainlink needs to hit $11.69. Claude AI suggests Chainlink will recover first, needing a 25.2% gain, while XRP needs a 30.8% increase. Chainlink has fared better this year, with a year-to-date drop of 25.4%, whereas XRP has plummeted by 47.8%. The AI predicts Chainlink will bounce back in May 2027, three months ahead of XRP's anticipated recovery in August 2027. The model estimates Chainlink has a 64% chance of recovering at any point in 2027, while XRP's chance is 58%.

Both coins clear the 50% mark because the model views 25% to 31% annual gains as typical in the cryptocurrency market. Both remain below 80% because of rising interest rates, with the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.10% on November 12, up from 4.84% on November 5. The model projects XRP at $0.88 in March 2027, $1.08 in June 2027, $1.31 in September 2027 and $1.48 in December 2027. Chainlink is projected at $8.90 in March 2027, $11.80 in June 2027, $12.60 in September 2027 and $13.10 in December 2027. Chainlink is forecast to hit its lowest point first, around $8.50 to $8.90, before crossing the $11.69 mark by the end of June.

XRP's main growth driver will be money flowing into U.S. spot XRP funds, which experienced outflows of $19.1 million from November 9 to November 13. Claude AI's August 2027 recovery date assumes inflows will average around $25 million weekly through the second quarter of 2027. The model estimates Ripple's dollar-pegged stablecoin RLUSD will have a supply of around $2.79 billion, but RLUSD needs to exceed $5 billion before it can significantly influence prices in 2027. At $19.1 million per week, outflows could total about $993 million over a year, which may keep XRP's price between 80 cents and $1.15 throughout 2027. Chainlink serves as an oracle network that supplies external data, like pricing information, to blockchain applications.

On November 13, Chainlink announced new integrations, including Aave and LlamaRisk using the Chainlink Runtime Environment to set Aave V3's borrow limits. Chainlink's announcement highlighted the introduction of dynamic borrow limits that adjust with demand, helping maintain liquidity for Aave V3 users. Chainlink tends to decline when Bitcoin drops in value, and if the 10-year Treasury yield remains above 5% and Bitcoin falls below $55,000, about 17% below its level of roughly $65,900, Chainlink could plummet toward $7. XRP has fallen 17.4% over the past week and trades 73.7% below its $3.65 all-time high from July 2025. Chainlink has dropped 16% and trades 82.6% below its $52.70 peak from May 2021.

For Chainlink to clear its $11.69 recovery line by May 2027, it must hold its projected floor of $8.50, while Bitcoin needs to remain above $55,000. If XRP funds attract around $25 million a week by spring 2027, XRP may close the gap. Should Bitcoin break below $55,000 first, neither coin may recover in 2027. The AI projects XRP could gain 50% from its current price to December 2027, compared to a 40.3% increase for Chainlink. Larger targets like the $5 mark for XRP seem distant right now.

stories.Headline: Gustavo Espinosa says agentic AI needs governance of unstructured enterprise data
stories.Summary:
Gustavo Espinosa, Head of Data & AI at NTT DATA International Clients USA, NTT DATA, Inc., published an article on November 10, 2026, titled Unstructured Data Governance: A missing foundation for agentic AI at scale. The article appeared on nttdata.com and was also dated 10 November 2026 in a second version. It says generative AI and now agentic AI are pushing organizations beyond databases and analytical datasets into unstructured enterprise data and content. That content includes documents, presentations, emails, contracts, policies, conversations, images, audio and video. The article says most of this content was never created or managed with AI consumption in mind.

The article says enterprise data governance has focused for years on structured data such as tables, fields, models, lineage, quality rules, access controls and ownership. It says the principles remain but the capabilities must evolve, and that organizations still need ownership, metadata, quality, lineage, security, retention and accountability. It says a customer table has fields, while a contract has clauses, dates, entities and obligations that first need to be extracted and understood. It says an AI pipeline may convert a document into text, divide it into chunks, create embeddings and place those representations into a retrieval index, requiring controls to propagate across every derived representation. It says an audio recording may need transcription and speaker identification before its meaning becomes machine-usable.

The article says traditional cataloging evolves into repository discovery and content inventory, and data profiling expands into OCR, transcription, parsing and multimodal inspection. It says classification expands into topic, entity and sensitivity detection, and lineage extends beyond systems and datasets into documents, chunks, embeddings and AI responses. It says data quality expands beyond completeness and validity into readability, structural integrity, semantic consistency, extraction accuracy and relevance to the intended AI use case. It says the goal is to transform fragmented enterprise content into information assets that are discoverable, understandable, trusted, protected and reusable. It says governance must answer not only whether information can be accessed but whether it should be used, for what purpose, by whom or by what agent, and under what conditions.

The article describes a continuous operating model with visibility, understanding, control and qualification, and activation. It says visibility covers what content exists, where it resides and who owns it, and understanding covers parsing, transcribing, segmenting and enriching content. It says control and qualification apply metadata, classification, quality rules, retention, access controls and AI-use criteria, and activation makes governed content available through search, analytics, RAG, assistants and agents. It says policies need to be executable and continuously enforced rather than documented separately and applied manually after the fact. It says governance becomes embedded in the flow of information itself.

The article says enterprises moving toward AI agents need a persistent enterprise context layer called the Company Brain, which is not simply an enterprise search engine or a collection of documents connected to an LLM. It says outdated documents lead agents to reason over outdated context, and conflicting versions without clear authority may lead agents to select the wrong source. It says permissions not carried into AI retrieval may let an agent expose information the user could never access directly, and missing semantics may let an agent retrieve the right words while misunderstanding their meaning. It says absent provenance leaves organizations unable to explain which information influenced a response or action. It says unstructured data governance is one component of a broader enterprise context governance discipline ensuring knowledge is current, understandable, traceable, protected and accountable.

The article says a chatbot that retrieves an incorrect policy may produce an incorrect answer, while an agent may use that same policy to initiate a workflow, modify a system or recommend an action. It says NTT DATA has been working with assets and accelerators that evaluate unstructured content across semantic quality, visual and structural quality, and compliance and risk, producing a quantitative assessment and a disposition that acts as an AI-readiness gate. It says a policy may say sensitive customer information must be protected, a standard defines that content as restricted, a machine-readable rule applies that classification, a control masks the content and prevents unauthorized retrieval, and evidence records what was detected and enforced. It says organizations that succeed with agentic AI will be those that turn enterprise information into trusted, governed and machine-usable context. It directs readers to read more about NTT DATA's AI services to learn how to operationalize AI throughout their organization.

stories.Headline: S&P 500 fund lists Alphabet twice, tying $10,380 of a $200,000 401(k) to one company
stories.Summary:
A hypothetical 58-year-old holds $200,000 of his 401(k) in an S&P 500 index fund and believes no single AI stock can do much damage. State Street published October 22 holdings for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) that show Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) listed twice. Gerelyn Terzo wrote the 24/7 Wall St. article published November 14, 2026, at 6:03pm ET. The piece appeared on The Full Benefits Desk, edited by Gerelyn Terzo. The article ran about three minutes of reading.

Alphabet Class A shares (GOOGL) carry voting rights, and Class C shares (NASDAQ:GOOG) carry none. Class B is held by insiders and does not trade publicly. The S&P 500 weights stocks by market value and gives each public class its own position. The October 22 report put Class A at 2.88% of the fund and Class C at 2.31%, or 5.19% together. SPY's March fact sheet listed the two classes at 3% and 2%.

At the combined 5.19% weight, $10,380 of his $200,000 is tied to Alphabet. If both classes fell 20% and every other holding stayed flat, the account would lose about $2,076, roughly 1% of his balance. Class A shares fell from about $353 on October 12 to $299 on November 12, a slide of roughly 15% in one month. The stock's 52-week high was nearly $409. In the July 31 filing for the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (NYSEARCA:RSP), the two classes together made up about 0.19% of assets, or roughly $388 on $200,000.

Alphabet's third-quarter Google Cloud revenue grew 103% to $31 billion, and capital spending reached $51 billion, up 114%, leaving free cash flow at negative $9 billion. CEO Sundar Pichai said Google Cloud revenue jumped 103% as demand for AI infrastructure surged. Alphabet missed Wall Street's revenue estimates, and earnings came to $2.12 a share, weighed down by an $8.7 billion loss on equity investments. Bloomberg Intelligence estimates U.S. hyperscalers will spend roughly $857 billion on capital projects in 2026. Reuters reports that Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Google stand to gain a large windfall from an Anthropic IPO.

The article suggests adding every share class together, weighting each fund's figure by the dollars held in it. It suggests setting a personal ceiling for any one company, limiting it at 5% of the total portfolio as one example. It suggests rebalancing inside the 401(k), where moving money between funds does not trigger capital gains. It suggests checking for overlap, since a large-cap growth fund or technology sector fund also holds both Alphabet classes. The article's moral is that two ticker symbols still mean one business, to be treated as one holding.

The article notes that at 58, a sharp drop just before withdrawals begin does more damage than the same drop at 35. It says the AI build-out may well pay off, and the issue for a saver near retirement is position size. It says the combined stake is easy to miss because the classes appear on separate lines of a holdings screen. It says this was already true earlier in the year. It says Alphabet is hardly alone.

stories.Headline: NTT Data is placed in the Leaders Category of IDC MarketScape for cloud services in the AI era
stories.Summary:
NTT DATA announced on 12 November 2026 that it had been placed in the Leaders Category of the IDC MarketScape for Worldwide Cloud Professional Services in the AI Era 2026 Vendor Assessment. The assessment was published by IDC in September 2026 under the number US54117426 and was written by Jennifer Thomson and Eren Eser. The vendor assessment examines the providers that help organizations build the data, governance and operating foundations required for AI at scale. NTT DATA shared the result in an insights post on its website dated 12 November 2026. The assessment frames cloud as no longer simply a destination for modernization but as the platform that enables AI-driven business outcomes.

It covers the role cloud must play in an AI strategy and treats AI-model and hyperscaler ecosystem access as a selection factor. It also addresses AI governance, FinOps and agentic operating models, along with sovereign cloud and data residency capabilities. The post says readers can learn why NTT DATA was recognized as a Leader and offers a download of the assessment. IDC MarketScape uses a rigorous scoring methodology based on both qualitative and quantitative criteria, which results in a single graphical illustration of each supplier's position within a given market. The framework lets technology buyers compare the product and service offerings, capabilities and strategies, and current and future market success factors of suppliers.

IDC describes the model as providing a 360-degree assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of current and prospective suppliers. The post attributes the Leaders placement to the independent assessment rather than to NTT DATA's own evaluation. The post presents cloud as the foundation for AI at scale and lists the topics the assessment covers for organizations weighing cloud providers. It does not state how many vendors were assessed, what scores NTT DATA received or where other providers were placed. The articles give no information on what happens next beyond the availability of the download and the related insights link.

stories.Headline: Riskified CEO Eido Gal warns fraudsters adopt AI shopping tools faster than consumers
stories.Summary:
Riskified Ltd. reported third-quarter results on Wednesday that beat analyst estimates and lifted its full-year forecast for the third time this year, and chief executive and co-founder Eido Gal used the earnings call to warn that fraudsters are adopting AI-powered shopping tools faster than consumers in some cases. The fraud prevention company posted adjusted earnings of 7 cents per share against a 3-cent estimate, while revenue jumped 41% year over year to $115.18 million and topped expectations of $103.41 million. Gross merchandise volume rose 18% to $44.56 billion, U.S. billings jumped 69% from 38% growth in the second quarter, and Digital Finance billings soared more than 300%. Adjusted gross profit rose 20% to $49.7 million even as gross margin fell to 43% from 51%, adjusted EBITDA climbed 47% to $8.1 million, and the net loss narrowed to $1.3 million from $7.8 million.

The company lifted its 2026 revenue forecast to a range of $427 million to $433 million from $400 million to $410 million, exceeding Wall Street's estimate of $406.7 million, and raised its adjusted EBITDA forecast to $39 million to $43 million from $33 million to $39 million. Riskified ended the quarter with $235 million in cash, deposits and investments and no debt, and it generated $15.2 million in free cash flow. It launched Agent Identity Risk Intelligence to address fraud involving AI agents and partnered with Zendesk to detect fraudulent refunds, returns and exchanges. Eight of its 10 largest new customers were based outside the U.S., with APAC and Other Americas billings up 14% and 17% while EMEA declined 3%.

Gal said growing demand for fraud prevention tools helped the company raise its outlook, and he highlighted new opportunities from AI-powered commerce. He warned on the call that Riskified is seeing more fraudulent attempts involving AI agents, particularly in refunds, returns and other customer service requests. The company attributed its raised forecast to strong quarterly results and continued momentum, and its stock surged Wednesday after the report. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the raised guidance and the new products.

stories.Headline: Australia attorney general Michelle Rowland weighs criminal charges against OpenAI over unauthorized website access
stories.Summary:
Australia's Attorney-General Michelle Rowland announced on Friday, November 13, 2026, that her office is considering criminal charges against OpenAI. This potential legal action follows reports that models developed by the company breached several Australian government websites without authorization. The government is currently investigating whether these unauthorized accesses violate existing laws or require new legal frameworks. Officials are working to determine if the actions of AI agents can be prosecuted under current statutes. The situation requires a detailed examination of potential criminal law reforms to address the unique challenges of artificial intelligence.

These proposed changes could include strict penalties for AI companies that fail to prevent harmful conduct by their systems. Government officials have not yet decided if any new laws created for this purpose could be applied retrospectively to past events. Additionally, the government is focusing on the unauthorized use of Australian creative works without payment or consent. The state believes that commercial licensing agreements between technology companies and rightsholders remain the best way to resolve these disputes. Attorney-General Michelle Rowland is the official responsible for overseeing these legal inquiries and potential prosecutions.

She stated that existing criminal laws in Australia have not yet been tested against the behavior of AI agents. Rowland expressed criticism regarding the way technology companies use creative content without providing proper compensation to the original creators. She emphasized that the government is still resolving whether the current legal system is sufficient to handle these breaches. The Attorney-General remains open to the possibility of charges while the legal analysis continues. More to follow.

stories.Headline: NTT Data Luxembourg leads NanoAI plan to link two Luxembourg data centres over 70km optical network
stories.Summary:
Luxembourg and NTT are exploring cooperation on photonic networks, artificial intelligence and quantum technologies, and the talks include a proposed project that would connect two data centres in Luxembourg using optical networking technology. The initiative, called NanoAI, is led by NTT Data Luxembourg and would link the two facilities over a connection of roughly 70 kilometres. It would use the All-Photonics Network technology of the Innovative Optical and Wireless Network Global Forum, known as IOWN. The project aims to investigate whether computing resources in geographically separate locations can work together in the way the partners hope.

The proposal rests on optical networking rather than the conventional electrical switching used in most data centres today, according to the description of the plan. The roughly 70-kilometre link between the two Luxembourg facilities is the concrete element named in the articles, and no start date, budget or participant list beyond NTT Data Luxembourg is given. The articles do not say how the NanoAI work would be funded or which other organisations, if any, have signed on. They also do not state whether the project has moved beyond the exploration stage or when any decision is expected.

NTT is the company behind the IOWN Global Forum's All-Photonics Network technology, and NTT Data Luxembourg is named as the leader of the NanoAI initiative. The articles do not attribute any direct statements to named officials from NTT or from the Luxembourg side, so no one is quoted on the record about the plan. Responsibility for the proposed link therefore sits with NTT Data Luxembourg as the named lead, with Luxembourg as the partner exploring the cooperation. The articles give no further detail on who within either organisation would oversee the work.

The context is that Luxembourg and NTT are looking at photonic networks, AI and quantum technologies together, and the data centre link is one proposed piece of that broader exploration. The articles describe the NanoAI project as aiming to test whether separated computing resources can be combined, which is the stated purpose of the roughly 70-kilometre optical connection. What happens next is not specified beyond the fact that the parties are exploring cooperation, and the articles do not say when the exploration might produce a decision. No timeline, no confirmed launch and no further steps are given in the material available.
