stories.Headline: Australia’s seat belt mandate shows how built-in safeguards cut road deaths and can guide AI security
stories.Summary:
Australia's experience with road safety shows how engineered protections can work alongside human accountability, according to an article published by IT Brief Australia on 13 November 2026. By 1970 faster vehicle speeds had pushed the annual road toll in Victoria alone to 1061, a level that public education and traffic rules could not address. In 1970 Victoria became the first jurisdiction in the world to make wearing seat belts mandatory. Seat belts were later supplemented with airbags, crumple zones and other safety features built directly into every car. That combination of engineered controls and driver training saw Victoria's annual road toll decline by more than 70 per cent over the next three decades.

The article argues that managing AI security risks now requires a similar shift from rules governing how technology is used to protections built into the technology itself. Regulatory guidelines set necessary boundaries, but they cannot stop an attack that tricks an AI system into following malicious instructions or halt a breach already in progress. The challenge grows when AI systems can act autonomously across multiple government systems, and the article says Australia is seeing rapid evolution of software that acts autonomously and with authority. The fundamental governance question for Australian leaders is no longer about controlling what software can see but about governing what software is authorised to do. The article says the Australian Federal Government parliamentary inquiry into Artificial Intelligence has made clear that acknowledging the risks of autonomous, rogue AI agents after a breach is not sufficient.

The article says organisations must rethink security practices, because autonomous AI agents can be tricked into revealing sensitive information, impersonating legitimate users or taking actions they were never authorised to perform. Traditional cybersecurity tools were not designed to manage these threats, and manual approvals and periodic audits cannot keep pace as adversaries use AI to compress attack timelines from days down to minutes. Modern AI applications are rarely built from scratch and are assembled from models, data and software components developed by numerous third parties, each of which can introduce its own security risks. The article says AI models and the tools they use must be checked before deployment, with their behaviour continuously monitored as systems evolve. It adds that under expert human supervision, advanced AI systems can help cybersecurity teams discover weaknesses, understand how attackers might exploit them and rapidly put protections in place.

The article says government policy must facilitate early, managed access to cutting-edge frontier models for national defenders, security researchers and critical infrastructure operators before those models are broadly deployed. It says Australia's AI Safety Institute has an important role in evaluating emerging risks, and that its role should extend to helping government agencies, security researchers and critical infrastructure operators safely access advanced AI capabilities for defensive purposes. The article draws a parallel with the mandated use of seat belts, which it says saw Australia lead the world in vehicular safety half a century ago, and says the country now has the opportunity to set a global standard for secure AI adoption. It says Australia can achieve the same balance between innovation and safety by building security into AI systems from the outset, adopting continuous technical safeguards, giving defenders timely access to advanced AI capabilities and ensuring those protecting critical systems can respond as quickly as attackers. The article says the recommendations from Parliament's inquiry provide an opportunity to ensure governance frameworks and technical defences keep pace with the technology itself.

Articles.Title: Built-in Protection: How Australia's Public Safety History Can Guide the AI Era - IT Brief Australia

stories.headline_source: Built-in Protection: How Australia's Public Safety History Can Guide the AI Era

stories.Headline: Researchers test AI patient simulations with first-year medical students and find the format feasible
stories.Summary:
Researchers at a United States medical school conducted a pilot study on AI patient simulations. The team tested these encounters with first-year medical students in November 2026. They wanted to see if large language models could be used for clinical training. The study compared two different ways of delivering the simulation. All participants completed the assigned tasks without any total technical failures.

The project involved 19 students recruited from a pool of 72, which was a 26 percent rate. Seven students were placed in a facilitated group, while 12 worked in a self-paced individual format. The group session lasted about 35 minutes, and the individual sessions had a median length of 31 minutes. Researchers used the Behavioral Safety Language Scale-Provisional to measure student perceptions. Most students, or 58 percent, preferred a hybrid model of working alone first and then in a group.

Shelley Tischkau, James Lynch, Sean McGinity, Andrew Primous, Elijah Meldrim, Samantha Lynch, and Richard Selinfreund led the investigation. They noted that the simulation was feasible and received favorable ratings from the students. However, the authors stated that the results are exploratory and do not prove educational effectiveness. They explained that the data must be confirmed with a larger, randomized sample. The team also mentioned that some students experienced intermittent technical problems.

This research fits into a broader effort to use generative AI for case-based and problem-based learning. Current medical education research often lacks specific details on delivery formats and outcome measurements. This pilot study attempted to fill those gaps by testing distinct learning environments. The researchers used Wilcoxon signed-rank exact tests and the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure to analyze the data. Future studies will be needed to determine if these tools actually improve medical training.

Articles.Title: Pilot Tests Show Feasibility of AI Patient Simulations in Medical Training

stories.headline_source: Pilot Tests Show Feasibility of AI Patient Simulations in Medical Training

stories.Headline: Grant County dispatch center uses AI to answer over 152,000 non-emergency calls since May 2024
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence has answered more than 152,000 non-emergency telephone calls for the Grant County emergency dispatch center since May 2024. This technology was used by the Multi Agency Communications Center to change how the agency handles calls from the public. Officials revealed these figures during a budget presentation to Grant County commissioners on November 10. The system handled roughly 84 percent of calls without transferring them to a human employee in Moses Lake, Washington. Approximately 25,000 calls were transferred to human personnel, but trained dispatchers continue to answer all strong emergency calls.

The agency also uses artificial intelligence for employee training, simulated calls, radio transcription, and Spanish language translation. Officials from the Multi Agency Communications Center said that dispatchers often face competing demands while communicating with firefighters and police officers. They stated that the automated attendant reduces these interruptions so employees can focus on assisting first responders. The agency believes these advancements allow dispatchers to spend less time on routine administrative tasks. Some residents remain confused about how the technology is being used by the dispatch center.

The agency has maintained a voluntary caller feedback program for over a year to identify and improve system problems. This program helps the agency understand how the public is affected by the new automated telephone system. The Multi Agency Communications Center operates the emergency call handling and communications infrastructure throughout Grant County around the clock. The agency uses artificial intelligence for facility assurance and radio transcription as part of its current operations.

These tools are intended to support public safety agencies and improve the efficiency of emergency communications. The agency plans to make artificial intelligence a central part of its modernization strategy over the next five years. Future applications could automatically flag officer safety concerns or retrieve information from multiple systems during police incidents. The articles leave open how the agency will resolve the remaining confusion among the local residents.

Articles.Title: AI Has Answered More Than 152,000 Calls for Grant County Dispatch Since 2024

stories.headline_source: AI Has Answered More Than 152,000 Calls for Grant County Dispatch Since 2024

stories.Headline: Apple releases Siri AI developer preview to let apps integrate with the assistant
stories.Summary:
Apple released the Siri AI Developer Preview in the 27.3 beta releases of its operating systems, which lets developers and apps integrate with the assistant and hand off actions to it. During the preview, access to Siri AI is restricted to developer builds and internal TestFlight testers. Apple describes Siri AI as an entirely new version of its assistant that is profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal. The preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, which makes it easier for all apps to tap into the newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, and natural language.

These capabilities let users make natural language requests and have Siri AI carry out any custom action the app supports. The framework also supports complex requests through Skills, a new feature that lets developers teach Siri AI how to combine several actions into a single experience. If a request does not name an app, it is automatically routed to the app currently in the foreground, the app associated with an active Live Activity, or the app previously mentioned in the ongoing conversation. An app running in the background receives only requests that explicitly mention its name, and requests can also include actions across apps, such as finding content in one app, sending it to another, and performing an action there.

Apple says all Apple Intelligence features, including Siri AI, may be subject to usage limits, with extended, premium access planned for the future. Developers based in the EU should be aware that Siri AI is currently unavailable in the EU on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS. One user who tested the preview said that with a good description on the intent and parameters, Siri can figure it out, and called it what Siri should have been all along. Another user said doing it via App Intents was the right move, comparing it to Google's AppFunctions and noting that Google instead made a separate agent skills SDK that developers have to implement.

Articles.Title: Siri AI Developer Preview Lets iOS, iPadOS, and macOS Apps Integrate with Siri - infoq.com

stories.Headline: AI pentesting frameworks scan Cloudflare customers as autonomous attack tools grow past 12,000 repositories
stories.Summary:
Over the last month, many Large Language Model penetration testing and orchestration frameworks have exploded in number. These autonomous tools automate offensive security workflows and have scanned Cloudflare customers globally in the last three days. The number of Internet Protocol addresses running these frameworks has grown into the thousands and increases daily. ARTEX was the only available framework until its creator, Autumn-27, took it down on October 8. Since then, the ecosystem has grown with over 12,000 repositories and hundreds of unique forks.

The Modern Security Model requires six pillars including a Web Application Firewall with rate limits and anomaly detection. Organizations must implement Bot Defense, Identity-Gated Access for high-risk applications, validated schemas, and Threat Intelligence for visibility. Since October 1, daily requests from AI pentesting tools have grown by 30x. ARTEX and its forks now make up over 60 percent of known orchestrators as of November 12. These tools use Model Context Protocol to connect standalone pentesting tools and map environments onto a graph.

Cloudforce One and authors Blake Darché, Myles Sloan, and Jacob Crisp are responsible for these security observations. They stated that the volumetric nature of these autonomously guided attacks makes it hard for defenders to keep up. The authors noted that the removal of the original ARTEX repository likely caused a hydra effect of modifications. They explained that these tools turn compromises into a hill-climbable problem that AI agents are specifically good at. The team recommended that every organization prepare to address this threat by adopting their new security model.

Threat actors are affecting organizations by chaining stolen customer credentials to move laterally throughout an environment. Some attackers compromised static tokens in CI/CD pipelines to pivot from hyperscaler environments into Cloudflare environments. In one case, ARTEX created Worker scripts with names like artex-pgrecon and made 400 database dump requests per hour. This specific attack saw activity exceeding 69 requests per minute across multiple unique parts of the infrastructure. These autonomous frameworks relentlessly test exposed services and configurations, meaning human skills are no longer the limit.

The articles explain that open-source frameworks orchestrate AI agents to carry out the traditional Cyber Kill Chain at scale. These tools can be fully autonomous, performing every step of the OODA loop without needing constant human direction. Top orchestrators like LuaN1aoAgent, Decepticon, Cairn, and PentestGPT-Agent each have over 1,000 GitHub stars. Some of these tools use Kali containers with root access to develop tools and perform cloud pivoting. This shift allows a single operator to target multiple organizations simultaneously, which greatly increases the blast radius.

The authors expect these AI penetration testing frameworks to continue to proliferate across the global internet. Organizations should now implement hardware based FIDO keys and security keys to better protect their internal web applications. The articles leave open how specific organizations will implement the six pillars of the Modern Security Model. It remains unclear how many other unique forks of ARTEX exist beyond the 12,000 repositories mentioned. The text does not state if any legal actions will be taken against the creators of these tools.

Articles.Title: Adapting to AI penetration testing orchestrators: The Modern Security Model

stories.Headline: AI support raises master's students' forward roll scoring accuracy and cuts effort
stories.Summary:
An international research team developed an artificial intelligence model to evaluate children performing the forward roll in a motor skills test. The study results were published in BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation on November 14, 2026. This AI system was designed to replicate expert consensus decisions to support movement instruction and long-term population monitoring. The researchers tested the model using a dataset of 66 forward roll video recordings with scores ranging from 0 to 5. They also conducted a counterbalanced experimental trial involving 20 raters from Poland and Malta.

The AI model achieved Cohen’s kappa values between 0.73 and 0.85 for individual criteria and a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.95 for aggregate performance. Human raters using AI support showed a mean absolute error of 0.68, compared to 0.99 for those working without any assistance. Concordance with a blinded expert consensus rose from 0.60 without support to 0.79 when the AI provided criterion-level recommendations. The AI reduced scoring errors for 19 out of 20 raters, a result confirmed by a Wilcoxon test with a p-value under 0.001. Perceived effort was the only workload metric to show a significant reduction, recording a p-value of 0.045 on the NASA Task Load Index.

The investigators stated that automating criterion-level evaluations could alleviate practical constraints in assessing fundamental motor skills. They noted that low proficiency in these skills among children creates an urgent need for dependable and feasible evaluation techniques. The team aimed to determine if algorithmic feedback could elevate human scoring fidelity and boost inter-rater reliability. They used the Holm correction method to adjust statistical data across various workload dimensions. The researchers concluded that the AI support brought human evaluations into significantly closer alignment with the blinded expert benchmark.

The study affected a cohort of 20 master's degree students who assessed two independent sets of 22 forward roll videos each. These students experienced a reduction in subjective evaluation strain and improved consistency across all four country-by-video-set experimental comparisons. The researchers used the two-way random-effects single-rater intraclass correlation coefficient to track this improved consistency. The findings suggest that AI can effectively reduce the cognitive demand placed on human evaluators during motor skill assessments. The results specifically describe the outcomes for master's students rather than seasoned education professionals.

The research focused on the Fundamental Motor Skills in Sport assessment system to address the need for valid evaluation tools. The team compared AI-produced scores against established expert consensus ratings under standardized video conditions. They implemented a blinded expert consensus panel to measure absolute error and agreement during the experimental trials. The study utilized a counterbalanced design to ensure that each rater performed both assisted and unaided assessment sessions. This background provided the baseline analytical accuracy needed to validate the automated system.

Future validation is required among practicing physical education teachers to extend the use of AI as a decision aid. The authors stated that the system must be tested across broader pediatric age groups and diverse motor skills beyond the forward roll. Further research is needed to determine if the AI remains effective within routine and unconstrained school environments. The articles leave open whether the same accuracy improvements will occur with professional educators instead of students. The generalizability of these conclusions remains limited to the standardized video recording conditions used in the study.

Articles.Title: AI Support Improves Human Forward Roll Scoring Accuracy in Motor Skills Test

stories.headline_source: AI Support Improves Human Forward Roll Scoring Accuracy in Motor Skills Test

stories.Headline: One Point BFG Wealth's Boockvar says investors question whether AI trade has peaked
stories.Summary:
Peter Boockvar, the chief investment officer of One Point BFG Wealth Partners, said on CNBC's Fast Money program that investors are starting to question whether the artificial intelligence trade is reaching peak capital expenditure. The segment featuring Boockvar was published on the CNBC website on November 13, 2026, and the video ran about five and a half minutes. In the appearance, Boockvar talked about the macro trends across the market that he is watching right now. The program presented his comments as part of its Fast Money coverage of investing and markets.

The discussion centers on whether the spending that has driven the AI trade has reached its high point, a question Boockvar said investors have begun to raise. The article gives no figures for that spending, no forecasts and no specific companies or stocks, so the size of any peak cannot be measured from what was published. It also gives no date for when the questioning began or how widely it has spread among investors. The only timing the article provides is the publication date of the segment, November 13, 2026, and its length of five minutes and thirty seconds.

Boockvar is responsible for the view as presented, since the article attributes the peak capex question to him in his role as chief investment officer of One Point BFG Wealth Partners. The article does not quote him directly beyond the framing of the segment, and it does not say what he recommends investors do about the question he raised. It also does not say whether One Point BFG Wealth Partners has changed any positions because of his view. No other person is named in the article as making a similar comment.

The context the article offers is limited to the program itself, which covers macro trends across the market, and to a separate CNBC video noting that the Federal Reserve's financial stability report drew concerns around AI from respondents. The article does not connect the two items beyond their appearance on the same page. It says nothing about what happens next, whether the questioning will continue or whether spending plans will change. More detail would be needed before any conclusion about the AI trade could be drawn from this segment alone.

stories.Headline: Oakland police investigate theft of $11.4 million in Nvidia hardware from a shipment
stories.Summary:
Six pallets of Nvidia computer hardware worth a reported $11.4 million disappeared during a shipment from Oakland, California, to Fort Worth, Texas. A truck collected the merchandise in Oakland on Aug. 29, and investigators reportedly tracked the vehicle through several extended stops before losing its trail in Southern California. The Oakland Police Department confirmed an ongoing grand theft investigation after a complaint was filed on Sept. 13, 2026. According to The Mercury News, the vehicle displayed a food transportation company's logo during the scheduled pickup, and investigators eventually lost track of the truck in San Bernardino County.

The Oakland Police Department said it is investigating a grand theft that occurred in East Oakland and that the victim reported the crime on Sept. 13, 2026. The department said the investigation is ongoing and asked anyone with information to contact its General Crimes Unit at (510) 238-3728. Police have not confirmed the reported $11.4 million valuation or identified the specific merchandise, and authorities have not identified the cargo's owner, shipper, motor carrier or driver. Investigators have not publicly explained the vehicle's extended stops or established whether criminals impersonated a transportation provider, and police have not announced arrests or confirmed any recovery. FreightWaves contacted Nvidia for comment and followed up, but the company has not responded.

The case comes amid reports of nearly $111 million in stolen data center freight involving other high-value technology shipments. A separate $12 million cargo theft investigation involved suspects who allegedly exploited established trucking identities to obtain freight, and authorities have not linked the two investigations. During 2025, Fremont and Union City police investigated burglaries involving more than $7.5 million in Nvidia products, and authorities have not established any connection between those investigations and the latest disappearance. In a separate September incident, thieves stole two PlusAI trailers, including one displaying Nvidia branding, from a Fremont warehouse, but the trailers contained approximately 40,000 pounds of sand rather than Nvidia hardware, and police recovered both trailers in nearby Newark.

Articles.Title: $11.4M in Nvidia hardware vanishes during shipment from CA to TX

stories.Headline: Software engineer Hugo Venturini says humans stay accountable for AI-written code
stories.Summary:
Hugo Venturini spoke to Shane Hastie, Lead Editor for Culture & Methods at InfoQ, about who is accountable when AI writes code, in a podcast published by infoq.com on 13 November 2026. Venturini said AI is a powerful tool but humans remain accountable for the decisions it makes possible and the code it produces. He said he still has wow moments with AI several times a week, not every day. He said that if the tool fails, the person conducting it is accountable and should answer for what goes wrong. He described himself as a software engineer who defended his PhD on the debugging of optimized code in 2008.

Venturini said pull requests have been growing for years and AI did not create the review-scale problem. He cited stories of pull requests of 2000 lines and a senior engineer with a backlog of over 300 pull requests, each hundreds of lines long, waiting for review. He said merging the software engineer and tester roles at Microsoft in 2014 raised quality by making engineers accountable for the whole product. He said AI risks reversing that gain if people blame the tool instead of owning outcomes. He said AI collapses the boundaries of the product manager, architect and tester roles, pushing engineers to ask better questions.

Venturini said asking better questions is a skill that defines seniority and that organisations need to deliberately teach it. He said cultures of transparency, honest no-blame Q&As, anonymous questions and naming solutions rather than people let people dare to take accountability. He said this can start at any level of the organisation, not just the top. He said his team does not review everything and trusts people's judgement about what needs no review. He said he has no good answer on how to review for the number of diffs and is eager for anyone to tell him.

Hastie said studies point to pull request sizes getting bigger and bigger. Venturini said teams should ask whether they should review everything, since boilerplate could already be automated before AI. He said if code compiles, passes the tests you created and behaves as you wanted, you may not need to review it. He said he worked in an organisation where people senior enough and trusted enough merged diffs without review and were accountable for fixing anything that went wrong. He said the heart of the product needs review for quality and for sharing knowledge.

Venturini said some people play a game of wow effect, claiming to have rewritten an entire big product in only one diff, which is just for the show. He said at his group of engineers, anyone doing this was told to help others review their code. He said he was a manager at Meta, Facebook at the time, accountable for the type checker and the compiler of the hack language. He said he was CTO of Qwant, the search engine, with 90 people from network engineers to AI researchers. He now works at a startup that deals with tooling for AI.

Venturini said he has seen software he uses lacking quality over the last month and read in the press that those people are massively using AI. He said he would like to know what feedback he can give to get them back on quality. Hastie said he would leave the review question open for the audience to respond. Hastie asked about the architect with collapsing roles, and the article does not give Venturini's answer. The article gives no further dates, figures or names beyond those above.

Davidson, told Investor's Business Daily that shares were up because the Anthropic roadshow was going well. Davidson, was the only person the article quoted on the rally, and he credited Anthropic's roadshow for lifting shares.

Responsibility for the reported moves was attributed to the market reaction to CoreWeave's results and to feedback from Anthropic's IPO campaign. stories.Headline: NTT Data's supply chain head urges firms to connect isolated AI uses through multiagent systems
stories.Summary:
Pedro Béjar Castán, the managing director and global head of supply chain at NTT DATA, published an article on 13 November 2026 urging companies to stop running isolated AI projects and instead connect the use cases they already have through multiagent systems, in which multiple AI agents work together across a business process to interpret what is happening, coordinate the response and take action. He wrote that most organizations have introduced AI function by function, launched pilots and encouraged employees to experiment, which produces many small use cases that save individual teams time but must be organized and connected for the whole organization to benefit. As an example, he described how NTT DATA ran 14 workshops for a manufacturer's customer service, production, logistics and warehousing departments and spoke with more than 60 people, cataloging 129 improvement opportunities. Following a multiagent approach, the firm grouped those 129 opportunities into just 36 prioritized AI use cases.

The article says AI already improves forecast accuracy, flags changes in demand patterns, surfaces supplier risk earlier and optimizes transportation routes in supply chain management, but each use case enhances only a single activity and a human must still pass the separate pieces of intelligence on. In a multiagent environment, Béjar Castán wrote, a system could read an incoming customer order, check the quantity against expected demand, identify anomalies, evaluate stock-out risk over a two-week horizon, recommend a revised quantity, update the planning system and notify the people who need to know. He noted that multiagent systems are mostly used in software at the moment but will increasingly extend into the physical world through autonomous handling equipment, vision systems and connected assets on plant floors. He also described a project where warehouse staffing volatility and unpredictable truck arrival patterns at the docks looked like two separate problems but were in reality one use case, and looking at them together allowed operator availability to be synchronized with inbound and outbound truck movements.

Béjar Castán is responsible for leading NTT DATA's work with the World Economic Forum's Advanced Manufacturing and Supply Chain initiative, according to the article, and he argued that firms should start with the value chain rather than a list of use cases and look for problems that appear in different forms in different functions. He set out six steps: set the ambition by deciding what the business needs to achieve before thinking about technology, identify improvement opportunities by speaking to employees about their pain points, define the use cases by grouping opportunities and determining which capabilities are worth building, prioritize the use cases using clear criteria, choose the technical architecture by ensuring the data, platforms and integrations are in place, and build a roadmap with a phased approach. He wrote that prioritizing involves weighing the value each use case could create and whether the organization is ready to deliver it, including data availability, process maturity and systems integration.

The article says most discussions and arguments are about prioritizing use cases, and it presents NTT DATA as a partner that combines strategy with implementation, bringing industry and process knowledge together with AI strategy, consulting, engineering and implementation expertise. Béjar Castán wrote that the processes a company connects today could eventually be executed by physical AI, so it makes sense to prepare for that transition. The article ends by inviting organizations to request a half-day workshop to identify where AI will create value and turn a long list of possibilities into a practical plan.

stories.Headline: Nvidia uses aggressive lobbying and invokes Donald Trump to expedite chip export licenses
stories.Summary:
In January, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter told government officials that President Donald Trump and Jensen Huang wanted chip export licenses expedited. Teter claimed he was with the president during these discussions and insisted that the process must move fast. The company used an adversarial attitude to target proponents of export controls and think tankers in Washington. Nvidia lobbyists leveraged their implicit White House backing to influence guidelines with global security and business implications. This aggressive approach occurred while Nvidia became the most valuable company in the world during the AI computing era.

The dispute involved proposed license conditions for exporting H200 chips to China, including requirements to identify cloud customers before shipping. Teter called the cloud-customer requirement a poison pill and pushed for know-your-customer checks only for purchases in the tens of thousands. Nvidia also argued that location verification in the 2025 Chip Security Act was not technically feasible and would create cyber vulnerabilities. However, Reuters reported in December that Nvidia had been privately demonstrating location verification technology for months before its May launch. These efforts were supported by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who sought to avoid trade wars and maintain a relationship with Trump.

Tim Teter and Jensen Huang are described as having a scorched earth attitude toward government officials and critics of the company. Teter accused officials of misrepresenting Trump's policies and insisted that the government staff should support the president's agenda. A spokesperson for the Bureau of Industry and Security stated that working with individual companies on commercial considerations is completely routine. The spokesperson added that Nvidia followed the same process as any other license applicant by consulting with non-political experts. The final versions of all license conditions are reviewed by the energy, defense, state, and commerce departments.

Congressional staffers said they often believed Nvidia's technical claims because they lacked the expertise to fight back on specific restrictions. One former staffer accused the company of gaslighting and creating an intense trust deficit between the government and the company. Bloomberg reported that Nvidia undercounted Megaspeed sales to the government by 50,000 chips, which are worth billions of dollars. The Information reported that companies tied to suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang purchased at least 7.5 billion dollars of chips since 2023. Former officials noted that Megaspeed could have been added to a government blacklist as early as the spring of 2025.

Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia and became a fixture at meetings and dinners with Donald Trump in the Oval Office. Huang recently stepped down from the company following media reports of extramarital affairs with two subordinates and a customer. The customer involved in the affair is suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang previously denied that evidence existed showing chips were being diverted to China. His departure and the surrounding scandals have resulted in a 1.5 trillion dollar loss in Nvidia's market value.

Nvidia declined to comment on the reported lobbying tactics or the location-verification technology used in its chips. The White House did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding the influence of the company on export licenses. The articles leave open whether the government will now take more aggressive action against companies like Megaspeed. It remains unclear how the company will manage its leadership without a known succession plan after Huang's exit. The relationship between Nvidia and government officials is expected to become a defining scandal of the current presidency.

stories.Headline: Nvidia names Colette Kress interim CEO as Jensen Huang steps down
stories.Summary:
Nvidia announced on Thursday, November 13, 2026, that CEO Jensen Huang would step down from his position. This decision followed reports of several affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The company board is now looking for a permanent replacement for the former leader. They have named CFO Colette Kress as the interim CEO to manage operations. Kress held her first executive meeting in Santa Clara on Thursday afternoon.

The board is currently choosing a search firm to help identify a new leader. They stated that they have not formally contacted any potential candidates yet. The company will consider both internal and external applicants for the role. This process follows reports that the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas. Haas previously worked at Nvidia for seven years before joining Arm in 2013.

The board of directors is responsible for the search and issued a statement to CNBC. They claimed that any speculation about specific candidates is premature at this time. The company also hired Wachtell Lipton on Tuesday to investigate foreign intelligence allegations. These probes involve Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, who is suspected of working for China. The board is managing these legal and leadership transitions simultaneously.

The news caused Nvidia shares to drop over 2 percent on Friday. This decline pushed the company's market cap below $4 trillion. Three House committees and the Senate Banking Committee want Huang to testify about national security. They are concerned that AI chips may have ended up in China. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also been asked to testify regarding these issues.

Articles.Title: Nvidia board says it is "in the process of selecting a search firm" for the CEO role and it has "not formally engaged any potential candidates" (CNBC)

stories.Headline: Adaspace Technology lists on Hong Kong Stock Exchange to fund space-based AI computing
stories.Summary:
The Chengdu-based artificial intelligence satellite maker Adaspace Technology Co Ltd began trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on Friday, November 13, 2026. This debut marks a significant step for the commercialization of orbital AI infrastructure and space-based computing. The company offered 30.121 million H shares at HK$24.90 each, which raised gross proceeds of approximately HK$750 million. After costs, the net proceeds totaled about HK$652 million, and the shares closed at HK$24.02 on the first day.

The company plans to use these funds to build a satellite research and testing center and advance in-orbit computing technologies. It will also pursue industrial acquisitions, supplement working capital, repay borrowings, and support its Star-Compute project. This project aims to deploy a constellation of 2,800 AI-enabled satellites by 2035 to provide computing power for millions of silicon-based agents. As of October 28, 2026, the firm had developed six AI payloads, four application satellites, and 26 computing satellites across 15 missions.

Li Chang'an, a professor at the University of International Business and Economics, stated that the listing reflects strong investor interest in China's commercial space economy. He noted that innovative mainland firms are using Hong Kong as a platform to raise funds and expand their international presence. Li further explained that the listing provides the company with the necessary funding to accelerate its space-based AI computing development. He highlighted a shift toward value-added services like orbital data processing rather than simple satellite manufacturing.

The company reported 2025 revenue of about 703 million yuan, which was a 27.0 percent increase over the previous year. By October 2026, Adaspace had secured orders for 114 AI satellites with a total contract value of approximately 3.475 billion yuan. This growth occurs as China integrates computing power into satellite networks to enhance orbital systems. Preliminary estimates suggest that China's space-based computing power industry could exceed 250 billion yuan by 2030.

Articles.Title: ADAspace HKEX debut marks milestone for space-based AI computing - Global Times

stories.headline_source: ADAspace HKEX debut marks milestone for space-based AI computing

stories.Headline: Chinese university student earns 2 million yuan from AI animated series
stories.Summary:
Xiao Tianle, a third-year student majoring in mechanical and electronic engineering at Soochow University, created an AI-powered animated series from his dormitory in Suzhou. This ambitious project drew more than 1.5 billion views and generated up to 2 million yuan in revenue for the young creator. Working with a dedicated team, he managed to produce hundreds of AI-generated animated productions in less than one year. The collective efforts of his team resulted in a total revenue exceeding 3 million yuan during that same period.

The production process requires a human touch because AI scripts are often too flat and lack necessary conflict. Xiao and his team must analyze these scripts and break them down into individual shots to ensure a compelling narrative. They also have to refine the AI-generated footage to correct physical errors and awkward facial expressions before the final release. To manage his growing business, Xiao registered a start-up company in Suzhou during August of this year. He now balances his university classes and project work with frequent online meetings and discussions with potential investors.

Xiao told the Yangtse Evening Post that he developed a fascination with making short films while he was still in high school. He spent his spare time carrying a camera to learn about camera positioning, storytelling techniques, and building emotional resonance. After entering university, he taught himself video editing and completed an apprenticeship at a company specializing in training newcomers. This experience allowed him to progress from adjusting simple prompts to overseeing entire productions for real short drama projects. He expressed his desire to eventually create a feature film with a story that truly stays with the audience.

Following his graduation, Xiao plans to remain in the city of Suzhou to further his professional education. He intends to study the arts of directing and screenwriting to improve the quality of his future cinematic works. His long-term goal involves recruiting new talent to lead a professional team producing television dramas and films using AI technology. By combining technical engineering skills with creative storytelling, he hopes to push the boundaries of modern digital animation.

Articles.Title: Undergraduate generates 2 million yuan with AI-powered animated series - Global Times

stories.Headline: Copper prices hit four-month low as AI investment worries and US rate hike fears weigh on demand
stories.Summary:
Global benchmark copper prices dropped to a nearly four-month low on Friday, November 13, 2026. This decline was driven by expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will increase interest rates. Lower industrial demand from China and the global technology sector also contributed to the slide. Investors also engaged in profit booking following a previous price rally.

The metal was trading at $13,461.99 per tonne, which is about 1.8% lower than the previous day. This shift follows mid-term elections in the United States that resulted in a divided government. Such a political outcome reduced fears regarding tariffs on refined copper imports. However, a fallout involving Nvidia created new worries about future investments in artificial intelligence.

The Federation of Indian Mineral Industries, known as FIMI, attributed the fall to a stronger U.S. dollar and weak industrial demand. FIMI stated that higher interest rates could increase the cost of the dollar-denominated metal. They noted that while short-term prices will be volatile, the long-term outlook is positive. This optimism is based on the growth of electric vehicles, renewable energy, and power infrastructure.

FIMI suggested that India must encourage domestic mining and processing to improve supply security. They argued that reducing import dependence is essential for the country. While lower prices help consumers by cutting costs, FIMI warned that a long decline might hurt exploration investments. The industry body believes that global mine supply constraints will eventually support prices.

stories.Headline: Shanghai Jiao Tong University researchers develop AutoDNA platform to conduct autonomous lab experiments
stories.Summary:
Researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University introduced a new agentic laboratory platform called AutoDNA on November 4, 2026. This advanced artificial intelligence system was presented in the journal Nature to showcase its ability to conduct complex experiments. Unlike standard generative AI, this technology can perform independent physical activities within a biological laboratory setting. The system functions as a set of agents that replace the roles typically held by human researchers.

The AutoDNA platform requires the ability to command physical tools like pipettes to transfer fluids into beakers. It can operate a thermal cycler to heat tubes and measure the degree of fluorescence in a chemical reaction. This system changes the research process by allowing AI to plan, execute, and document a series of experiments. The AI can observe the resulting data and interpret the findings without needing a human to guide every step.

The scientists from Shanghai Jiao Tong University are responsible for developing this autonomous research capability. They demonstrated that the AI can move beyond the computer screen to control physical objects in the real world. The researchers highlighted that the system can decide on a plan and work on its own to complete lab tasks. This shift represents a significant leap from earlier AI models that struggled with basic factual information.

This development marks a transition from chatbots that only provide text to agents that can physically manipulate a laboratory. While humans previously held the guide wire for AI, the AutoDNA system operates with a high level of independence. The integration of agentic AI into science may lead to more efficient and potentially cheaper research methods. The ability of a machine to interpret its own experimental results suggests a new era for biological discovery.

Articles.Title: Now agentic AI can perform complex lab research, and maybe cheaper too

stories.headline_source: Now agentic AI can perform complex lab research, and maybe cheaper too

stories.Headline: South Korean chip firms eye China as US political shifts threaten AI infrastructure demand
stories.Summary:
The Financial Times published a report on Thursday warning that Democratic victories in the US midterm elections could halt the construction boom of data centers. This political shift creates significant uncertainty for South Korean semiconductor firms that rely heavily on the American market for their high bandwidth memory and server DRAM. These specific memory products are primarily used in artificial intelligence servers, meaning any slowdown in US infrastructure development directly threatens the demand underpinning South Korean exports. Consequently, these chipmakers now face a situation where their growth prospects in the United States may stall or decline due to these new political headwinds.

The impact of this shift is evident when looking at the Bank of Korea data from July regarding shipments in 2025. The United States ranked as the fourth largest destination for South Korean semiconductor exports, with shipments totaling 19.02 billion dollars compared to 13.626 billion dollars three years prior. This growth saw the US share of total exports rise from 9.6 percent to 10.3 percent, while the Chinese mainland remained the largest market. China took shipments worth 74.46 billion dollars in 2025, which represented 40.3 percent of the total semiconductor exports from South Korea. These figures highlight why South Korean firms may now prioritize diversifying their markets toward China to sustain their growth.

The Yonhap News Agency reported in September that South Korea intends to double its semiconductor production capacity within the next five years. To maintain their presence in China, South Korean firms must offer their most advanced products, though US restrictions on high bandwidth memory exports make this difficult. This challenge is compounded by the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which has led to fresh calls in Washington for even tighter restrictions on Chinese chip access. South Korean chipmakers must navigate these pressures while competing against Chinese domestic producers who are making rapid technological progress. These domestic firms possess extensive industrial supply chains that could allow them to scale up production quickly once technical hurdles are overcome.

The Global Times suggests that South Korea should assert its own economic interests because semiconductors are vital to the national economy. The publication argues that chipmakers have every reason to press for more room to sell advanced products in the Chinese market. Following US priorities alone risks undermining South Korean industrial interests, especially as Washington attracts investment while simultaneously imposing restrictive trade barriers. The situation remains complex as memory chip prices stay high, indicating strong underlying demand that South Korean suppliers cannot afford to ignore. Future success will likely depend on whether these firms can overcome American restrictions to serve their largest customer in China.

Articles.Title: GT Voice: AI jitters in US raise stakes in China for S.Korea chip firms - Global Times

stories.headline_source: GT Voice: AI jitters in US raise stakes in China for S.Korea chip firms

stories.Headline: Xinxiang First People's Hospital uses AI to screen diabetic patients for retinopathy
stories.Summary:
Since September, the Xinxiang First People's Hospital in Henan province has utilized artificial intelligence to screen diabetic patients for retinopathy. This specific medical complication can gradually destroy a person's eyesight if it is not detected and treated early. The charity-backed pilot program aims to provide free screenings to local residents to prevent permanent vision loss. Organizers hope that this successful model can be copied in other cities across the country.

The program runs until December and is managed by the Chinese Foundation for Lifeline Express alongside other medical institutions in Xinxiang. These efforts were reviewed at a hospital meeting held before World Diabetes Day on November 14, which marks the twentieth anniversary of the United Nations recognizing the day. The International Diabetes Federation's Diabetes Atlas reported that China had approximately 148 million adults with diabetes in 2024. This number continues to rise as the general population ages and daily lifestyles change.

Guo Wei, the secretary-general of the foundation, stated that Lifeline Express began screening for retinopathy in 2014. The foundation is best known for a hospital train that provided free cataract surgery to over 250,000 people since 1997. Guo Wei noted that more than 310,000 diabetic patients have been screened, with about 23 percent having the condition. Nearly 3 percent of those screened were found to have severe cases of the disease.

The foundation cited studies showing that retinopathy affects about 19 percent of patients who have had diabetes for less than five years. This risk increases significantly over time, affecting more than 70 percent of patients who have lived with the disease for over 15 years. One patient, 46-year-old Li Jikun, has managed his diabetes with insulin injections and medication for more than a decade. He experienced the severity of the condition when he woke up one morning unable to see properly.

Articles.Title: Hospital in Henan uses AI to screen diabetics for retinopathy - China Daily

stories.Headline: AI data center power needs drive uranium prices to record highs
stories.Summary:
Uranium prices reached record highs on November 14, 2026, due to a global revival of nuclear energy. This surge was driven by the rapid growth of artificial intelligence data centers and ongoing crises in the Middle East. These factors combined to create a very tight global electricity supply. The increased demand for power has pushed the cost of fuel to unprecedented levels.

The shift toward nuclear power is evident as the number of reactors under construction globally has risen to 79. In Japan, Kansai Electric Power has already restarted seven of its nuclear power reactors to meet energy needs. This movement is part of a broader effort to secure stable fuel sources for the future. The industry is now adapting to the massive power requirements of the AI boom.

Market analysts and energy officials are responsible for monitoring these supply constraints. They suggest that the thirst for data center power is a primary driver of the current price spike. These experts believe that nuclear energy is becoming essential for maintaining grid stability. They note that the transition is necessary to support new technological infrastructure.

The broader context involves a global race for energy security amidst geopolitical tensions. Japan is specifically looking into next-generation fast breeder reactors to keep pace with China and Russia. The country is also exploring nuclear reprocessing technology to salvage rare earth elements. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Uranium price hits record as AI demand prompts nuclear comeback

stories.headline_source: Uranium price hits record as AI demand prompts nuclear comeback

stories.Headline: Japanese firms expect a 20% net profit rise as non-AI businesses lift forecasts
stories.Summary:
Major Japanese companies are expected to see their total net profits rise by 20% during the current fiscal year. This growth would mark the sixth consecutive year that these firms have reached a record high. The increase follows a series of upgraded earnings forecasts for various large corporations. These gains are happening even for businesses that are not part of the artificial intelligence boom.

The financial improvements are driven by better capital efficiency and price hikes. A weak yen has also helped manufacturers increase their profit outlooks. Specific companies like Astellas and Mitsubishi have upgraded their forecasts to record levels. Other firms, such as Komatsu, are seeing higher demand for construction and mining in the Americas.

Kazuki Kawahara reported that these trends are benefiting a wide range of industries. He noted that drugmakers are among the sectors seeing success without relying on AI. The report suggests that corporate Japan is finding growth through diverse operational improvements. These changes allow companies to maintain a strong upward trajectory in their earnings.

The current economic environment is supporting these record-breaking profit projections across the country. Many manufacturers are leveraging global demand and currency fluctuations to boost their bottom lines. The reports indicate a broad recovery and expansion within the Japanese corporate sector. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Growth beyond AI puts corporate Japan on track for 20% profit gain

stories.headline_source: Growth beyond AI puts corporate Japan on track for 20% profit gain

stories.Headline: Ni Yueju proposes a framework for AI cooperation among Northeast Asian economies
stories.Summary:
Ni Yueju, a research fellow at the Institute of World Economics and Politics within the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, discussed artificial intelligence cooperation on October 30. She shared these insights during a symposium that was co-organized by the China Daily Opinion Channel and the International Business School of Beijing Foreign Studies University. The event took place in Beijing to explore how Northeast Asian economies could utilize their complementary strengths for practical gains. This gathering focused on turning theoretical potential into actual regional partnerships through strategic technological alignment. The proposed framework requires a step-by-step approach to building regional trust through specific practical applications.

Ni Yueju suggested that cooperation should begin with smart manufacturing and the implementation of in-vehicle artificial intelligence systems. She further outlined significant opportunities in the fields of green computing, the sharing of public data, and the exchange of professional talent. Additionally, the strategy emphasizes the need for increased supply-chain resilience to ensure the stability of regional technological growth. Ni Yueju is responsible for these recommendations and believes that regional trust must be established gradually.

She argued that focusing on concrete applications first would allow these economies to bridge gaps more effectively. By prioritizing shared interests in manufacturing and data, the nations can create a foundation for broader collaboration. Her perspective emphasizes that practical successes are the most reliable way to foster long-term diplomatic and economic ties. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Tmall integrates AI token services into its e-commerce platform for Singles Day sales
stories.Summary:
A Chinese livestreaming star sold 100,000 monthly membership cards for the AI productivity service QwenWork during a recent Singles' Day shopping event. This sale occurred in just half an hour and offered the subscriptions at a promotional price of 0.01 yuan each. The total allowance for these memberships combined was about 2 trillion tokens, which are basic units for measuring large language model inference. This event marked an unusual moment for the annual shopping festival by bringing AI services into mainstream e-commerce.

Tmall launched a token recharge center on September 3 and brought in providers including DeepSeek, Alibaba Cloud, Zhipu AI, and Kimi. MiniMax opened its first official flagship store on the platform, while QwenWork and StepFun also joined the e-commerce site. Transaction value in the token category soared 450 percent month on month after the sales campaign began on October 20. These changes allow consumers to compare prices in one place rather than paying different providers separately based on usage.

A Tmall representative stated that the main customers are individuals and small businesses, including households and people using AI for research. Fan Yubo from the Shandong Academy of Social Sciences said providers are making services easier to buy by packaging them into subscriptions. He noted that nominal prices encourage first time users, but lasting habits depend on whether AI delivers stable and tangible value. Ding Ding of China Unicom Data Intelligence Co., Ltd. warned that token services cannot follow the low marginal cost model of mobile data.

Zhang Ji, an office worker in Shandong Province, used Qwen for work documents and planning a family trip to Singapore in August. Su Guoqing, a video enthusiast in Xining, Qinghai Province, bought tokens to improve complex scene creation and action storyboarding for his videos. Wang Daoxing, an executive director of a Chongqing AI company, purchased a year of Qwen memberships for software development and presentations. These users and businesses are affected by the shift toward prepaid credits and fixed quota subscriptions on e-commerce platforms.

Tencent Research Institute found in May that only 9.8 percent of surveyed AI users had paid for tools, while over 90 percent used free services. Tokens represent AI generated output involving costs for graphics processing units, electricity, and equipment depreciation, which differs from mobile data economies of scale. Ma Shenglong of China Mobile Qinghai noted that token consumption for the same text can vary by 20 to 50 percent across models. Billing rules currently vary widely among providers, making it difficult for consumers to compare different packages on an equivalent basis.

Wang Jiandong of the State Information Center suggested establishing unified standards for token measurement, improving billing disclosures, and introducing third party verification. Consumers are also requesting that e-commerce platforms strengthen after sales services with clear rules for handling unused quotas and purchase disputes. Industry insiders say that challenges remain in measurement, accounting, pricing mechanisms, security controls, and compliance before these services become mainstream. The articles leave open whether users will renew subscriptions after using their initial promotional packages.

Articles.Title: Economic Watch: Singles' Day delivers AI services into Chinese shopping carts - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Harvard economist Kenneth Rogoff warns an AI bubble burst would hit South Korea especially hard
stories.Summary:
Harvard economist Kenneth Rogoff warned on Thursday that a burst of the AI bubble could hit South Korea especially hard. He spoke at a panel discussion after a lecture on secular stagnation at the Bank of Korea in central Seoul. Rogoff is a Harvard University economics professor and a former chief economist at the International Monetary Fund. He said the bursting of the AI bubble is clearly going to happen at some point and will be very painful, and very painful in Korea.

Rogoff cautioned the Korean government against expanding spending commitments too aggressively during economic upswings. He warned that the AI-driven boom could expose the economy to greater volatility and said Korea starts from a very favorable position, which will make demands very big. He also warned that rapidly expanding AI could push up living costs and resource prices, including land and minerals, saying AI will devour many resources. He acknowledged that Korea has majorly benefited from the AI boom and is in a more favorable position than economies that missed the expansion, describing it as being like a suburb of Silicon Valley.

Rogoff also highlighted growing generational tensions as a major challenge for Korea. He noted that older generations hold a disproportionate share of wealth and housing assets, while younger workers face greater exposure to AI-driven labor market disruption. He said this will involve reshaping how money is spent and how things are done across many societies, and called it the biggest pressure on budgets and fiscal policy. He framed the task as cutting a deal between the elderly, who worked very hard and created a great country, and young people who need to have hope.

On monetary policy, Rogoff welcomed the Bank of Korea's efforts to internationalize the Korean won. He said wider use of the currency in cross-border transactions could reduce costs and strengthen the economy's resilience. He said the won obviously is not going to be a global currency, but Korea can still get a lot of benefits by internationalizing it. He said he gathers the Bank of Korea is moving to do that and called it very smart, saving a lot of costs and protecting Korea to some extent, and said modern technology makes this possible in a way that was not much cheaper before.

Articles.Title: Korea's AI windfall comes with risks: Rogoff

stories.headline_source: Korea's AI windfall comes with risks: Rogoff

stories.Headline: CI Guarantee unveils AI innovation vision at 30th anniversary ceremony
stories.Summary:
CI Guarantee, South Korea's leading construction guarantee provider, marked its 30th anniversary on Thursday with a ceremony at the Westin Josun Seoul. The event brought together about 250 guests, including Kim Sung-hwan, director of the construction industry division at the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, and Nam Young-hee, Incheon's deputy mayor for balanced development. Former chairmen and executives of member companies also attended. At the ceremony, the organization announced plans to speed up AI-driven innovation and expand digital financial services.

CI Guarantee unveiled a new long-term vision called "A Leap Forward in Trust: Building the Next 100 Years through AI Innovation." Under this vision, the organization aims to improve the safety and efficiency of its asset management and to upgrade digital financial services for members. The article says the organization was established in May 1966 with government approval and 3,221 member companies. By the end of 2025, membership had grown to 10,054, and total assets reached 1.55 trillion won, or about 1.16 billion dollars. It began with guarantees for construction-related transactions and later expanded into lending and mutual aid, offering eight mutual aid products.

Choi Un-gu, acting chairman of CI Guarantee, said the organization's 30-year history was one of partnership built on the trust and solidarity of its members through difficult times. He said it would build on that trust and embrace AI and digital innovation to become a more accessible and reliable financial partner for members. He added that this would help shape the next 100 years of the mechanical construction industry. The article also says the organization has recently lowered guarantee and mutual aid fees and expanded digital services, including self-serve guarantees and Kakao-based guarantee services, to cut costs and improve accessibility for members.

Articles.Title: CI Guarantee marks 30th anniversary with AI-driven innovation push

stories.headline_source: CI Guarantee marks 30th anniversary with AI-driven innovation push

stories.Headline: Korail blocks AI agent Pickle while United restricts AI bots access
stories.Summary:
Korail recently blocked access across automated programs overall, including macros and AI agents such as Pickle, according to reporting compiled on the 12th. On that day, functions to connect to Korail via Pickle to make bookings or perform operations were not operational. Korail implemented the blocking measures against the AI agent Pickle, which plans the tasks it needs on its own and carries them out. The blocking is seen as a measure to prevent confusion that could arise if AI agents book train tickets such as KTX. Earlier, in September, Amazon in the United States blocked Meta's AI agent Muse from accessing its shopping mall and making purchases by proxy when it was released.

United Airlines said on Wednesday it would restrict AI bots' access to its digital platforms, citing data security. United warned that sharing account credentials with third-party AI assistants could expose sensitive information and lead to unintended purchases, account modifications or the unauthorized use of frequent-flyer miles. United also said automated AI tools performing actions like flight check-in, which requires human acknowledgment for prohibited items such as explosives, could create regulatory risks. The carrier said it would take steps to restrict access both directly through its digital platforms and indirectly through travel agencies and aggregators. Those steps include updates to its booking, ticketing and distribution policies.

Korail explained that it is advancing its macro-blocking solution to provide a fair and stable ticket reservation environment. Korail also said it is strengthening its security policies regarding the access and use of automated programs. Scott Kirby, chief executive officer of United Airlines, said AI is a powerful tool for solving operational challenges and complex problems, but that the airline will take a cautious approach to agent commerce. Kirby added, to be frank, that they do not want to create yet another middleman. Naver is considering allowing AI agent access for parties partnered with Naver.

Naver plans to launch an AI agent within the year and is expected to clarify its policy toward external AI agents accordingly. Currently, Pickle can access Naver by using a user ID and password to log into websites through its own browser. At present, KakaoTalk is not connected on Pickle. Kakao plans to check from the perspective of user protection whether there are any issues under related policies and laws and to respond. Many companies are reviewing whether to allow or block access by external AI agents.

Pickle is an AI agent that orders goods on behalf of users, contacts others, and handles ticketing and reservations, gaining popularity mainly on social media. Concerns have also grown about the harms that the indiscriminate activity of AI agents could bring. The concern is that AI agents can act at will without human approval. In addition to security and safety considerations, there is a strategic aspect of operating services by leveraging their own ecosystems as much as possible rather than bringing in external AI. Companies across industries are taking divergent approaches to the rapid rise of AI agents capable of carrying out tasks on behalf of users, with some restricting access to protect their platforms and others embracing partnerships.

Amazon has blocked Meta's AI agent Muse, while Walmart has partnered with it. Meanwhile, online travel firms such as Expedia and Booking are working with ChatGPT-parent OpenAI. On this day, United Airlines in the United States also announced it would prevent AI agents from accessing its website and app to book airline tickets. The articles do not say how Pickle or other AI agents will respond to the blocking by Korail and United. The articles also leave open what policy Naver will ultimately set for external AI agents.

stories.Headline: South Korean court sentences man to seven years for using AI to forge documents and defraud victims
stories.Summary:
A South Korean man was sentenced to seven years in prison on Thursday for fraud and forgery. He used artificial intelligence to create fake documents to deceive victims and a judge. These crimes took place between July 2025 and January of this year. The man posed as a businessman and a doctor to carry out his schemes.

The defendant swindled two victims out of 377 million won, which is about 283,000 dollars. He used AI to forge a medical license certificate and cryptocurrency trade records. He also faked a prosecution notice and bank statements. One forged certificate claimed he had over 900 million won, though the account only held 23 won.

The Busan District Court’s Eastern Branch handed down the sentence. The judge stated that the man's indiscriminate forgery of public and private documents was extremely dangerous. The court noted that the victims were not compensated and had not forgiven him. Because of these factors, the judge gave a longer sentence than the six years requested by prosecutors.

The man initially avoided jail when he used the fake balance certificate to convince a judge to reject an arrest warrant. He claimed through his lawyer that he could use those funds to pay back his victims. Prosecutors later discovered the document was a fraud and secured a second warrant. The man was then taken into custody for his crimes.

Articles.Title: Man who used AI to fake 900 million won balance and fool judge gets 7 years

stories.headline_source: Man who used AI to fake 900 million won balance and fool judge gets 7 years

stories.Headline: Chinese manufacturer Qingdao Ruilijie Metal uses AI to program precision mold machines and cut costs
stories.Summary:
Qingdao Ruilijie Metal Co., Ltd. implemented an artificial intelligence programming system in July 2026 to write instructions for precision mold machines. This technology helps the factory produce parts like washing machine front panels while reducing costly waste caused by design deviations. The transition required an 80-person team to spend one full year collecting and standardizing technical drawings to create a usable dataset. After engineers added an automatic verification function to fix early sizing errors, the system began expanding to other moldmakers.

The new system shortened development cycles for new orders by approximately one week and saved the company over 3 million yuan, or about 447,000 U.S. dollars, annually. This project is part of a broader AI Plus initiative launched by the government in 2024 to develop tools for mining, ports, and logistics. Official figures from October indicate that over one-third of larger manufacturing enterprises have adopted AI in key application scenarios. Developers now aim to bring these tools to 100 small and medium-sized firms by the end of the year.

Factory director Guo Weiwei stated that the AI system reduced defects and significantly lowered annual costs for the company. Yu Tao from the State Grid Tai'an power supply company noted that AI drone inspections of electricity lines around Mount Tai are six times more efficient. Miao Yanliang, the chief economist at China International Capital Corporation, suggested that China's comprehensive industrial base and vast market provide a competitive edge. These leaders believe that directing AI toward wider practical applications will continue to drive industrial efficiency.

China is applying these technologies across various sectors, including healthcare systems at West China Hospital of Sichuan University and lung cancer research in Guangzhou. A September study by the International Labour Organization found that some Chinese manufacturers saw production efficiency gains between 20 and 30 percent. AI is also being used to analyze digital pathology images and manage patient follow-ups across 43 clinical departments. The government continues to encourage the integration of these tools to refine specific industrial and medical tasks.

Articles.Title: China has a job for AI - Xinhua

stories.Headline: US and Chinese filmmakers meet in Los Angeles to discuss AI integration and co-productions
stories.Summary:
American and Chinese filmmakers, scholars, and industry representatives gathered in Los Angeles during the week of November 11, 2026. These professionals met at the historic TCL Chinese Theatre to participate in the 22nd Annual Chinese American Film Festival and the Chinese American Television Festival. The group focused on exploring new ways to collaborate on animation, film distribution, and short-form mobile dramas. They also discussed the integration of artificial intelligence and the potential for future co-productions.

This cooperation requires a two-way exchange where American companies help Chinese stories reach global audiences while Chinese platforms provide new production capabilities to Hollywood. The scale of this partnership is significant because the United States and China represent the two largest movie markets in the world. Comscore reported that the combined U.S. and Canada market reached 8.87 billion U.S. dollars in 2025 ticket sales. Meanwhile, the China Film Administration recorded 2025 box office sales of 51.83 billion yuan, which is approximately 7.37 billion dollars.

Academy Award winner Richard L. Anderson praised the talent and hard work of Chinese crews, stating there are no technical differences between them and American teams. Producer Arthur Sarkissian noted that the most difficult part of co-production is creating a story that appeals to both Chinese and American viewers. Former studio executive Michael Fisk described artificial intelligence as a useful tool that will lead to a massive explosion of content. Bob Underwood of the Writers Guild of America West emphasized that working with China can enhance the ability of real people to tell stories.

The participants discussed how artificial intelligence can help the industry overcome language barriers and facilitate more efficient collaboration across the Pacific. The appeal of the Chinese market was highlighted by the success of Zootopia 2, which earned over 630 million dollars in China. This specific film accounted for about 35 percent of its total worldwide earnings and received the Most Popular U.S. Film in China Award. The filmmakers believe that mutual cooperation will allow both nations to better navigate the rapid technological changes currently affecting the global film industry.

Articles.Title: American, Chinese filmmakers gather in Los Angeles to explore cooperation in AI era - Xinhua
