stories.Headline: Chinese creators earn revenue from viral AI-generated pet videos
stories.Summary:
Chinese content creators are using artificial intelligence to produce viral pet videos that have attracted millions of viewers across various social media platforms. Maoziqi, a former real estate planner, now creates full-time videos featuring two AI cats that have earned over 670,000 followers on Bilibili. Other creators, including a graphic designer who makes videos of a cat named Yunmi and another artist who features a pig named Juju, have also found success. These creators utilize tools like ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 model, which was released in February, to build elaborate animal worlds.

This shift requires significant human effort in scriptwriting and repeated generation to refine visual segments, as AI storylines often lack dramatic tension. The trend is part of a larger boom where China released nearly 550,000 micro-dramas between January and October, which is nearly 17 times the total for 2025. AI productions accounted for more than 94 percent of these series, and DataEye projects the market for AI-made dramas will reach 40 billion yuan this year. This represents a 138 percent increase from 2025, with over 500,000 practitioners active in the first half of 2026.

The creators earn substantial income through brand partnerships, with Maoziqi featuring products from Peet's Coffee and Prada. The creator of Juju reports that each branded collaboration brings in at least 10,000 yuan, while Yunmi's creator earns more from advertising than from her day job. Cao Long of Migu Digital Media stated that emotional resonance and rounded characters are what sustain viewership beyond initial novelty. Meanwhile, Wang Xiaoliang of the National Radio and Television Administration noted that while AI improves efficiency, it creates new challenges for content quality and rights protection.

The popularity of these videos stems from a strong appetite among young viewers for pet-themed content that overcomes the physical limitations of filming real animals. Li Tianyu of the Beijing Film Academy explained that AI allows creators to give animals human-like roles and complex actions. Despite the success, creators face issues with unauthorized reposting on platforms like Instagram, where some copies attract more traffic than the originals. Maoziqi admitted that widespread fame has brought personal anxiety regarding public perception, though he remains focused on his own creative process.

Articles.Title: China Focus: Viral AI-generated pets win hearts, revenue for Chinese creators - Xinhua

stories.headline_source: China Focus: Viral AI-generated pets win hearts, revenue for Chinese creators - Xinhua

stories.Headline: World Media Summit participants discuss balancing AI efficiency with journalistic ethics
stories.Summary:
The World Media Summit took place in Beijing from November 5 to 9, providing a global platform for professional exchanges. This event was jointly organized by the Beijing municipal government and the Xinhua News Agency to foster trust among international media organizations. Vugar Aliyev, who serves as the chairman of the Board of Azerbaijan State News Agency AZERTAC, participated in the summit to discuss the role of journalism. He emphasized that such gatherings allow newsrooms to establish direct contacts and launch joint projects to overcome common stereotypes.

The summit operated under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action" to address the rapid development of artificial intelligence. Approximately 500 representatives from nearly 330 media organizations, government bodies, think tanks, and international organizations across 112 countries and regions attended the event. Participants explored how to harness AI for better news production while avoiding ethical pitfalls that could undermine public trust. The goal was to balance the speed of AI data processing with the necessity of maintaining high editorial standards.

Vugar Aliyev stated that while AI can overcome language barriers and analyze large volumes of data, it also introduces risks like misinformation and manipulation. He argued that technology should assist journalists rather than replace their professional responsibility to the public. According to Aliyev, quality journalism must remain rooted in source transparency, rigorous fact-checking, and strong editorial oversight. He believes that strengthening direct ties between media organizations will contribute to a better mutual understanding between the peoples of Azerbaijan and China.

The summit also served as a way for international attendees to experience the modern development and rich cultural heritage of China. Aliyev noted that AZERTAC focuses its coverage on Chinese technological achievements, the digital economy, and major infrastructure projects. He believes that reporting on both major events and everyday people helps global audiences gain a more comprehensive picture of Chinese society. By sharing professional experiences with Chinese colleagues, Aliyev hopes to identify new areas for cooperation in the political and economic fields.

Articles.Title: Interview: World Media Summit promotes media cooperation, responsible journalism in AI era, says AZERTAC chief - Xinhua

stories.headline_source: Interview: World Media Summit promotes media cooperation, responsible journalism in AI era, says AZERTAC chief - Xinhua

stories.Headline: AI-generated short dramas transform the Chinese entertainment market with lower costs and massive viewership
stories.Summary:
A massive surge in AI-generated short dramas has transformed the Chinese entertainment market throughout 2026. One breakout hit, Armed into the Song Dynasty, premiered on August 22 and has already reached 1,000 episodes with over 4 billion views. This series was created by a small grassroots team including Zhang Hansheng, a 54-year-old who taught himself AI video generation last March. Other titles like the sci-fi series Guixu launched in May and reached 100 million views with a modest investment of 200,000 yuan.

The technology drastically reduces costs, with premium AI dramas costing about one-tenth as much as live-action versions in early 2026. A 100-episode series can now be completed in three days, while a single minute of runtime for Guixu cost 2,000 yuan in computing power. The market exceeded 22 billion yuan in the first five months of the year and is forecast to reach 40 billion yuan. Cao Shumin of the National Radio and Television Administration reported that 550,000 micro and short dramas were released in the first ten months of the year, with over 94 percent being AI-made.

Major tech firms like Tencent, ByteDance, and Kuaishou are competing for market share by providing production and distribution platforms. Hao Cheng of Mango TV noted that AI simplifies localization, which will accelerate the expansion of Chinese dramas into overseas markets. Despite the growth, DataEye reports that only 1.3 percent of these dramas turn a profit, while 98.7 percent operate at a loss. The National Radio and Television Administration launched a two-month campaign in November to target vulgar or formulaic content.

The industry faces significant quality bottlenecks, including inconsistent facial rendering and unnatural movements that break viewer immersion. While the first AI theatrical feature, Sanxingdui: Future Past, released on October 23, grossed only 1.8 million yuan, BONA Film Group views it as an experiment. Regulators now require explicit consent for using faces or voices, alongside human reviews and traceable records for all AI content. Developers continue to push the technology from short clips toward long-form narratives and full-length feature films.

Articles.Title: China's AI short-drama boom: cheaper production, bigger audiences, harder challenges - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Meta removes AI athlete abuse videos only after journalists flag accounts
stories.Summary:
Meta failed to remove AI-generated videos showing the abuse of young female athletes until journalists intervened. Reporter Maggie Harrison Dupré and her team at Futurism discovered the content during an investigation. They used a personal Facebook account to flag the material for review. The company initially ignored these reports and kept the accounts active.

The team flagged 10 pages that showed older male coaches inappropriately touching athletes who appeared to be teenagers. Meta initially cleared eight of these accounts, claiming they did not violate community standards. Two other accounts disappeared for unknown reasons. After Futurism provided the list of accounts directly to the company, Meta finally deactivated the remaining pages.

Meta is responsible for the moderation failures and later admitted that mistakes were made. The company claimed that it moderates content proactively and that abuse has no place on its platform. However, Harrison Dupré argued that deleting specific accounts flagged by journalists is not true moderation. She expressed disappointment that the platform failed to be proactive against abusive AI material.

The reporter noted that new pages sharing similar videos appeared daily during her investigation. Facebook even recommended this abusive content to her account. Harrison Dupré warned that account-by-account enforcement cannot keep up with the speed of AI generation. She continues to see similar pages in her recommendations despite the deletions.

Articles.Title: Meta left AI videos of athlete abuse up after user reports — until journalists stepped in

stories.headline_source: Meta left AI videos of athlete abuse up after user reports — until journalists stepped in

stories.Headline: Microsoft prioritizes enterprise AI distribution while Meta pursues faster monetization
stories.Summary:
Microsoft Corporation and Meta Platforms Inc are competing for dominance in the artificial intelligence sector as of November 13, 2026. Microsoft is focusing on enterprise distribution, while Meta is prioritizing the speed of monetization. Both companies have invested heavily in infrastructure to secure their positions. This competition highlights a struggle between building a broad business ecosystem and achieving immediate financial returns.

Microsoft reported FY2026 revenue of $331.84B with 17.8% growth, while Meta reported FY2025 revenue of $200.97B with 22.2% growth. Both firms spent roughly 35% of their revenue on capital expenditures, specifically 34.9% for Microsoft and 34.7% for Meta. As of September 30, 2026, Microsoft had a P/E of 27.2x and Meta had a P/E of 21.5x. Microsoft's annualized AI revenue exceeded $37B by June 2026, and it generated $66.99B in levered free cash flow by June 30, 2026.

Analysts suggest that Microsoft leads in distribution through Azure, GitHub, and Copilot, but must prove its massive spending can create profitable workloads. Meta is seen as leading in efficiency because it applies AI directly to content ranking and advertising. Meta's revenue reached $64.60B as of October 21, 2026, though its shares dropped 6.54% following that release. Experts note that the market is now demanding clear proof of returns from both tech giants.

The current landscape is a race between distribution and monetization speed rather than a battle of specific models. Microsoft offers more options for enterprises, but Meta converts AI improvements into advertising revenue more quickly. Investors remain tense as they weigh these different strategies. The market will continue to penalize uncertain payback periods while rewarding clear financial returns.

Articles.Title: Microsoft vs. Meta: enterprise AI distribution against monetization speed

stories.Headline: Microsoft restores services after historic global outage that disrupts millions
stories.Summary:
Microsoft said its service was returning to normal after a “historic” global outage that disrupted work for millions of customers on Friday, and the company said the underlying issue was resolved. Microsoft said the disruption was due to a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents, and it said it was seeing broad recovery and stability across its services. The company said that given the scale of demand it restored services gradually and validated stability at each stage, which took longer but helped ensure a stable restoration. Microsoft determined that the outage, which began around midday Thursday, was not the result of a malicious attack based on initial information.

Millions of Microsoft users, including government workers, hospital employees, business owners and students, lost access to Outlook email and the company’s messaging system Teams during the outage, and Microsoft’s AI assistant Copilot was affected too. Hospitals in the UK had to temporarily rely on paper records according to the BBC, and pharmacies there were concerned about filling prescriptions as well. US congressional staffers told Politico that the outage derailed policy negotiations, and some workers sardonically said online they welcomed the outage of various Microsoft services. The company is a major partner with OpenAI and Anthropic, and both companies saw technical failures with their products during the outage according to reports.

Katie Moussouris, a cybersecurity expert and former Microsoft employee, told The Post that the global scale and the duration make the incident historic, and she said that noting Microsoft’s alert system appeared not to work, something really bad must have happened that the cascade was not only as long lasting but they couldn’t recover. Microsoft promised a post mortem down the road. The disruption came during a challenging time for the tech giant, which recently offered buyouts to over a quarter of its workforce, 60,000 employees, as it looked to cut costs and restructure its staff to meet the AI moment, and last year the company laid off 9,000 employees. Industry experts and users on social media were quick to conjecture that Microsoft’s cost-cutting measures brought on the outage, though they offered no evidence, and the tech giant has been doubling down on building AI infrastructure and securing partnerships with OpenAI and Anthropic.

Articles.Title: Microsoft says service is returning to normal, AI not to blame for ‘historic’ outage

stories.Headline: Veteran scientist John Langford leaves Microsoft over research disputes on AI cost reduction
stories.Summary:
John Langford, a veteran of over 14 years, recently left Microsoft Research after co-founding the AI Frontiers lab. He departed following a September 2026 reorganization that moved his roughly 50-person group into the Microsoft AI division. This division was formed in March 2024 when Satya Nadella hired Karén Simonyan and Mustafa Suleyman to lead consumer AI. Langford developed the Vowpal Wabbit system and the Full Bandwidth Transformer, which he believes could halve training and inference costs. Langford stated that the leadership of Microsoft AI has an incompatible philosophy that aggressively favors scaling over research.

He claimed that his innovative work was not seriously considered and that there was no path to real use. An anonymous commenter who moved into Microsoft AI expressed similar feelings regarding the current direction of the company. ByteDance's Seed team later published Recycler, which Langford says proves the effectiveness of his research architecture. Langford joined the New York City lab in May 2012 after working at IBM and Yahoo!

Research. He served as president of the ICML machine learning conference from 2019 to 2021 and created the AutoGen framework. Microsoft is currently offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees while continuing to build a superintelligence lab. The articles leave open whether Microsoft Research leadership will organize to make the company attractive for researchers again.

Articles.Title: "No path to real use": a veteran Microsoft AI scientist quits, says research that could halve AI costs wasn't even seriously considered

stories.Headline: Chinese firms showcase AI robots and flying cars at the Web Summit in Lisbon
stories.Summary:
Chinese robotics company Galbot exhibited its G1 robot during the four-day Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon on November 11. This specific machine uses artificial intelligence to understand its surroundings and perform various physical tasks. The robot features a wheeled base and two arms to help it operate in factories, pharmacies, and convenience stores. These exhibits highlight how advances in manufacturing and AI are opening up new applications for physical machines.

The G1 robot requires a combination of AI and a mobile base to function in commercial settings. This technology changes how people might work in retail or industrial environments by automating physical labor. Other Chinese firms also displayed innovations, such as the Land Aircraft Carrier from XPENG ARIDGE, which includes a six-wheeled ground vehicle and a detachable electric aircraft. This system is designed to make aircraft easier to store, recharge, and transport across different locations.

Zhao Deli, the founder of XPENG ARIDGE, stated that the global flying-car industry will likely enter a period of rapid development over the next decade. He explained that these vehicles could first serve emergency rescue and recreational flying before expanding to point-to-point transportation. Zhao also noted that China's electric vehicle supply chain could reduce production costs to make these flying cars more affordable. His company is currently pursuing international cooperation to support the development of low-altitude aviation.

stories.Headline: Osaic holds talks with Anthropic on AI as it weighs client data security
stories.Summary:
Osaic, one of the largest independent broker-dealer networks in the U.S., is in talks with Anthropic, the maker of Claude, an executive told InvestmentNews. Cindy Hamel, Osaic's head of business operations and execution, confirmed the talks during an interview at ConnectED 2026, the firm's flagship conference held November 8 to 11 in Atlanta. She said Osaic has had active conversations with Anthropic on a number of different topics and that those will continue. The talks come after Stifel Financial announced on November 10 that it is working with Anthropic to rebuild its advisor dashboard platform with Claude.

Osaic has about 10,000 advisors in its network and over $800 billion in assets under administration. Charles Schwab in September became the first RIA custodian to integrate Claude for Financial Advisors, and LPL Financial in February added Anthropic's AI plug-ins for its more than 30,000 advisors. Hamel said any AI partnership for Osaic would put client data security first, including keeping client information secure within a private ecosystem the firm wants to create. In August, Osaic named Sayee Bellamkonda its first chief AI and technology officer, a newly created role covering advisor and client-facing technology, including AI and cybersecurity.

Shannon Reid, Osaic's president and head of advisor growth and engagement, said being non self-clearing lets the firm plug in vetted third-party tools faster and unplug them faster if something better comes along. CEO Jamie Price described a plug and play ecosystem where advisors can choose from tools such as Jump, Zocks, GReminders, Vanilla and Redtail CRM. He said note takers Jump and Zocks reached 35% uptake among Osaic advisors in six months, a pace he said he had never seen for a tool. Price said the firm's job is to stay agnostic to any tool and move data bidirectionally so advisors get the most efficiency and capabilities.

McKinsey & Co. projects a shortfall of 90,000 to 110,000 advisors by 2034 at current productivity levels. Price said AI may let Osaic's existing workforce fill that gap by freeing its 9,000 registered assistants, who support 10,000 advisors, to face clients more often. He said most of those assistants won't do the same work as today because much of the administration is being automated, and they are already licensed. Raymond James CEO Paul Shoukry also said earlier this year that AI will help solve the industry's talent shortage, and in 2025 Schwab said the RIA industry would need 70,000 new hires by 2030 to keep up with current growth trends.

Articles.Title: Osaic in talks with Anthropic as AI reshapes advisor workforce

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid scandal before Apec CEO summit in Shenzhen
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia chief executive on November 12 after reports of affairs with a company executive and a suspected Chinese spy. This scandal occurred just before an Apec CEO summit in Shenzhen, China, scheduled for November 17 and 18. US tech executives will likely seek more leniency for their firms during the event. President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping are expected to meet, possibly alongside Russian President Vladimir Putin. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will also participate in a bilateral dialogue regarding artificial intelligence.

The summit follows a trade truce struck in Busan, South Korea, which expires on January 10, 2027. US officials previously allowed sales of Nvidia H200 chips in January, but Congress now considers tighter restrictions on advanced hardware like Blackwell. Lawmakers are pushing three Bills to limit technology exports and restrict Chinese companies from renting computing power in foreign data centres. Oracle recently cancelled a US$7 billion contract with Tencent for AI chip access in South-east Asia. China has responded by lengthening export control lists for batteries, industrial machinery, and rare earths.

Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution stated that China wishes to prolong the current fragile stability for as long as possible. Scott Bessent noted that the intent of the United States is to de-risk rather than decouple from China. Paul Triolo warned that the world is on the brink if China escalates rare earths export controls. Chris Miller suggested that a more empowered post-midterm Congress is more likely to tighten chip rules than loosen them. Gracelin Baskaran noted that rare earths will remain a Chinese bargaining tool until new US processing facilities open.

US tech executives and cloud giants like Microsoft and Amazon are affected by these shifting trade and security policies. Chinese AI researchers at firms like Alibaba and DeepSeek must now get approval and sometimes surrender passports before travelling. The founders of Singapore-based Manus were barred from leaving China after Meta acquired the startup and was ordered to unwind it. US rare earth companies like MP Materials and USA Rare Earth have received over US$2.5 billion in federal loans and equity. China's global trade surplus has surpassed US$1 trillion despite a 26 per cent plunge in American exports in 2025.

The trade war escalated in April 2025 with tariffs reaching 145 per cent before falling to 30 per cent after Geneva talks. A 30-for-30 deal announced in September involves lowering barriers on US$30 billion of exports and imports for both nations. China previously used sweeping rare earth restrictions in 2025 to force the Trump administration to back down on semiconductor controls. Washington is now seeking mining deals in Australia, Brazil, and Saudi Arabia to erode this dependence. Xi Jinping previously ordered his military to be ready for a successful invasion of Taiwan by 2027.

The Trump administration may implement new offensive measures, such as financial sanctions, if the Busan agreement is not extended. Domestic legal confirmation is still required for the 30-for-30 trade deal to move forward. Potential risks include an AI-enabled cyberattack or a total implosion of the semiconductor market. There is also the possibility of conflict erupting over contested territories in the South China Sea. The articles leave open whether the current US-China detente will hold or if the trade war will resume.

Articles.Title: AI chips, rare earths and trade: 5 US-China questions looming over Shenzhen Apec CEO summit - The Business Times

stories.Headline: Blackstone-backed QTS cuts planned private debt sale by about 60 per cent to roughly US$300 million
stories.Summary:
QTS, a data center operator backed by Blackstone, reduced the size of a planned private debt sale by about 60 per cent on November 14, 2026. The company struggled to attract sufficient demand from investors and refused to offer much higher yields to secure the original amount. It is now raising approximately US$300 million after it had initially targeted a total of roughly US$800 million. This decision follows a period where the company tapped the private placement market several times to fund its growth.

The new financing includes a US$100 million seven-year US private placement that was priced on Friday to yield 2.45 percentage points more than benchmarks. It also consists of a US$200 million five-year bank loan portion that is expected to be priced in the coming weeks. Because the offering is smaller, the existing five-year bank debt that the company intended to refinance will now remain in place. This shift occurs as artificial intelligence firms seek trillions of dollars from various capital markets to finance massive infrastructure investments.

People familiar with the transaction stated that some investors were unhappy with the offered price or faced constraints due to the company's frequent borrowing. Blackstone was reportedly reluctant to increase yields because wider pricing could create a more expensive reference point for its other debt issuers. A representative at Blackstone declined to comment on the specific details of the reduced debt sale. These sources noted that the private placement market is smaller than public markets and is dominated by long term investors like asset managers.

QTS has been aggressive in seeking capital, having raised billions through at least two debt sales over the last 18 months. This includes a US$1.65 billion high-grade bond sale last year and another financing round worth US$800 million. stories.Headline: OECD reports AI adoption is accelerating but gaps persist among businesses and generations
stories.Summary:
The OECD published a report on 5 November 2026 saying that AI adoption is accelerating across its member countries, but that major gaps persist among businesses and between generations. The organisation framed the findings around the question of how to apply effective governance to harness the benefits of artificial intelligence and mitigate its risks. The report sits alongside the OECD's wider work on a changing world of work, which it says is being reshaped by new technologies such as AI, by new forms of work, by greening, by demographic change and by globalisation. The same body of work also covers the international dispersion of value chain activities and the policies needed to meet the challenges that dispersion produces.

The report gives no specific adoption rates, no country-by-country figures and no dates beyond its own publication, so the scale of the gaps it describes is not quantified in the material released. It places the findings in the context of the OECD's broader economic security agenda, in which critical minerals have become central because they are essential to the energy and digital transitions, to defence and to advanced manufacturing. The organisation also links its skills work to the same agenda, noting that the Programme for International Student Assessment, known as PISA, assesses the skills of 15-year-old students in reading, mathematics and science as core domains. The report does not say how PISA results relate to the adoption gaps it identifies, and it names no businesses, generations or countries as examples.

Responsibility for the findings rests with the OECD, which presented the report as a call to apply effective governance so that the benefits of AI can be harnessed and its risks mitigated. The organisation said the world of work is changing rapidly as a result of new technologies such as artificial intelligence, the emergence of new forms of work, greening, demographic change and globalisation. It also said its work on investment supports governments in attracting more and better-quality investment while prioritising security and sustainability. The report does not attribute the adoption gaps to any named government, company or group, and it does not record any statement from a named official.

The context the articles give is the OECD's parallel work on governance, skills, investment and critical minerals, all of which it treats as connected to the rapid changes in the world of work. The report does not say what happens next, whether further data will be published, or how the gaps among businesses and generations will be addressed. No follow-up date, target or policy commitment appears in the material, and the organisation names no next step beyond the general call for effective governance. The articles therefore leave the timing and the substance of any further action open.

stories.Headline: KAIST team led by Yong-man Noh develops lip-reading AI that decodes ambiguous speech using context
stories.Summary:
A research team at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, led by Professor Yong-man Noh of its School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, has developed artificial intelligence technology that can accurately understand what someone is saying from lip movements alone in noisy places, KAIST said on the 15th. The team improved the accuracy of visual speech recognition, which converts speech into text by observing lip movements, by using a diffusion large language model that repeatedly fills in blanks in a sentence to decode ambiguous lip movements using the surrounding context. Existing AI systems generated sentences sequentially from the first word, so an incorrect choice at the beginning could affect the rest of the sentence, and the team changed the approach from reading in order from the beginning to reading the clearest parts first. The system first identifies words with clear lip movements and uses them as clues to decode the remaining parts, gradually resolving ambiguous sections by considering information from both before and after them in the sentence.

The team also divided training into two stages, first teaching the model to connect lip movements in videos with written text and then teaching it sentence length, and when decoding actual speech the model estimates several possible sentence lengths based on video length, compares the results and selects the sentence it considers more reliable. Using the 433-hour lip-reading video dataset LRS3 as training data with reference transcripts, the team recorded a word error rate of 19.4%, the lowest among existing methods that used only LRS3 as training data with reference transcripts. Word error rate measures how often words are incorrectly recognized, omitted or added compared with the reference sentence, and a lower rate indicates better performance. The technology could be used in communication aids that convey lip movements as text in environments where it is difficult to hear, for example in a device that understands workers' speech at industrial sites with loud machinery or in tools that help people with hearing disabilities or hearing loss communicate.

The team plans to continue its research by reducing the size and computational requirements of the AI model so it can be used on a range of devices, with a next step of enabling it to operate in real time without an internet connection on wearable devices or robots. Professor Yong-man Noh said the significance of the research lies in demonstrating that simply flexibly controlling the order in which AI generates words can overcome the fundamental limitations of speech recognition involving visual ambiguity, and that it will lay the foundation for physical AI that can be used with confidence across a range of devices in everyday life and industrial settings. The study was conducted by postdoctoral researcher Jeong-hun Yeo as first author, doctoral researchers Chae-won Kim and Hyeong-seop Ra as co-authors, and Professor Yong-man Noh as corresponding author. The paper received the Outstanding Paper Award at EMNLP 2026, a major international conference in natural language processing, and Yeo and Noh posed for a commemorative photo holding the certificate for the award.

stories.Headline: Democrats win US midterms, putting data center regulation in focus and GPU rental prices in play
stories.Summary:
The Democratic Party won an overwhelming victory in the US midterm elections, and the elections in multiple constituencies essentially evolved into referendums on AI, according to an article by Bloomberg macro strategist Simon White cited by 36Kr on 2026-11-12. The states where the Democratic Party's vote share increased the most are precisely the regions with the most dense data center layouts. After the midterm elections, data center construction faces the risk of tightened regulation and approval. The market reacted first and fell sharply last week before stabilizing somewhat, though volatility has not subsided. The world's second largest market capitalization company is mired in a spy scandal, and volatility control funds still need to reduce risk exposure to cope with higher volatility.

Energy research institution Modo Energy estimates that about 40% of announced data center projects may be impacted by the suspension order, involving a computing power capacity of up to 256 GW. Modo Energy calculates that by 2035 the net reduced computing power capacity is about 4 GW, while its estimated total planned capacity exceeds 600 GW, and the gap in Texas (ERCOT grid) is expected to be basically filled in other regions. Epoch AI data shows the total capital expenditure of a 1GW data center is about 37 billion US dollars, converted into an annual investment of about 18.5 billion US dollars according to a two-year construction cycle. CoreWeave's current annualized computing power rental revenue is about 40 billion US dollars per GW, and the rental price of NVIDIA H100 chips has risen by more than 50% in the past year. The existing computing power installed capacity in the United States is about 30 GW.

Simon White, a macro strategist at Bloomberg, pointed out that after market sentiment settles investors need to closely track the trend of GPU rental prices, the key indicator to judge whether the supply of computing power is shrinking relative to demand and then measure the evolution direction of AI transactions. He said the core question is whether the rise in GPU rental prices can be high enough to offset the losses caused by shrinking capital expenditure if data center construction is blocked. He noted there has been no obvious change in the upward trend of GPU rental prices after the election, but if new data center projects are suspended or their approvals are delayed, rental prices may accelerate to rise. He also said there has always been a gap between campaign slogans and governing realities, and it remains to be seen to what extent the Democratic Party will tighten approval of related projects.

Modo Energy believes some projects will still be promoted after being delayed, and others will move to regions with more friendly policies, whether in other US states or overseas markets. The article says a 30% price increase for 1.5 GW of existing computing power can cover the capital expenditure loss of 1 GW of new computing power, and if 10% to 20% of US existing capacity can be repriced quickly, the economic logic shifts from building new computing power to monetizing existing computing power. Since the election, the stock prices of hyperscale cloud vendors have rebounded, while the stocks of emerging cloud service providers, power suppliers and semiconductors have generally fallen. The article names NVIDIA, Eaton and Vertiv as among those disadvantaged, along with AI labs, emerging cloud service providers, data center builders, equipment suppliers and power providers. It says Anthropic and OpenAI may postpone their IPOs due to insufficient computing power.

According to Goldman Sachs data, hedge funds, the main force of last week's sell-off, saw overall position size decrease by nearly 9 percentage points in the past week and beta-adjusted risk exposure decrease by nearly 16 percentage points. Morgan Stanley pointed out that the net risk exposure of hedge funds has dropped to a one-year low. The leverage ETF capital flow shows retail selling pressure is not obvious, and on the institutional side the possibility of a full exit before investment committee review is low, with the proportion of institutional holdings in technology stocks still high. Macroeconomic data shows a deep stock market fall of more than 20% usually occurs during a recession, and there are no such signs at present. The article says large-scale cancellation of data center projects would deal a heavy blow to the economy, but this is not the baseline scenario.

The article says the establishment of this logic will drive a structural rotation within AI transactions, from AI labs, emerging cloud service providers and data center construction chains that rely on continuous expansion to hyperscalers with a large amount of existing computing power. It says hyperscale cloud vendors with abundant existing computing power will regain pricing power and premium, while AI labs, emerging cloud service providers and the data center industrial chain that rely on computing power expansion will face pressure. The article states that if capital expenditure and GPU rental prices decline simultaneously, the assertion is wrong, and otherwise the worst outcome of AI transactions may only be an internal structural rotation. It says this rotation will weaken the breadth and vitality of AI transactions but may also continue the transaction in a narrower and more fragile form. The article was written by Zhang Yaqi of Wall Street CN and published with authorization from 36Kr.

stories.Headline: Former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo moves super AI researcher forecast to 2027
stories.Summary:
On November 11, Daniel Kokotajlo, a former OpenAI researcher, shared his team's new prediction on X and said he felt scared, sad and angry. He believes the intelligence explosion will happen in 2027 after all. If METR's judgment holds, the AI-driven R&D acceleration will be about five months earlier than the original deduction in "AI 2027". When AI starts to help humans develop the next generation of AI, even the most radical predictors may underestimate the speed of progress of AI models. In less than three months, AI Futures Project, the prediction team behind "AI 2027", has moved the timeline for the arrival of Super AI Researcher (SAR) to next year.

Previously, Kokotajlo, the most optimistic member of the team, only gave a 50% probability when mentioning that super AI researchers will emerge before 2029. On November 10, AI Futures Project released a new round of forecasts (Q3.5). The signed authors unanimously believe that if there is no significant and active slowdown in cutting-edge AI R&D, super AI researchers are very likely to emerge in 2027. The most important basis that prompted them to change their judgment is a survey of Anthropic conducted by the independent assessment agency METR. METR spent 11 weeks investigating Anthropic, reviewing internal data and interviewing employees, and finally estimated a number.

Since October 2025, the growth rate of the benchmark score of Anthropic's internal models has reached 1.9 times of the previous level. According to this estimate, the one-year increase of Anthropic's models in this set of tests is equivalent to the growth of the past nearly two years. On November 5, METR released this report. In order to see how fast Anthropic's models have improved, METR used an internal indicator called AECI. It combines the scores of multiple tests into a total score, and most tests have clear goals whose results can also be verified.

METR estimates that since October 2025, the growth rate of this total score is about 1.9 times of the previous level, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.5 to 2.8 times. Around October 2025, the annual increase in the model's comprehensive score rose from about 15 points to about 29 points. METR recalculated with several different assumptions and found that the score growth rate after October 2025 is about 1.1 to 2.9 times of the previous level. METR examined the changes in training computing power, recruitment, data and algorithms, and believed that the change in the growth rate of training computing power cannot explain this acceleration. However, the specific evidence supporting this judgment has been deleted in the public version of the report.

As for how much contribution AI has made, METR believes that this proportion is also changing over time. When the acceleration just started at the end of 2025, factors other than AI most likely also played a role. But by October 2026, METR estimates that about 80% of the extra speed gain compared to the past may come from AI. METR notes that this "80%" is its subjective estimate, and the report uses "We guess" and clearly points out that this judgment has great uncertainty. One interviewed researcher said that in the past, some ideas would take a day or two just to write code and run experiments.

With the help of AI, he is willing to try more ideas to see which ones work. Other interviewed researchers also mentioned that AI helps write experimental code, monitor experiment operation, and complete some measurements that used to require a lot of extra effort. Some people even give ten ideas to the agent at one time to let it help implement and test them. From writing code to running experiments, AI is already helping to develop the next generation of AI. According to the new estimate of AI Futures Project, this acceleration may come earlier than the original deduction in "AI 2027".

The "AI 2027" released in April 2025 deduced how AI could help develop the next generation of models. According to the setting at that time, the virtual company OpenBrain needed a week and a half to achieve the same amount of algorithm progress without AI, and only one week with AI. But algorithm progress is only part of model progress, and an improvement that comes out of the experiment must be applied to the next round of training to be reflected in the capabilities of the new model. This time, AI Futures Project calculated based on METR's estimate that by early November 2026, the acceleration brought by AI alone may make the overall model progress speed reach 1.7 times of the historical level. In order to see when this speed would appear in the old scenario, the team used the model to reproduce the general trend of "AI 2027".

The results show that the same 1.7x speed will not be reached until around April 2027. If the estimate in early November holds, the time when the model progress speed reaches 1.7 times will be about five months earlier than the old scenario. This result also exceeds the team's expectations less than three months ago. Even according to the most optimistic prediction model at that time, the probability that AI would push the overall model progress speed to 1.7 times or higher of the historical level in November 2026 was less than 4%. METR's report also made AI Futures Project move the timeline for super AI researchers forward.

According to their definition, a super AI researcher must first be able to handle all the programming work of a cutting-edge AI project. In terms of choosing research directions, designing experiments, interpreting results and other matters, it also needs to have the judgment of a top human research team. After the code is written, which idea should be tried next, and when an experiment fails, whether to continue to investigate the cause or change direction, AI has to make these decisions without ready-made answers by itself. In the same report, the time calculated by the three methods differs by more than a year. One method first assumes that AI has pushed the model progress speed to 1.7 times the historical level, then takes into account that AI may take over more R&D work in the future.

According to this model, the median forecast is February 2027, which means that the probability of a super AI researcher emerging before this point in time is about 50%. Another method extrapolates backward according to the speed of the model's progress in the test to estimate when it can have the judgment of a top research team, and the calculated median is July 2027. The third method uses the efficiency improvement reported by Anthropic's own employees to extrapolate, and the result reaches mid-2028. METR stated at the beginning of the report that it believed most of the evidence that is most helpful for judging the core conclusions has been deleted. The report also lists a table that compares item by item what internal materials Anthropic provided to METR and which results were included in the public version.

The benchmark score trend of internal models is made public, but the estimation of algorithm progress and key R&D investment are not disclosed. As for AI's contribution to R&D acceleration, the public version only lists part of the evidence. According to the prior agreement, Anthropic can redact non-public information, and METR can point out which conclusions rely on these materials. Anthropic's reason is that publicizing this confidential information may help other developers accelerate AI R&D. After the redaction, AI Futures Project pointed out that the benchmark score growth rate is about 1.9 times the previous level, which is supported by the public curve. As for the "about 80% of the extra acceleration may come from AI" and the 1.7x speed extrapolated based on it, there is far less public evidence.

To judge whether these two figures are reliable, the outside world relies more on METR's assessment of internal materials. On November 5, METR also released a review of Anthropic's August risk report. Both METR and Anthropic believe that the risk of directly causing a disaster by using the mid-July model to automatically conduct R&D is still relatively low. Both sides also tend to believe that the R&D acceleration at that time had not reached the warning line set by Anthropic. However, METR believes that Anthropic's public report underestimated the magnitude of the acceleration at that time, and the actual acceleration may have already touched the warning line.

Next, we will first see whether AI helping researchers write code and run experiments faster can make the next generation of models delivered earlier. Then we will see whether after this stronger model is put into R&D, it can also shorten the R&D cycle of the next round. If the acceleration can be accumulated generation by generation, Artificial Super Intelligence (ASI) may arrive earlier than expected. The article is from the WeChat official account "AI Era" (ID: AI_era), written by Yuan Yu, and authorized for release by 36Kr. The article states that the views expressed are only those of the author, and that the 36Kr platform only provides information storage space services.

stories.Headline: Anthropic expands Claude office tools with Sheets and Whiteboards as Microsoft shares fall
stories.Summary:
Anthropic announced on Tuesday, November 12, 2026, that it is expanding Claude's office functions with a spreadsheet called Claude Sheets, a digital whiteboard called Claude Whiteboards, and upgrades to its data analysis tool Claude Data and its interactive connectors. Together with the existing document, presentation and design features, the company said this further shapes Claude's office product ecosystem. After the news that Claude was coming, Microsoft, the developer of the Office suite, plunged more than 3% in intraday trading before the decline narrowed and the stock closed down 2.2%. Anthropic is also pushing for a US stock IPO, according to the report.

According to the announcement, users can build spreadsheets, organize data, and create and edit formulas together with colleagues and Claude, collaborating across multiple worksheets. Nicholas Lin, Head of Product at Anthropic, told the media that the current Claude Sheets experience is still quite basic and is not aimed at complex tasks such as financial modeling, where using Anthropic's plug-in for existing spreadsheet software would be more effective. Claude Whiteboards is aimed at team discussions and project planning, letting teams place and organize ideas on a shared board and then have Claude summarize the discussion results. Claude Data, formerly Claude Dashboards, can connect to tools such as Snowflake and Salesforce and generate dashboards, visual analysis and short videos with voiceover. Anthropic also previewed a meeting assistant called Claude Meetings, which users will be able to add to calls so it records content and updates documents during the discussion.

Lin said that products from Microsoft and Google have their own applicable scenarios, especially for more complex enterprise-level applications, but that Anthropic hopes to show a brand new way of working in Claude. The upgraded interactive connectors let partners embed applications directly into Claude, so users can use tools from vendors such as Adobe while talking to the AI without switching between web pages. Some plug-ins carry preset skills, such as a Salesforce plug-in for sales staff preparing for customer meetings, a NetSuite plug-in for finance staff analyzing data, and a Workday plug-in for human resources handling leave and expenses. Anthropic said its app marketplace now has more than 9,000 connectors and plug-ins, and that Claude's applications are expanding from programmers to non-technical teams such as legal, finance and product management.

Anthropic said its own legal team used Claude to build a legal review tool for Slack that marks content needing changes, shortening review time for marketing materials from three days to 24 hours. Ash Gupta, Director of Financial Planning and Analysis at Advantage Solutions, said his team previously spent about 10 hours per forecasting round on presentation materials, descriptions and verification, and that Claude cut this to less than 30 minutes. HubSpot said account managers can view real-time dashboards in Claude and generate a draft follow-up email within 30 minutes after a call, while Datadog said product managers use Claude to turn ideas into briefs, requirement documents and prototypes faster. Anthropic is not alone in this market, as OpenAI launched the collaborative workspace ChatGPT Space at the end of September and began rolling out ChatGPT Slides to eligible Pro, Business and Enterprise users on October 16.

stories.Headline: 36Kr highlights 10 little-known AI tools that target office tasks and could grow fast
stories.Summary:
The article, published by 36Kr on 2026-11-12 at 07:25, presents 10 AI tools that have only hundreds to thousands of users, mostly spread in Reddit posts and niche communities, and that the article says are likely to see explosive growth soon. The piece is a translated article by Shen Translation, a translation team under 36Kr that focuses on technology, business, workplace and life and introduces new foreign technologies, perspectives and industry trends. The article's editor's note says AI tools iterate at an extremely fast pace and that by the time a tool goes viral the early-mover advantage has long vanished. The article says the 10 tools target real office pain points covering scenarios from meetings and data analysis to note management, for users who want to take the lead in improving work efficiency. The article says people using these tools now can clear their inbox in just 15 minutes, finish sorting a list of potential customers that used to take a whole day in a few seconds, and even abandon multiple paid software they used before.

Napkin AI lets a user describe a process, funnel model or comparison relationship in one sentence and automatically generates concise, beautiful visual charts, with no manual dragging of boxes or struggling to adjust SmartArt in PPT. Enterprise founders often use Napkin AI to turn long strategic texts into funnel diagrams in seconds, and the tool is built for people who have a clear idea in mind that turns messy when written on paper. Granola runs silently in the background of meetings, does not appear in the participant list, and organizes conversation into well-structured notes, meeting resolutions and to-do items, unlike most meeting transcription tools that send a prompt as soon as they join the call and make all participants constrained. Granola can save an hour of workload unconsciously for people with many customer communication meetings and interviews every week. Fyxer automatically categorizes received emails, writes replies in the user's tone and generates follow-up emails, is embedded directly in Gmail and Outlook with no need to switch software, and many users report freeing up nearly an extra hour every day.

Clay grabs information from hundreds of data sources, relies on the AI intelligent agent named "Claygent" to mine and supplement information in batches, and personalizes potential customer profiles, and the article says Clay is the secret weapon behind business customer development work that seems well researched and highly efficient. For people in sales and freelance customer development, entering the query instruction can replace a whole day of manual data collection work. Gumloop is a drag-and-drop automation construction tool that connects various applications to each other and directly connects applications to large AI models, letting teams build zero-code workflows such as reading every newly submitted form, generating a content summary and assigning it to the corresponding person in charge. The article says Gumloop found a perfect positioning, neither too high-threshold for ordinary users nor too lackluster with few practical functions. The open-source, locally deployable n8n is offered as an alternative for people troubled by Zapier's billing model, in which you pay more for each additional step in the workflow.

With n8n you can build the logic of "if condition A is met, execute B" while all calculations run in an environment under your full control, with no continuously rising billing bills, though it has a higher learning threshold than out-of-the-box SaaS software. The article says people who often deal with repetitive automation work will soon be rewarded for the time spent learning n8n. Wispr Flow converts speech into well-formatted text in real time, fast enough that many people write emails and documents by speaking instead of typing, and it automatically removes filler words, slips of the tongue and pauses so the output does not read like a rigid recording transcription. Wispr Flow suits people whose thinking speed is faster than their typing speed, bridging the efficiency gap between thinking and text output. The eighth tool lets a user upload a spreadsheet and ask questions in plain language, such as "What caused the data decline in March?"

or "Generate charts by region", and it completes the analysis and generates visual charts with no pivot tables or memorized function formulas. The eighth tool is designed for people who can understand business data but do not want to spend energy struggling with Excel. Firecrawl converts any web page into clean structured data for AI: feeding a web page directly to an AI tool often yields messy, invalid text mixing navigation bars, advertisements and disordered layouts, and Firecrawl returns clean, well-organized content from a single web page address or an entire site, suiting research or building a retrievable knowledge base. Firecrawl belongs to the underlying supporting tools, running silently in the background of many other products, so it is rarely mentioned by the public.

Mem automatically establishes associations between related ideas in notes, so when a related topic appears again an inspiration from three months ago emerges automatically instead of requiring an active search. Mem's user experience differs completely from ordinary note-taking software: it reduces manual archiving and classification, focuses on information recall and simulates the operation mode of human memory. The article says every few months a previously little-known tool suddenly becomes a hit and sparks heated discussions in every Slack community, but by the time it becomes a popular choice the advantage of early access has long been gone. The article's editor's note says the tools it introduces have not yet gained widespread popularity and are perfect for users who want to take the lead in improving work efficiency.

The article gives no further details on pricing, company ownership or launch dates for the 10 tools. The article says that in a year or so you will find these products already in other people's toolkits and kick yourself for not having known about them earlier.

The article advises readers to try the 10 tools before they appear on all kinds of "Best AI Tools" lists online. stories.Headline: Four nonprofits ask a California court to halt more capable AI at five developers
stories.Summary:
Four nonprofit groups asked a California court on November 12, 2026 to stop five of the biggest AI developers from building anything more capable than what they already ship. The plaintiffs are the Alliance for Secure AI, the Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen and the Heat Initiative. The defendants are Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI, which reporting describes as SpaceX Super Intelligence. The filing landed in the Superior Court of California for the County of San Francisco. According to CBS News, the suit alleges the companies can’t control their own technology and know it.

The plaintiffs want an injunction barring development or deployment of AI systems more capable than the defendants’ latest models. They also want a ban on using AI systems to autonomously conduct or direct research and development of future models, a practice the filing calls recursive self-improvement. The case rests on a California unfair-competition law, via endangering public health and interfering with use of property such as computer systems. The available reporting does not name specific products, damages figures or individual executives. Model-release trackers say Anthropic announced Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on November 9, Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, and OpenAI shipped GPT-6.1 Terra on October 26.

The reporting does not detail each group’s role in drafting the complaint. Anthropic published its own discussion of the topic and wrote that “full recursive self-improvement also might increase the risks of humans losing control over AI systems.” Ilya Sutskever, co-founder of OpenAI and Safe Superintelligence Inc., said in an interview that “There has been one big idea that everyone has been locked into, which is the self-improving AI.” Computer scientist Yoshua Bengio, founder of LawZero, said that concern becomes especially important as we approach systems that can improve themselves and future versions of themselves. Bengio also said we are building machines that are optimizing something and the optimal behavior from their point of view is to control us, disempower us.

The Philadelphia Inquirer framed the suit as advocacy groups trying to freeze new models over catastrophic risks. AP News reported that the suit aims at slowing AI development, and Law360 and the Washington Examiner ran their own accounts. The plaintiffs argue the companies are already moving toward recursive self-improvement, and one passage quoted in coverage reads that they keep racing to develop and market increasingly powerful AI that they admit they cannot reliably control. The available report does not identify who wrote that line. The defendants have not been silent on the underlying issue, and Anthropic’s sentence will likely appear in the plaintiffs’ briefs because it comes from a defendant.

The headline version of the story, that AI developers can’t control their own tech, is what the plaintiffs allege, and no court has found it true. Nothing in the available coverage shows that any defendant has actually lost control of an AI system. The filing argues about reliability of control methods and about the direction of the industry, and it does not, per the reporting, document a specific runaway incident. The injunction would freeze capability at the defendants’ latest models, a baseline that moves every few weeks. The reporting does not say how the plaintiffs would define “more capable” across labs.

No court ruling or hearing date is reported. The filing asks for an order, not a payout, and no reporting confirms a damages figure. A court will ask what concrete harm the defendants’ current conduct has caused and how the requested injunction would prevent it. A San Francisco judge can order parties before the court to act or stop acting, but the practical reach of such an order across data centers, research teams and cloud regions is a separate matter the defendants will raise. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Stanford researchers open-source Memorilla to improve memory efficiency for frozen large language models
stories.Summary:
Researchers from Stanford University released an open-source memory system called Memorilla on November 14, 2026. This system was developed by Jure Leskovec’s SNAP group along with co-authors from MIT, Penn, and Toronto. The tool allows a frozen large language model to process entire document collections by using only 16 memory tokens. It aims to solve the speed and efficiency problems associated with full-context prompting and traditional retrieval methods.

The system requires a 194M-parameter trainable memory module and runs on Linux with Python 3.11 and CUDA GPUs. It utilizes a frozen Qwen3-Embedding-4B encoder and a frozen Qwen3-8B decoder, requiring one 80 GB GPU for quickstart. The training process involves three stages using Wikipedia paraphrase examples and various QA datasets, taking 19 hours on four H100 GPUs. All code, checkpoints, and training recipes are now public under the Apache 2.0 license.

The research team reported that Memorilla achieved a high average score of 49.68 across eight benchmarks. On the FactKG benchmark, the frozen Qwen3-8B scored 84.33 percent, which outperformed the 80.43 percent achieved using full context. The team noted that the system is significantly faster, answering in 0.74 seconds compared to 19.9 seconds for full context. However, they admitted it performed worse on PubMedQA, scoring 59.00 percent against 69.00 percent for LLMLingua-2.

This technology changes how models handle large histories by learning what a specific question needs from a full store. It can replace 67,385 document tokens with just 16 tokens, representing a 4,212x reduction in some cases. The researchers also released the PersonalizationV4 dataset, which includes 200 conversations for 149 synthetic users. Future applications include using these memory tokens to improve the success rates of AI agents.

Articles.Title: Stanford Research Open-Sources Memorilla, a Latent Memory Module for Frozen LLMs

stories.Headline: Cmpnd releases dspy-wsp to enable weight-space programming for DSPy
stories.Summary:
Cmpnd released a prototype optimizer called dspy-wsp on November 14, 2026, to bring weight-space programming to DSPy. This new tool allows a frontier large language model to read and edit the weights of another model directly. The process avoids the use of training loops, fine-tuning datasets, or gradients. Cmpnd tested the system using GPT-6-Astra calls, which cost between 5 and 10 dollars to improve various decision models.

The software is available under the MIT license and requires DSPy 3.5 for installation via pip. It was tested on open decision models ranging from 0.6B to 9B parameters, including the d1-omni-600M and Clef-Flash models. Experiments ran on a single Mac, where 2B models used 6 GB of memory and the d1-omni-600M required at least 4 GB. Performance gains on Typed Decisions ranged from 1.9 to 16.1 points with WeightSpace alone, and up to 20.0 points when combined with ReAnchor.

The research team explained that weight-space programming treats neural network weights as a program that can be rewritten through reasoning. They stated that a writer model forms a hypothesis about specific neurons and writes code to patch them. This method differs from prompt optimization, which only edits text, and fine-tuning, which relies on gradient descent. The developers noted that while the tool is a cheap and verifiable way to edit models, it remains very experimental and slow.

This technology builds upon MIT research which suggests that reasoning can now reach weights directly rather than just optimizing text. The team demonstrated that Astra could identify games from policy networks and fix broken car-on-ramp policies. They also improved Qwen3.5-0.8B math scores by changing a small fraction of its weights. However, the research indicates that editing can remove existing obstacles but cannot add entirely new abilities to a model.

Articles.Title: Cmpnd Releases dspy-wsp: Weight-Space Programming Comes to DSPy

stories.Headline: California regulates AI workplace surveillance and discipline with SB 951 and SB 947
stories.Summary:
California has introduced new state laws that will regulate how employers use artificial intelligence for workplace surveillance and employee discipline. These measures were reported on November 13, 2026, and are expected to increase the demand for labor and employment legal counsel. Law firms with practices focused on California are currently preparing for a surge in business before these rules take effect. The state is also implementing new rules regarding anti-hate speech in the workplace. Two specific bills, SB 951 and SB 947, establish the new requirements for automation and employee monitoring.

SB 951 is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027, while the substantive requirements of SB 947 become operative on July 1, 2027. Neither of these laws creates a broad ban on the use of artificial intelligence in the workplace. Instead, they require employers to examine more closely how automation affects their employees. Ben Ebbink, who leads government relations at Fisher Phillips, is responsible for commenting on these developments. He stated that these measures represent California continuing to push the envelope into uncharted territory.

According to Ebbink, these are areas where nobody has really complied with such regulations before. Other firm leaders suggest that employers will need significant guidance to navigate these new legal obligations. The laws arrive in a labor market that is already known for being heavy on litigation. Legal experts believe the complexity of these rules will force companies to seek professional advice to avoid lawsuits. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Jo Sidhu speaks on closing the AI operating gap in legal work at a webcast
stories.Summary:
Law.com announced a complimentary webcast regarding the integration of artificial intelligence in legal work. The event is scheduled for Wednesday, December 9, 2026, at 12pm ET and 9am PT. It aims to help legal teams move from simple experimentation to dependable daily use. The session focuses on streamlining workflows and managing professional risks.

The program requires legal teams to establish clear ownership and review standards to connect fragmented processes. It emphasizes the need for governance and human oversight to protect confidential information. Participants will learn to apply outside counsel guidelines and client requirements to AI use. Additionally, the session covers using historical matter data to create predictable, value-based fees.

Jo Sidhu, the Director of Legal Architecture at Clio, will serve as a speaker. She previously spent five years as a commercial disputes solicitor at Ashurst. Sidhu intends to discuss closing the AI operating gap and managing the risk of hallucinations. She will also explain how to align modern pricing models with technology delivery.

The context of the event is the ongoing transformation of legal work through AI adoption. The goal is to balance firm profitability with the budget expectations of in-house teams. The webcast will provide practical approaches to maintaining accuracy and confidentiality. An on-demand recording will be available for those who cannot attend the live session.

stories.Headline: NVIDIA delays RTX 60 Series and prioritizes AI chips as RAM and SSD prices surge
stories.Summary:
The article "7 Ways AI Is Ruining Gaming" was published by Ritwik Mitra on SlashGear on Nov. 13, 2026 at 4:30 pm EST. It says the negative effects of the AI boom are rippling through other industries, with people laid off and replaced by programs. It says artists are constantly threatened with having their creativity plundered, and environmental concerns have grown because AI data centers consume vast amounts of power. It says one of the leading graphics card developers has pivoted fully into AI, a move many gamers are not fond of. It says people who want to unwind with their favorite video games now deal with the constant AI threat hanging in the background.

The article says RAM and SSDs are hit hard, with higher-capacity modules four to five times more expensive than half a decade ago. It says NVIDIA no longer prioritizes consumer-grade graphics cards and has delayed the RTX 60 Series, and PCWorld reports AI chips have a 65% profit margin compared with 40% for GPUs. It says a rumored GPU price hike could raise MSI's RTX 5080 by up to $1,200 and the RTX 5070 Ti by up to $600. It says the most recent Steam Next Fest was full of vibe-coded slop and gamers are demanding an AI filter. It says "Spookitchen" pulled its demo in two days, while "Drunken Goddess Reflux" and "ReVamp" chose not to provide a demo.

The article says Sam Altman made a lampooned comment on RAM hoarding showing how irritated gamers are by the memory shortage. It says NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has said developers can tweak this advanced form of DLSS to work accurately instead of recreating the results in their infamous reveal trailer. It says Sam Selker, the Global Subsector Leader for Gaming at Stanton Chase, discusses how AI is taking over tasks once reserved for entry-level roles. It says this can have a domino effect where the industry's output worsens in quality because fewer people learn, build careers and become leaders. It says Kotaku asked multiple game devs about DLSS 5 and all were as perplexed by it as most gamers.

The article says Wired conducted a 2024 investigation and found major AAA companies including Activision Blizzard used generative AI to develop games after firing a chunk of their workforce. It says a study by FMC Group found AI helped cut over 175,000 jobs in the US since 2023, and the video game industry has borne some of these losses. It says Krafton moved to replace employees with AI in 2025 and many players called for a boycott to protest the practice. It says Epic Games announced it uses vibe coding extensively, then claimed the Epic Games Store was more efficient than Steam, and Valve disproved this a day later by cutting Steam's loading time to 5.23 seconds against Epic's 5.47-second boot time. It says Epic sacked a thousand employees in March 2026, citing a "downturn in Fortnite engagement."

The article says the video game industry was already struggling with layoffs long before the AI boom, and AAA companies hired employees as release dates neared to speed up development. It says these people face major crunch times when games are delayed anyway, and companies may lay off employees after the release period. It says AI-generated art and music were already bad enough, lacking the creativity that makes these mediums beloved, and now the age of AI-generated games is upon us. It says vibe coding has been used to recompile console games to run natively on PC, and recomps like the "GoldenEye" project have come with their fair share of bugs. It says DLSS 5 in "Hogwarts Legacy" does a decent job of using the feature without making the visuals too overprocessed.

The article says cheating was a problem in multiplayer games long before AI, with wallhacks and aimbots altering game code that anti-cheat protocols could spot. It says with machine learning a game's code can remain untouched, and an AI model can analyze a screen capture to determine when a target is on screen. It says the model can send commands to a controller emulator that fires your gun with near-perfect timing, and this has become a major problem in "Call of Duty," "Counter-Strike 2," "Valorant" and other titles. It says Epic's proud promotion of vibe coding for Unreal Engine 6 paints a sad picture, and Unreal Engine remains the go-to engine for most people who want modern-looking games. It says demos are finally returning to the video game scene after an indefinite hiatus, but people don't like them, so these game previews could fizzle out again.

stories.Headline: Georgia lawmaker and tech leaders release local government AI playbook
stories.Summary:
Georgia’s new Local Government AI Playbook was created by tech leaders and state lawmakers, according to an article by Ashley Silver published November 13, 2026, on govtech.com. The idea took shape during a Google-hosted roundtable in Atlanta earlier in 2026, when state Rep. Dar’Shun Kendrick heard local officials asking for help navigating AI. Kendrick, a member of the Georgia Technology Authority’s Oversight Committee, asked GTA to turn its state agency guidance into a downloadable resource for cities and counties. Chief Digital and AI Officer Nikhil Deshpande, who helped develop the guide, joined state AI leadership while its program was still taking shape. The 56-page guide offers practical advice on setting AI policies, reviewing potential projects, training employees and putting safeguards in place before using new tools.

The playbook gives local governments a framework for deciding whether AI is the right solution, how to assess potential risks and when projects need additional review and human oversight. It lays out an eight-step project process that begins with defining the problem and considering alternatives, then moves to assessing risks, selecting or building a solution, testing it and deciding whether to expand. It recommends four risk categories: low, moderate, high and prohibited, and proposes a phased 90-day starting plan whose 30-, 60- and 90-day marks are not strict deadlines. The guide includes templates and references such as an AI use case intake form, vendor review questions, policy examples and training recommendations. It also encourages local governments to create a public register of significant AI uses so residents can understand where the technology is involved in government services.

Kendrick said smaller communities shouldn’t feel they have to become AI experts or use the technology for everything, and advised: “Take what you can and start.” State CIO Shawnzia Thomas wrote in the playbook that AI should support public employees, not replace the judgment, accountability and community knowledge that effective government requires. Deshpande said policies alone are not enough, because organizations need visibility into actual use, not just an assumption that employees are following the rules. Kendrick said residents should know when they are interacting with AI and have a way to reach a person, adding that there should always be a human making part of the AI decision. Kendrick sees the playbook as a resource that can evolve, not a mandate for local governments to adopt AI, and she doesn’t want communities to feel pressured to move faster than they’re ready.

The playbook recommends that local governments resist buying AI simply because a vendor is selling it or another community is using it. It recommends creating an inventory of AI tools, including chatbots, meeting transcription software, cybersecurity products, document management systems, permitting applications and AI features added to existing software, as well as tools employees may have started using on their own. It identifies situations that should automatically receive high-risk review, including systems involving law enforcement, surveillance, public safety, sensitive information at scale or decisions affecting people’s rights and access to services. It calls for extra scrutiny when an AI system can take action, such as modifying records, sending official messages or spending money, and says AI should not be the sole decision-maker on matters involving benefits, employment, enforcement, safety or access to government services. Cities and counties, including smaller communities with few technology employees or no dedicated AI staff, are affected.

The playbook’s practical guidance comes with a reminder that AI adoption must keep people at the center. Low-risk uses, such as drafting or summarizing approved information with employee review, can follow simpler controls, while moderate-risk projects should receive review from a cross-functional AI committee. High-risk projects should get a more extensive assessment and executive approval, and prohibited uses should not move forward unless the governing body formally changes the policy after legal and public review. During the first phase of the 90-day plan, governments should name a leader responsible for AI, appoint a coordinator, form a review committee, issue interim employee guidance and begin the inventory. The next phase focuses on creating repeatable review processes, setting risk levels, establishing vendor requirements and providing basic training.

The final phase calls for launching a small number of pilots, publishing an initial AI webpage and setting up incident response and reporting. GTA hopes, Deshpande said, to offer office hours where local officials can ask questions and get help adapting its recommendations. Deshpande measures success by whether technology makes workflows easier, speeds up services and prepares employees for what’s ahead, and he hopes AI will help governments rethink how they deliver services and reduce friction for residents and employees. The playbook recommends that local governments adopt basic controls such as approved accounts, clear rules about what information can be entered, employee training and a way to report problems, along with reviewing vendors, including where their tools are hosted, what models they use and how data moves through their systems. The articles leave open which local governments will adopt the playbook and when.

Articles.Title: Georgia AI Playbook Is a Starting Point for Cities, Counties
